Statement of Work 
 
National Institutes of Health (NIH) 
National Cancer Institute (NCI) 
Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology (CBIIT) 
Biomedical Information Technology, Software Development, and Informatics 
Support (BITSDIS 2) 
 
1 
 
 
2.1. PURPOSE 
 
The purpose of this Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) vehicle is to acquire 
professional biomedical informatics, data science, information technology, software 
development, and artificial intelligence support services in support of the National Institutes of 
Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute (NCI) to assist in achieving NIH’s mission. NCI’s 
Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology (CBIIT) is the sponsor of this 
requirement; however task orders may be issued on behalf of any NCI Division, Office, or 
Center (DOC) in addition to any NIH Institute or Center (IC). 
 
2.2. BACKGROUND 
 
The NIH’s mission is to seek fundamental knowledge about the nature and behavior of living 
systems and to apply that knowledge to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce illness and 
disability. The NCI is one of the 27 institutes that make up the NIH, the nation’s primary 
federal agency for biomedical and public health research. that conducts and supports research, 
training, and health information dissemination with respect to the cause, prevention, diagnosis, 
and treatment of cancer, rehabilitation from cancer, and the continuing care of cancer patients 
and the families of cancer patients.  
 
CBIIT is an important NCI component entrusted to lead and coordinate efforts in the fields of 
informatics, data science, and information technology. CBIIT is defining, designing, 
developing, and deploying key infrastructure, standards, and application-level components of 
the Information Technology (IT) fabric to support a modern vision for integrated cancer and 
biomedical research, translational and population science, and personalized medicine. CBIIT 
establishes and develops the framework, infrastructure, standards, processes, and tools for data 
collection and management to ensure the long-term value of NCI’s investment in research 
through data accessibility, interoperability, sharing and reuse. CBIIT creates mechanisms to 
build and support information networks enabling all constituencies in the cancer community – 
NCI programs, other institutions, researchers, physicians, and patients – to facilitate new 
discovery, integrate data, implement knowledge, make research results available for the 
community, minimize the burden of cancer, and improve the lives of patients. 
 
Major ongoing NCI initiatives and programs supported under this vehicle include, but are not 
limited to, the Cancer Research Data Commons (CRDC), a comprehensive Clinical Reporting 
and Research Informatics (CRRI) initiative that include elements of the Cancer Moonshot and 
Precision Medicine Initiative (PMI). CRRI will include Precision Medicine Activities (PMA), 
Correlative Study Management (CSMS), the Clinical Trials Reporting Program (CTRP) and 
CTRP’s Clinical Trials Reporting Office (CTRO), as well as Computational Genomics and 

 
 
2 
 
Bioinformatics research and ancillary support services. Specifics include: 
 
• A Precision Medicine Analysis and Coordination Center (PMACC) that will support 
current and next generation NCI precision medicine trials. This center will provide 
support for existing trials, new treatment studies for the existing trials as well as new 
major initiatives; each of which will be composed of an umbrella/basket screening 
platform and linked clinical trials. Each master protocol will require both a 
MATCHBox precision medicine trial platform to determine patient eligibility for 
specific therapies and associated precision diagnostic laboratories provided by the 
NCI/DCTD Molecular and Immunologic Diagnostics Network of Laboratories 
(MDNet). The PMACC will provide the treatment assignment decisions based on data 
obtained from MDNet, other qualified laboratories, and the trial groups. The MDNet 
will provide primary diagnostic screening for trial arms that require specialized 
laboratory testing for patient allocation,  
 
• CIDC (Cancer Immunologic Data Center) and CIMAC (Cancer Immune Monitoring 
and Analysis Centers) are both components of a collaborative effort aimed at advancing 
cancer immunotherapy research. CIDC is the data management and analysis platform 
that works alongside CIMAC. It collects, organizes, and stores the data generated by the 
CIMAC centers and other cancer immunotherapy trials. It also facilitates data sharing 
among researchers, ensuring that data is accessible for analysis and fostering 
collaboration. Supports the use of advanced computational tools and analytics to 
identify patterns in immune responses and potential biomarkers for treatment success. 
The Correlative Study Management System (CSMS) supports the NCI Cancer Immune 
Monitoring and Analysis Centers (CIMAC) Biomarker Network and works along the 
CIDC to support tracking specimen from enrolling sites. CBIIT has migrated the CIDC 
to the NCI Cloud and both CIDC and CSMS should be maintained and enhanced to 
support study management dashboards, unique sample identifier generation, manifest 
and sample label generation, biospecimen tracking, document management and 
information management capabilities. 
 
• The Clinical Trial Reporting Program (CTRP) fulfills a recommendation made by the 
NCI Clinical Trials Working Group (CTWG) to the National Cancer Advisory Board. 
CTRP is designed to be a comprehensive database of regularly updated information, 
including accrual, on all NCI supported clinical trials. This comprehensive database of 
the entire NCI portfolio will help identify gaps in clinical research and duplicative 
studies, as well as facilitate effective clinical trial prioritization, trial search and trial 
matching. The CTRP engineering works on system enhancements, software updates, 
and technical improvements to ensure that researchers and institutions can submit trial 
data efficiently, while ensuring compliance with regulatory standards. Additionally, the 
CTRP engineering team plays a key role in developing interfaces that allow for 
interoperability with other NCI systems and external databases, helping to streamline 
data sharing and foster collaboration.  
 
• The CTRP PMO (Program Project Management Office) is responsible for overseeing 
and managing the CTRP at the NCI. Its primary function is to ensure that all NCI-

 
 
3 
 
supported clinical trials are properly registered, updated, and tracked throughout their 
lifecycle. The PMO ensures the standardization and accuracy of clinical trial data, 
which is critical for research, regulatory compliance, and patient safety. It also provides 
support to researchers and institutions, helping them meet reporting requirements and 
ensuring the smooth submission of data. Additionally, the CTRP PMO manages the 
overall operations of the program, ensuring the system remains functional and up to date 
while enabling efficient data sharing and collaboration among the research community. 
Through these efforts, the CTRP PMO plays a key role in improving the transparency 
and efficiency of cancer clinical trials. 
 
• The Clinical Trial Reporting Office (CTRO) provides task management, data 
abstraction, coding, characterization quality assurance, user support and reporting in 
support of NCI’s Clinical Trials Reporting Program (CTRP). The CTRO manages 
CTRP content, including abstraction of submitted clinical trial protocols, updating and 
maintaining the content of the CTRP database, ensuring the accuracy of content through 
quality assurance procedures, managing the NCI’s ClinicalTrials.gov account, and 
responding to queries from stakeholder in a timely and accurate manner.  
  
• The semantic infrastructure (SI) of the NCI relies on well-defined vocabularies, 
terminologies, and data models to ensure that information from clinical trials, research 
studies, and healthcare systems can be easily shared and understood by different 
stakeholders. At the core of this infrastructure is the NCI Thesaurus, a large, curated 
vocabulary that provides consistent definitions for cancer-related terms, drugs, diseases, 
and treatments. Additionally, the NCI Metathesaurus integrates multiple biomedical 
terminologies to facilitate data interoperability across systems. This semantic foundation 
allows researchers, clinicians, and data scientists to collaborate more effectively by 
ensuring that data is represented consistently, enabling meaningful comparisons and 
analyses across studies. NCI’s SI also supports key initiatives like the Cancer Data 
Standards Repository (caDSR), which provides common data elements (CDEs) and 
models to further standardize data collection and sharing, ultimately accelerating cancer 
research and improving patient outcomes. 
 
• The Real-World Data (RWD) program at the NCI focuses on leveraging data generated 
from real-world settings, such as electronic health records (EHRs), cancer registries, 
claims data, and other healthcare sources, to enhance cancer research and improve 
patient outcomes. This program aims to complement traditional clinical trial data by 
providing insights from larger, more diverse patient populations and real-world clinical 
practices. By integrating and analyzing RWD, the NCI can better inform clinical 
decision-making, accelerate the development of new therapies, and improve the 
understanding of cancer progression in various healthcare settings. The program also 
supports data-sharing efforts and fosters collaboration between researchers, clinicians, 
and healthcare institutions to maximize the impact of real-world evidence in advancing 
cancer research and care. 
 
The National Cancer Institute's Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) serves as the 
central authority for enterprise-wide IT governance, strategic planning, and service delivery 

 
 
4 
 
across all NCI operations. Operating under federal IT management requirements including 
Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Federal Information 
Security Modernization Act (FISMA), and National Institute of Standards and Technology 
(NIST) guidelines, the OCIO oversees comprehensive IT infrastructure management, 
cybersecurity operations, technology standardization initiatives, and project management 
following established federal frameworks including Project Management Institute (PMI) 
standards and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidelines for IT capital planning. 
 
The OCIO's core responsibilities include enterprise architecture planning aligned with the 
Federal Enterprise Architecture Framework; establishment and management of IT engineering 
standards consistent with NIH and HHS policies; implementation of IT security controls 
including continuous monitoring, risk assessment, and incident response; and management of 
IT support services encompassing help desk operations, asset management, and user 
provisioning across NCI's research and administrative environments. 
 
OCIO delivers enterprise IT services that enable seamless user experiences across 
geographically distributed locations, maintain secure and high-performance computing 
environments supporting both administrative functions and computationally intensive research 
workloads, optimize service delivery through cost-effective solutions, and promote enterprise 
standardization while supporting specialized research requirements. This approach ensures IT 
services support NCI's cancer research mission while maintaining federal compliance with 
security, privacy, and operational requirements. 
 
All contract awardees are required to utilize NIH-approved IT services and designated 
providers and collaborate effectively with the OCIO and its authorized representatives to 
execute technology-related efforts in full alignment with established enterprise requirements, 
standards, and operational expectations. 
 
2.3. OBJECTIVE 
 
NIH’s mission is to seek fundamental knowledge about the nature and behavior of living 
systems and the application of that knowledge to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce 
illness and disability.  
 
To support, enable, and advance this mission, the goals of this IDIQ are the following: 
 
1. Provide the NIH with access to high-quality contractor services that deliver results-oriented 
solutions to enhance biomedical informatics programs across the enterprise, including support 
to the NCI. 
2. Strengthen the OCIO’s ability to effectively manage, analyze, process, and share biomedical 
data in accordance with NIH/HHS policies, applicable federal regulations and scientific best 
practices.  
To achieve these goals, the IDIQ will enable the provision of highly qualified contractor 
support with subject matter expertise in biomedical information technology systems, 
application and database design, development, implementation, and maintenance; data science; 
biomedical informatics; clinical and health data sharing policy implementation; and specialized 

 
 
5 
 
biomedical IT and informatics. 
 
2.4. SCOPE 
 
The Contractor shall provide several general categories of consulting, planning, process 
improvement, management, systems and software development, information technology 
operations, subject matter expertise, and terminology analysis, development, maintenance, 
publishing, and support services to accomplish the NIH mission.  
 
These services shall include but not be limited to overall project and technical management, 
consulting, and technical support to the NIH/NCI, including participating in efforts 
supporting other NIH/NCI Divisions, Offices, and Centers in biomedical informatics, 
biomedical information technology, and cancer research projects in all stages of their life 
cycle in accordance with the tasks specified below. These services require interaction with 
multiple NIH/NCI DOC’s, Government Program Manager (s), senior business and IT 
managers, program stakeholders, and other NIH contractors.  
 
The scope of services to be provided shall fall under one or a combination of the 
following task areas:  
  
1. Contract Management  
2. Program and Project Management Support 
3. Enterprise Architecture Services 
4. Definition and Design Services 
5. Development Services 
6. Validation, Testing, and Quality Assurance 
7. Implementation Management and Support 
8. Semantics Support Services  
9. Clinical Trials Reporting Office (CTRO) Support Services  
10. Technical and Policy Consulting  
11. Website Development and Maintenance, Content Management and Update 
12. Data Science Services  
13. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Services  
14. Other IT Services 
15. Transition Out Planning and Support  
 
The Contractor shall report directly to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR)

 STATEMENT OF WORK 
SECTION C – DESCRIPTION/SPECIFICATION/WORK STATEMENT 
 
C.1 BACKGROUND 
 
The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Dahlgren Division (NSWCDD) Electromagnetic and Sensor Systems 
Department (B) provides products and services for efforts related to Sensor Systems in support of the US Navy, 
US Marine Corp and the Missile Defense Agency. B Department provides Systems expertise across the entire 
acquisition lifecycle from concept exploration through sustainment of Navy and Marine Corps Systems. 
Contractor support is required for Operations support services such as configuration management, systems 
administration, program and financial analysis, information technology, technical writing, facilities operations, 
property management, procurement, and test support. 
 
C.2 SCOPE 
 
B Department has a requirement for technical and support services in the general Work Areas of: Information 
Technology, Program Financial Management, Technical Writing/Editing, Operations Support, Configuration 
Management, Program Analysis, Facilities Operations, Property Management, Procurement Support and 
electronics Technician Support. These services shall be provided in support of existing, near-term, and out-year 
projects, programs, technology developments, technology insertions, prototyping and technology 
demonstrations, fielding and sustainment, and related acquisition efforts. The Contractor shall provide technical 
support services at NSWCDD, test facilities, Contractor facilities, and in the field. 
 
C.2.1 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
 
The following documents are applicable to this SOW.  The most current versions of these documents are 
accessible through the internet or will be provided to the Contractor upon request. 
 
Other Department of Defense Specifications/Standards/Other Applicable Documents may become applicable 
throughout the life of the Task Order and may be added to the Task Order via modification.

C.3 REQUIREMENTS 
 
The following paragraphs describe each of the support elements required in detail. During the performance of 
this Task Order, the Contractor shall respond to urgent requirements within 60 minutes of notification of the 
urgent requirement. 
 
C.3.1 PROGRAM BUDGET PLAN DEVELOPMENT AND MONITORING 
 
C.3.1.1  The Contractor shall perform program and financial analysis required to accomplish the technical 
objectives of Sensor System projects. 
 
C.3.1.2  The Contractor shall assist in the maintenance of budgetary, financial, and scheduling status of the 
various Tasks and Task areas within Sensor System projects. 
 
C.3.1.3  The Contractor shall provide financial and programmatic assistance for the development of budget 
planning estimates for Task Planning Sheets, cost estimates for Rough Order of Magnitude (ROMs), and impact 
statements due to reduced allocations. 
 
C.3.1.4  The Contractor shall track expenditures and expenditure rates, identify variances, and provide cost 
projections. 
 
C.3.1.5  The Contractor shall develop financial summaries, reports, and graphs for project reviews, 
presentations, and data calls to project Sponsors, project Leads, and the Department (CDRL A009, A00A, 
A00B). 

Page 3 of 30 
 
C.3.1.6 The Contractor shall use the applicable DoD and NSWCDD Systems and Databases to report on, 
analyze, budget, forecast, track, and solve problems for the Government's financial accounts. (A00A) 
 
C.3.1.7 The Contractor shall provide financial analysis support to the organizations' divisions, branches, 
program managers, group leaders, and Business Office in accordance with applicable Department processing 
timelines. The Contractor shall provide financial management and cost analysis of projects within the 
organization. The Contractor shall process incoming and outgoing funding for NSWCDD in accordance with 
applicable Department processing timelines. The Contractor shall recommend the allocation of financial 
resources. The Contractor shall provide funds status inputs to the Government. (A00A) 
 
C.3.1.8 The Contractor shall generate, update, and maintain program, project, and budget estimates, tracking 
budget execution by appropriation and funding type, addressing budget issues, and providing data for budget 
data calls in accordance with applicable Department processing timelines. (A00A) 
 
C.3.1.9  The Contractor shall use the Integrated Budget, Planning & Execution (IBPES) application to report on, 
analyze, budget, forecast, track, and solve problems for the Government’s financial accounts. (A00A) 
 
 
C.3.2 LABORATORY CONTROL 
 
C.3.2.1  The Contractor shall perform all aspects of laboratory control and maintenance of designated Sensor 
System laboratories. 
 
C.3.2.2  The Contractor shall follow all maintenance standards and procedures for all lab equipment. 
 
C.3.2.3 The Contractor shall analyze repair practices and develop procedural instructions for use by others on 
methods and steps to repair equipment (CDRL A009, A00C). 
 
C.3.2.4  The Contractor shall design and analyze circuits, determining design feasibility, evaluate equipment 
performance under varying environmental conditions, and collect performance data to achieve performance and 
cost objectives. 
 
C.3.2.5  The Contractor shall enforce Government access and use policies and procedures for designated 
laboratories. 
 
C.3.2.6  The Contractor shall run reports on up-to-date inventory of the equipment and instrumentation housed 
in the laboratory via an online database and assist individuals in locating equipment and parts upon request. 
 
C.3.2.7  The Contractor shall perform periodic inventories no less than annually of classified materials. 
 
C.3.2.8  The Contractor shall attend Laboratory meetings. The Contractor shall provide agendas, minutes, action 
items and their responses, and status of assigned items (CDRL A003, A009, A00A). 
 
C.3.2.9  The Contractor shall assist with establishing and maintaining standard operating procedures for 
laboratory operations and instruct users of the laboratory on these procedures (CDRL A00C). 
 
C.3.2.10 The Contractor shall maintain standards and procedures for use by others. 
 
 
C.3.3 INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) 

Page 4 of 30 
 
C.3.3.1 The Contractor shall develop, maintain, and enhance network systems supporting the Electromagnetic 
and Sensor Systems Department. Examples include workstations, servers, and printers. 
 
C.3.3.2 The Contractor shall perform requirements analysis for existing/proposed network systems supporting 
the Electromagnetic and Sensor Systems Department to determine feasibility. 
 
C.3.3.3 The Contractor shall prepare security access rules and system constraints for systems supporting the 
Electromagnetic and Sensor Systems Department. 
 
C.3.3.4
 The Contractor shall assist the Government to compile application specifications and recommendations 
for selected activities such as data management, configuration management, program management, and security 
(CDRL A009). 
 
C.3.3.5 The Contractor shall install software applications.  
 
C.3.3.6 The Contractor shall support Assessment & Authorization (A&A) activities by performing vulnerability 
scans and Security Technical Implementation Guidance (STIG) assessments and submitting those results and 
associated reports to the appropriate online repositories.  
 
C.3.3.7  The Contractor shall comply with hardware and software system standards and procedures. 
 
C.3.3.8
  The Contractor shall develop, document, and test computer programs and system configurations to 
optimize the analysis of network data (CDRL A009, A00D, A00E). 
 
C.3.3.9
  The Contractor shall create build disk(s) that can be delivered to the fleet in order to update system 
software (CDRL A009). 
 
C.3.3.10 The Contractor shall ensure the appropriate operational security posture is maintained for all 
information systems. 
 
C.3.3.11 The Contractor shall participate in Electromagnetic and Sensor Systems Department’s Configuration 
Control Board (CCB) processes. 
 
C.3.3.12 The Contractor shall actively maintain a cloud-based storage array. Maintenance shall include 
configuring permissions, working with corporate on new storage needs for programs, and identifying future 
needs. 
 
C.3.3.13 The Contractor shall operate and maintain cloud-based services to include Virtual Machines in 
Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, or hybrid environments. 
 
C.3.3.14 The Contractor shall respond to Incident and Request tickets from the command’s OneStop portal and 
resolve issues within the associated Service Level Agreement (SLA) period for each.  
 
 
C.3.4 TECHNICAL EDITING 
 
C.3.4.1 The Contractor shall provide technical editing and associated word and graphics processing using 
Microsoft (MS) Office tools and MS Access database, MS Publisher, MS Project and Dynamic Object-Oriented 
Requirements System (DOORS) in the preparation of technical presentations, technical reports, technical notes, 
miscellaneous publications, and other document types (CDRL A009, A00A, A00C). 

Page 5 of 30 
 
C.3.4.2  The Contractor shall compile project status reports from individual team inputs (CDRL A00B). 
 
C.3.4.3  The Contractor shall collaborate with project engineers to generate specifications, abstracts, technical 
reports, whitepapers, and technical briefing materials in NSWCDD, Sponsor, Conference, or DoD required 
formats (CDRL A009, A00A). 
 
C.3.4.4
  The Contractor shall provide formal documentation of project meeting minutes and project decisions 
(CDRL A003). 
 
C.3.4.5
  The Contractor shall develop promotional materials and flyers for projects and the Division (CDRL 
A00A). 
 
C.3.4.6
  The Contractor shall provide conference planning to include attending meetings, preparing agendas, 
providing minutes, and tracking the status of action items (CDRL A003). 
 
C.3.5 OPERATION SUPPORT 
 
C.3.5.1  The Contractor shall coordinate shipboard installations of radar equipment. 
 
C.3.5.2  The Contractor shall support activities requiring adherence to the Navy Modernization Process to 
include meeting major milestones required for successful Regional Maintenance and Modernization 
Coordination Office (RMMCO) check-in and check outs to support the installation, modification and removal 
of equipment that is installed aboard Navy Vessels and land Based Test Sites. 
 
C.3.5.3
  The Contractor shall coordinate with various RMMCO Offices located throughout the Navy including 
but not limited to Bahrain, Guam, Mid-Atlantic, Mid Pacific, Northeast, Northwest, Sasebo, Southeast, 
Southwest, and Yokosuka. 
 
C.3.5.4  The Contractor shall maintain and update program calendars and schedules. Examples include planned 
test events, reviews, technical meetings, and computer program deliveries. 
 
C.3.5.5
  The Contractor shall coordinate the movement of materials to including preparation of documents to 
facilitate the shipment and receipt of materials and media to support system installs and removals at NSWCDD 
laboratories and test sites, at external test sites, and at field activities and operational units. 
 
C.3.5.6  The Contractor shall assist in the preparation of documentation required to support the purchase of 
materials and equipment. 
 
C.3.5.7  The Contractor shall maintain a space-by-space map of each test site, laboratory, and software factory 
laboratory clearly indicating the infrastructure and working capacity for each assigned to B Department. 
 
C.3.5.8  The Contractor shall plan and coordinate laboratory and test site renovations to include furniture build-
outs and project transitions. 
 
C.3.5.9  The Contractor shall coordinate the installation or move of phone lines. 
 
C.3.5.10 The Contractor shall schedule IT services, riggers, security, and furniture designer/installers for site 
renovations. 
 
C.3.5.11 The Contractor shall track the progress of each renovation.

C.3.5.12 The Contractor shall coordinate and submit requests for necessary laboratory and test site maintenance 
for all spaces assigned to B Department (CDRL A009). 
 
C.3.5.13 The Contractor shall assist in the monitoring and reporting on the condition of B40 test site and 
laboratory spaces and the safety thereof (CDRL A009).

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
(Includes associated Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) 
 
 
 
PWS 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT  
 
US Army Aviation Center of Excellence (USAACE), Fort Rucker, Alabama 
Aviation Future Capability Directorate (A-FCD) support for Modernization Activities  
19 February 2026 
 
 
Part 1 
General Information 
 
 
1.  General: This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering 
the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its 
administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the 
Government and its employees. The non-personal services contract provides professional 
support services for T2COM subordinate units located at United States Army Aviation Center 
of Excellence (USAACE), Fort Rucker, Alabama. This effort enables T2COM subordinate units 
in the conduct of their specific Doctrine, Organization, Training, Materiel, Leader Development, 
Personnel, Facilities and Policy (DOTmLPF-P) integration and synchronization efforts 
addressed in respective directives from Headquarters Army Transformation and Training 
Command (T2COM), Commanding General Aviation Center of Excellence (ACOE) 
Commanding General Futures and Concepts Center (FCC), and Headquarters Department of 
the Army (HQDA) for the enduring force modernization efforts and supporting the fielding of 
emerging capabilities from the T2COM. 
 
1.1  Description of Services/Introduction: This is a non-personal service(s) contract to 
provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, materials, supervision, and other 
items and non-personal services necessary to perform support services for the A-FCD and  
assigned T2COM Units located at Fort Rucker, Alabama. The Contractor shall provide 
analytical support to Aviation A-FCD Directors, Training and Lessons Learned Managers 
(TLLM) these recommendations on decisions may drive materiel development and future Army 
policy. Those recommendations, on whether to procure a particular item that may be 
commercially available or pursue developing an item that will provide a future capability for the 
Army, drives budgeting and procurement decisions. These same analysts are often required to 
assess and comment on how a particular capability will impact U.S. Army DOTMLPF-P. Each 
of these subjects reflect current Army policies and the Contractors are expected to comment 
on how a proposed capability will impact those same policies. When Contractors make 
assessments and offer recommendations, following the conduct of an experiment, that 
information delivered to the Government may be used to develop policy to deliver the Army of 
2030, and design the Army of 2040. The primary skill that is being procured is critical thinking 

Page 2 of 53 
  AUG 22 
and specialized knowledge with military-specific capabilities. This contract-support is not 
intended as general administrative functions, though the Contractor may be expected to 
perform both administrative and analytical functions. The services being procured are functions 
equivalent to those performed by former-Government employees, whose skills and experience, 
military education level, and specialized knowledge uniquely qualify them to perform capability 
development functions.The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this task order. The 
Government retains approval and acceptance authority for any analysis, feasibility studies, and 
strategies developed under this contract as well as decision authority for course of action 
selection, approval, and implementation. In addition, the Government is responsible for 
approving all work products the Contractor provides in connection with this PWS. The work 
products become Government property when approved. The Contractor shall provide the 
necessary subject matter expertise, have the ability to perform the tasks required for the 
integration and synchronization of the DOTmLPF-P domains for Army UAS, Army Aviation 
Manned Reconnaissance/Attack aircraft, Army Aviation Manned Utility/Cargo rotary/vertical lift 
aircraft, Aviation weapons and munitions, and Army Aviation portfolio subsystem Training Aids, 
Devices, Simulators, and Simulations (TADSS), Systems Integration and Management 
Support and Army Aviation Survivability Equipment (ASE) utilizing the Department of Defense 
(DoD) Joint Capability Integration and Development System (JCIDS) requirements 
development processes and documentation, Army Regulation 71 – 9 Warfighting Capabilities 
Determination Dated 29 June 2021, T2COM Regulation (TR) 71-20, dated 28 June 2013, and 
TR 71-12 dated 3 October 2012 and applicable emerging T2COM regulations. 
 
1.2  Background: This effort includes development of operational methodologies that support 
the Warfighter Functions and capture the capabilities/requirements into requirements 
documentation (materiel and non-materiel) as well as materiel development work statements 
to reduce acquisition time, costs and technical risks. The Contractor shall have the operational 
and Army Aviation system subject matter expertise for manned Reconnaissance/Attack 
aircraft, Army Aviation manned Utility/Cargo rotary/vertical lift aircraft UAS, Army aviation 
weapons and munitions, and subsystems, Army Aviation manned Reconnaissance and Attack, 
Utility, Cargo, and Fixed Wing Aircraft, and associated TADSS which they shall use to provide 
input and recommendations to the supported Directors of TLLM, A-FCD, and CEAD. During 
the base year, the Government will require Contract Man-year Equivalent (CME) for Army 
UAS, Army Aviation manned Reconnaissance/Attack, Army Aviation manned Utility / Cargo 
Aviation Platforms, Army Aviation Weapons and munitions, Launched Effects, and associated 
Aviation portfolio TADSS, DOTmLPF-P Integrator and Aviation Survivability Equipment. 
Historically, this level of effort has required seventeen (17) CMEs. Contractors shall possess 
broad understanding of all Army aviation systems to enable A-FCD and TLLM to meet mission 
requirements as necessary.  
 
1.3  Scope: The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s).
 The services provided for in 
this contract focus on Aviation capability development and analytic areas to include Army 
unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), Army Aviation manned Reconnaissance and Attack aircraft, 
Army Aviation manned Utility and Cargo rotary/vertical lift aircraft, Future Aviation Tactical 
Ecosystem (FATE), Launched Effects, and Army Aviation weapons and munitions 
requirements development. This includes associated Army Aviation Aircraft and subsystem 
TADSS. Includes support for DOTmLPF-P efforts with Headquarters Department of the Army, 

Page 3 of 53 
  AUG 22 
T2COM, T2COM Commands, and other Army Branch Centers of Excellence FCDs. Services 
include enduring Aviation portfolio modernization strategies and fielding of current and future 
aviation systems. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the 
Contractors performing the services herein. While the Contractor shall make recommendations 
on results of analysis and collaboration, a Government official will make all final decisions.  
 
1.4  Objectives: The Contractor shall conduct analysis of Aviation organizations in support of 
formation-based assessments, simulation activities, and annual capabilities needs 
assessments. The Contractor shall tailor methodology and conduct analysis to best examine 
Aviation tasks, conditions, standards, and gaps across select Aviation formations. The 
Contractor shall write/support the revision or re-writing of a substantial number of JCIDS, 
supporting, and new emerging requirements documents. The contract shall review each of the 
manned/unmanned platform programs currently in effect requirements documents and analyze 
to determine validity of the current capability in respect to Large Scale Combat Operations and 
the ability of the systems to operate in a Large Scale Combat operational environment.  
 
1.5  General Information: 
 
1.5.1  Quality Control Plan (QCP): The Contractor shall develop and maintain a QCP to 
ensure services are performed in accordance with (IAW) this PWS. The Contractor shall 
develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of 
defective services. The Contractor's QCP is the means by which it assures that the work 
provided complies with the requirements of the contract. 
 
The Contractor’s Proposed QCP shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer (KO) through the 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) for review within within 30 days after contract 
award. A comprehensive written QCP shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer (KO) and 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) within 5 working days when changes are made 
thereafter. After acceptance of the quality control plan, the Contractor shall receive the KO’s 
acceptance in writing of any proposed change to his QC system.  
 
The Government will review and either notify the Contractor in writing of acceptance of the 
plan or return their comments to the Contractor within 30 days. If the Government has provided 
comments, the Contractor shall then have 14 days to submit a Final QCP. After receipt of the 
Final QCP, the Contractor may receive the Contracting Officer’s acceptance in writing. Any 
proposed changes to the accepted QCP are required to be resubmitted for acceptance by the 
Contracting Officer no later than 30 days prior to the anticipated change and before 
implementation by the Contractor. The timeline noted above will apply for review and 
acceptance for proposed changes. At a minimum, the QCP must include and answer the 
following to be acceptable:  
 
(a) A chart showing the organizational structure and lines of authority, the names, 
qualifications, duties, responsibilities, and classification of each member of the Contractor's 
Quality Control Team; 
 

Page 4 of 53 
  AUG 22 
(b) How the Contractor will monitor work to ensure performance complies with all 
deliverables (etc. timelines, deadlines, and goals); 
 
(c) How the Contractor will monitor work to ensure performance complies with all 
specifications and requirements of the contract, including the contract’s clauses; 
 
(d) How the Contractor will monitor and ensure staff qualifications remain current and 
valid including Department of Defense (DoD) Contractor Personnel Office (DOCPER) 
processes/approvals throughout contract performance; 
 
(e) How the Contractor will ensure all keys issued will remain controlled items 
(Paragraph 1.7 Key Control); 
 
(f) How the Contractor will inventory and track maintenance of all Government Provided 
Equipment / Materials; 
 
(g) How the Contractor will identify, investigate, and correct any non-conforming 
performance and prevent similar deficiencies in the future; and 
 
(h) How the Contractor will file and save all Quality Control related documents for the 
life of the contract plus 5 years. 
 
1.5.1.1  The Contractor shall inform the COR of issues or potential issues that might affect the 
performance within 2 working days of identifying those issues. Verbal reports shall be followed 
up by written reports within 14 working days.  
 
1.5.2  Quality Assurance: The Government will evaluate the Contractor’s performance under 
this contract in accordance with the Government quality assurance procedures. These 
procedures primarily focus on what the Government must do to ensure that the Contractor has 
performed in accordance with the performance standards. They define how the performance 
standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the acceptable quality levels 
(performance thresholds). 
 
1.5.3  Recognized Holidays: The following provides information on recognized holidays for 
the purpose of the PWS. If submittal of any documentation (e.g. deliverables, submittals, etc.) 
deadlines fall on a holiday, the closest work day prior to the holiday will apply as the deadline 
for submittal.  
 
1.5.3.1  U.S. Holidays: Work shall not be performed on U.S. federally recognized holidays 
occurring during the normal workweek unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer. 
When a U.S. holiday occurs on a Saturday or a Sunday, the holiday is observed on the 
preceding Friday or following Monday, respectively.  
New Year’s Day January 1st   M. L. King Memorial Day 3rd Monday in Jan 
Presidents Day 3rd Monday in February  Memorial Day last Monday in May 
Juneteenth June 19th                                          Independence Day July 4th     
Labor Day 1st Monday in September                  Columbus Day 2nd Monday in October

  AUG 22 
Veteran’s Day November 11th                            Thanksgiving Day 4th Thursday in November 
Christmas Day December 25th  
 
1.5.4  Operating Hours: The Government facility office hours, facility operating hours, and the 
Contractor support hour requirements are the same. The Contractor is responsible for 
conducting business, between the Government Facility hours of 0730-1630 Monday thru 
Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or 
national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings. 
For other than firm fixed price contracts, the Contractor shall not be reimbursed when the 
Government facility is closed for the above reasons. The Contractor must at all times maintain 
an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS 
when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons.  The Contractor shall 
maintain an adequate workforce at all times, for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks 
defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons. 
When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the 
workforce is essential. In the event of a Contractor employee position vacancy exceeding thirty 
(30) days the Contractor shall invoice the Government at a rate reflecting the reduced labor 
level of effort until such time as the Contractor identifies a replacement Contract employee 
(acceptable to the Government in accordance with the qualifications set forth in this PWS), 
hires the individual, and the employee is on-site supporting the contract work effort. Contractor 
personnel work schedules may be flexed to meet manpower requirements for weekend and 
extended duty periods during unit visits, training and exercises. Any time the Contractor is not 
in the office due to appointments, leave, or other reasons, the Contractor shall make the 
appropriate entry on the applicable Directorate calendar to ensure the Government lead is 
aware. Emergencies and unexpected absences will be addressed on a case-by-case basis.

DARPA-SN-26-63
1
Special Notice
Area-Multiplied Photonic-crystal Enhanced Devices (AMPED)
Proposers Day
DARPA-SN-26-63
April 8, 2026
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency 
Microsystems Technology Office 
675 North Randolph Street 
Arlington, VA 22203-2114


DARPA-SN-26-63
2
AMPED Proposers Day
Special Notice DARPA-SN-26-63
Area-Multiplied Photonic-crystal Enhanced Devices (AMPED)
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)
Microsystems Technology Office (MTO)
Posting Date: April 8, 2026
Event Date: May 13, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time (ET)
Registration Deadline: April 29, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET)
Registration Website: https://cvent.me/Veexab
Attendance is restricted to U.S. Persons only (U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents)
Technical POC: Dr. David Meyer, MTO Program Manager
E-mail: AMPED@darpa.mil
PROPOSERS DAY DESCRIPTION:
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) will host an in-person Proposers Day in support 
of the DARPA Program Solicitation (PS) for AMPED on May 13, 2026, at the DARPA Conference Center 
(DCC), Arlington, VA, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET. DARPA anticipates releasing the AMPED Program 
Solicitation (PS) prior to Proposers Day. If released, the PS will be made available at https://sam.gov/.
The goals of the Proposers Day are:
(1) To introduce the science and technology community (industry, academia, and government) to the 
AMPED program vision and goals;
(2) To facilitate interaction between researchers with capabilities and interests relevant to the 
AMPED program goals;
(3) To collect questions during the event that DARPA may answer and make available in a Question 
and Answer (Q&A) document; and
(4) To encourage and promote teaming arrangements among organizations that have the relevant 
expertise, research facilities, and capabilities for executing research and development responsive 
to the AMPED program goals.
The Proposers Day will include overview presentations by government personnel and opportunities for 
team building among the participants. The meeting will start with presentations by DARPA, including a 
technical briefing and a contracting discussion to further describe the planned PS objectives and content. 
These will be followed by a Q&A session, a poster session, and breakout meetings with the Program 
Manager.
PROGRAM OBJECTIVE AND DESCRIPTION:
The Area-Multiplied Photonic-crystal Enhanced Devices (AMPED) program aims to create a new paradigm 
in scalable semiconductor laser technology. By leveraging novel photonic structures, AMPED will 
overcome fundamental scaling limitations of current laser designs, creating the foundation for a highly 
manufacturable, low-size-weight-and-power (SWaP), and widely proliferated laser technology for the 
Department of War (DoW) and relevant commercial applications. AMPED will demonstrate single-mode, 
diffraction-limited, continuous-wave laser devices capable of high power.
The ability to increase the power of today’s single-mode semiconductor lasers is fundamentally 
constrained by physical limitations inherent to their traditional device architecture. This constraint 
manifests as two primary technical challenges:

DARPA-SN-26-63
3
Technical Challenge 1: Area scaling for single-mode emission
Single-mode semiconductor lasers such as edge-emitting lasers (EELs) and vertical-cavity surface-emitting 
lasers (VCSELs) are fundamentally limited to 1D scaling. While their output power generally scales with 
the volume of the active gain region, expanding this region in the transverse directions allows for 
unwanted higher-order lasing modes to emerge, which significantly degrades the beam quality. In other 
words, the physical volume overlap of the cavity geometry and the gain medium geometry prevents 
independent scaling of each. Photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers (PCSELs) offer a path forward by 
physically separating the gain medium from the optical cavity, but current PCSEL designs face their own 
scaling challenges. As the PCSEL device diameter increases, the mode margin between the desired 
fundamental mode gain and competing higher-order mode gain collapses rapidly, making it very difficult 
to maintain a stable, single-mode beam beyond a certain size. Current approaches using simple photonic 
crystal lattice designs are approaching their single-mode limits and cannot deliver further scaling.
Technical Challenge 2: Maximizing power density by minimizing loss
Once laser device area is maximized, power can be further increased by increasing the number of photons 
generated per unit area. However, this power conversion efficiency is reduced by optical, electrical, and 
other losses. Stacking multiple gain regions vertically, a successful technique used in VCSELs, may be 
limited in current PCSEL designs because n++/p++ tunnel junctions between gain layers introduce 
substantial free-carrier absorption, counteracting the benefits of additional gain. Similarly, as more 
features are designed into the photonic crystal to extend single-mode operation to larger device size, the 
area of high conductivity material shrinks leading to more resistive loss in the vertical path of current flow. 
Today, these challenges are handled with incremental modifications to existing PCSEL designs, which have 
yielded diminishing returns. It has become apparent that the search for piecewise improvements cannot 
solve the problem of limited power scaling. The key to addressing these two technical challenges is to 
redirect the effort to a fundamental redesign of the laser device’s architecture, leveraging all three 
dimensions of design flexibility. AMPED seeks innovative strategies that combine novel in-plane photonic 
crystal designs with out-of-plane epitaxial and gain structures to overcome the limitations of current 
approaches and produce the next generation of semiconductor laser technology.
This meeting will be held at the CUI level. Attendance is restricted by registration and to U.S. Persons 
(U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents) only. 
All attendees will be required to present Government-issued photo identification upon entry to the 
event. All U.S. Permanent Residents will be required to present their permanent residency card.
REGISTRATION INFORMATION:
Registration is limited by the venue capacity. The maximum number of registrants per organization may 
be limited. The determination of maximum participants per organization and what constitutes an 
organization will be made by the DARPA Program Manager. Registrations will be cut off at the registration 
deadline listed above or once attendance capacity is met, whichever comes first. Early registration is 
strongly recommended. Any change to the registration deadline will be captured via an amendment to 
this notice and an update to the registration website. There will be no on-site registration. 
The Proposers Day is open only to registered potential proposers. The event is closed to the general public 
and media. An online registration form, preliminary agenda, links to required forms, and meeting details 
for the Proposers Day can be found at the registration website.

DARPA-SN-26-63
4
AMPED CUI Materials Request Forms must be filled out by a representative from each organization 
attending the event, asserting the organization’s ability to safeguard CUI. The AMPED CUI Materials 
Request Forms must be submitted at the time of registration via the registration website. 
A completed DARPA Form 104, “DARPA Conference Center Visitor Requirements for Unclassified 
Meetings” must be filled out by all attendees. For additional information please refer to the Visitor 
Information page on the DARPA website (http://www.darpa.mil/policy/visitor-information). DARPA Form 
104 can be accessed and submitted at https://dtsn.darpa.mil/eform104/visitor/9aa7757f-a017-451c-
ae8f-bf484c1dfb65. 
Additionally, all meeting registrants who are not U.S. Citizens must complete and submit a DARPA Form 
60 “U.S. Permanent Resident and Foreign National Visit Request”, which can be submitted via the 
following link: https://dtsn.darpa.mil/eform60/. Additional questions regarding foreign national visits to 
DARPA, or its events, may be sent to your DARPA Point of Contact or the Security and Intelligence 
Directorate International Security staff at SIDInternationalsecurity@darpa.mil.
All forms must be submitted no later than the registration deadline of April 29, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET. 
Failure to complete and submit the required forms prior to the date and time noted above may result in 
cancellation of existing registration.
TEAMING: 
While not required, DARPA is open to teaming amongst the community as appropriate and when strategic 
to achieve program outcomes. To facilitate the building of teams, Proposers Day registrants may choose 
to participate in the options below: 
1. Attendee List: Participant contact information (name, title/position, organization, email 
address) will be included on an AMPED Proposers Day attendee list distributed to other 
prospective proposers. Registrants may indicate during registration whether they approve 
publication of their contact information. 
2. Proposer Profile List: Interested parties should submit a one-page profile consisting of their 
contact information (name, title/position, organization, email, telephone number, mailing 
address, and, if applicable, organization website), a brief unclassified description of their technical 
competencies, and, if applicable, the expertise desired from other teams/organizations. All 
profiles must be emailed to AMPED@darpa.mil no later than April 29, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET. 
Following this deadline, the consolidated teaming profiles will be sent via email to the proposers 
who submitted a profile. Specific content, communications, networking, and team formation are 
the sole responsibility of the participants. Neither DARPA nor the DoW endorses the information 
and organizations contained in the consolidated teaming profile document, nor does DARPA or 
the DoW exercise any responsibility for improper dissemination of the teaming profiles. 
3. Requests Through Email: Prospective proposers can also request the attendee list and/or the 
prospective proposer profile list through email at AMPED@darpa.mil. All email requests must be 
received by June 19, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET and follow the same security requirements as Proposers 
Day attendees (e.g., government photo ID and DARPA Form 60). It is incumbent on email 
requesters to ensure all provided information is accurate. DARPA will not provide access to secure 
data transfer capabilities (e.g., DoD SAFE), and DARPA reserves the right to deny requests 
stemming from its vetting of requesters’ security documentation.

DARPA-SN-26-63
5
POSTERS:
A poster session will be held to facilitate interaction among attendees and provide an opportunity to those 
who would like to showcase their capabilities and build strong teams to solve the challenge presented in 
AMPED. There is no specific template for the poster; however, posters should highlight proposer 
capabilities and teaming requirements and must include presenter’s contact information. Posters should 
not contain any Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or classified information and must be suitable 
for unlimited public release. There is a limit of one poster per organization, and posters should be no 
larger than 24 x 36 inches. Registrants must indicate their intent to participate in the poster session during 
registration. Poster presentations will be limited to the first 80 requests due to room constraints, but for 
any prospective proposer who conveys interest in participating in the poster session after the quantity 
limit has been reached, that prospective proposer’s poster will be distributed to all other confirmed 
Proposers Day attendees.
BREAKOUT SESSIONS: 
One-on-one breakout sessions with the AMPED Program Manager will be available during the Proposers 
Day. CUI discussion will be allowed. Advance registration is required. 10-minute breakout sessions will be 
scheduled from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET. To request a session, please indicate your discussion topic and 
participating attendees (no more than five) when registering. Please note that all members participating 
in the breakout sessions must be successfully registered in order to attend. Requests submitted through 
registration do not guarantee selection for an individual session. All registered attendees chosen to 
participate in breakout sessions will receive notification by May 6, 2026, containing their selection, 
scheduled time and location, and detailed guidance.
DARPACONNECT:
Entities who have not worked with DARPA before are encouraged to learn more about DARPAConnect, 
an initiative established to facilitate collaboration between DARPA and potential performers. The 
DARPAConnect team offers customized support, resources, and guidance on how to prepare ideas for 
high-impact conversations with DARPA program managers. Please visit DARPAConnect.us to access a 
digital hub of online resources, including a curriculum for self-paced learning, personalized support, and 
in-person and virtual events. To prepare for the Proposers Day, attendees can leverage the learning 
module on “Making the Most of a DARPA Proposers Day.” In addition to the self-paced online materials, 
the DARPAConnect team is able to schedule one-on-one conversations to discuss specific ideas, questions, 
and paths to DARPA. Use the contact form at DARPAConnect.us or email the DARPAConnect team directly 
at darpaconnect@darpa.mil to request assistance.
ADMINISTRATIVE:
All administrative and technical questions should be directed to AMPED@darpa.mil. Please refer to the 
Special Notice number (DARPA-SN-26-63) in all correspondence.
This Special Notice is issued solely for information and program planning purposes and does not 
constitute a formal solicitation for proposals or proposal abstracts; any so sent will be disregarded. 
Attendance is strictly voluntary and shall not obligate, or be construed to require, any attendee to respond 
to any subsequent Special Notice (SN) or Solicitation related to this topic. DARPA will not provide 
reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this Special Notice. Respondents are advised that 
DARPA is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of any information received or provide feedback to 
respondents with respect to any information submitted under this Special Notice.

THIS IS AN INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT FOR MARKET RESEARCH, INFORMATION, AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS OR PROPOSAL (RFQ/RFP). THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT BE OBLIGATED TO ISSUE A SOLICITATION OR AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS EVENT. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT REIMBURSE ANY COSTS INCURRED BY VENDORS IN CONNECTION WITH ATTENDANCE OR PARTICIPATION.

The Federal Prison Industries (UNICOR), Office Furniture Business Group, will host an in-person Industry Day on May 8, 2026, in Coleman, FL.  This is a no-cost event, open to all industry partners with capabilities in comprehensive space planning and office furniture layout design.

UNICOR is a self-sustaining, wholly-owned government corporation established in 1934 that provides job training and skills to federal inmates. It manufactures products and provides services—ranging from furniture and electronics to clothing and data entry—primarily for federal agencies.

UNICOR's Office Furniture Group (OFG) provides an extensive range of high-quality, cost-effective office furniture and services to Federal civilian agencies and the DoD, while simultaneously providing valuable work experience and training for Federal inmates.

Event Location:

FCC Coleman/UNICOR

846 NE 54th Terrace

Coleman, FL  33521

Event Schedule:

May 8, 2026 – 8:30 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. EST

8:30 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. Welcome, FPI Introductions, Factory Tour, Presentations by FPI staff

11:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. Lunch

12:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. One on one industry sessions 

A limit of one, 30-minute session (15 minutes for presentation and 15 minutes for Questions and Answers), per company is permitted.  Companies interested in participating must register by the stated due date below.  Invitations will be sent out to registered companies once a timeslot has been scheduled.  These sessions will take place between the hours of 12:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m.  These one-on-one demonstrations will allow a company to showcase its current and future capabilities relevant to the Government’s need.  The Government is interested in the registrant’s space plan and design of office furniture placement capabilities, historical successes and future goals, and other relevant information.  

Note:

Please be advised that laptops, mobile phones, electronic communication tools, and recording devices are strictly prohibited within the correctional facility. Each firm will present to a panel of up to ten FPI personnel and is encouraged to provide printed handouts or physical materials for distribution. Any digital presentations must be limited to PDF or PowerPoint formats and submitted to the designated Point of Contact prior to the event date, as all electronic media will be displayed via a government-owned computer operated exclusively by FPI staff.

RSVP & Registration Information

To attend, all participants must complete the attached registration form and back ground clearance form and email them to peyton.perry@usdoj.gov with the subject line: “UNICOR Industry Day, Sales and Marketing” no later than 3:30 p.m., EST, April 20, 2026.

Registration is required prior to beginning of the day.

Firms must indicate on the form if they wish to request a one-on-one session.  

As this event is at a secure site, all attendees must be pre-approved and listed on the registration form.  Individuals not on the list will not be permitted past the security check point.

One-on-one appointments are limited and will be scheduled on a first come, first serve basis.

Rules of Engagement:

This is merely an opportunity for an exchange of information and NOT a solicitation.  

NO gifts or giveaways are permitted.

The use of recording devices (cameras, tape recorders, etc.) is strictly prohibited.

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY 
FDA-SS-2026-040726 
 
   
 
1 | Page  
 
Title: ThinkTrends Software Implementation and Support  
Agency: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 
Notice Type: Sources Sought / Market Research 
Posting Date: April 7, 2026 
Response Due Date: April 17, 2026 
NAICS Code: 541511 – Custom Computer Programming Services (or appropriate) 
Size Standard: $30M 
1. Purpose 
The FDA is conducting market research to identify capable vendors to support the 
implementation and integration of ThinkTrends software and related human interventions 
across FDA operations. This enhanced effort will leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI), 
automation, and emerging technologies to improve operational efficiency, data management, 
and regulatory processes. 
This Sources Sought notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not a 
solicitation. Responses will be used to determine the availability of qualified vendors and to 
inform future acquisition strategy, including potential sole-source justification or competitive 
procurement. 
2. Background 
The BPA will support FDA’s efforts in: 
• Advanced Data Management: Data migration, integration, cleansing, cataloging, 
annotation, and implementation of data lakes or data mesh architectures.  
• Emerging Technology Integration: RPA, AI-based OCR (>90% accuracy), blockchain, 
edge computing, generative AI, NLP, and LLMs for document summarization.  
• Intelligent Question-Answering: AI-assisted drafting of regulatory responses, 
highlighting issues, and providing contextual/historical data.  
• Advanced Visualization & Analytics: Interactive dashboards, predictive analytics, and 
virtual/augmented reality for data visualization.  
• Automation & Process Enhancements: Workflow automation, AI-driven quality 
control, and regulatory tracking.  
• FDA System Enhancements: Next-generation OCR, FAERS support with AI signal 
detection, and intelligent digitization of document rooms.  

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY 
FDA-SS-2026-040726 
 
   
 
2 | Page  
 
• Data-Driven Tools: AI decision support, predictive models, and digital twins to optimize 
regulatory processes.  
• User Experience Improvements: Intuitive AI-assisted interfaces, personalized 
dashboards, and voice-activated assistants.  
• Comprehensive Support: ThinkTrends license acquisition, agile project management, 
and continuous staff training.  
 
3. Capability Requirements 
Interested vendors should demonstrate experience in: 
1. Implementing AI-based software solutions in large-scale enterprise environments.  
2. Data migration, integration, and management using modern architectures (data lakes, data 
mesh).  
3. AI/ML model development, deployment, and explainability.  
4. OCR, NLP, RPA, and emerging technology solutions in highly regulated environments.  
5. Designing user interfaces and dashboards for diverse user roles.  
6. Agile project management and technology adoption support in federal or regulated 
organizations.  
 
4. Response Instructions 
Please submit responses in PDF format via email to Lilibeth Deato at 
lilibeth.deato@fda.hhs.gov by COB, April 17, 2026. Responses should be no longer than 6 
pages and include: 
1. Company name, business size, and point of contact.  
2. Description of relevant experience, including past performance.  
3. Capabilities related to AI, automation, and emerging technologies listed above.  
4. Any certifications, licenses, or unique capabilities relevant to the requirement.  
5. Ability to support a BPA with multiple optional tasks or pilot projects.  
6. If on GSA, identification of the firm's GSA Schedule contract(s) by Schedule number and 
SINs that are applicable to this potential requirement. Detailed list of items included and 
not included on the GSA contract to meet this requirement. 
 
 

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY 
FDA-SS-2026-040726 
 
   
 
3 | Page  
 
5. Additional Information 
• This is market research only; no award will result from this notice.  
• Responses will assist the Government in determining:  
o Availability of qualified sources  
o Potential for small business set-asides  
o Whether a sole-source BPA is justified  
• All questions regarding this notice should be submitted in writing to Lilibeth Deato at 
lilibeth.deato@fda.hhs.gov by COB, April 17, 2026. 
 
6.Disclaimer and Important Notes  
 
This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the 
information provided in the response. The Government reserves the right to use information 
provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any 
organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently 
detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization’s qualifications to perform the 
work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge 
receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any 
information submitted. After a review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and 
solicitation may be published. However, responses to this notice will not be considered adequate 
responses to a solicitation. 
 
7.Confidentiality  
 
No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your 
response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in 
any resultant solicitation(s). 
 
(End of SS)
