DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK 
WEAPONS EFFECTS 
 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD), Survivability and Weapons Effects Division 
(Code 66) is responsible for theoretical and applied research efforts to extend the understanding of the response of US 
Navy platforms to threat weapon engagements.  These engagements includ e underwater explosions (UNDEX) , air 
explosions (AIREX), and penetrating weapons  with modeling & simulation (M&S) of UNDEX and AIREX events 
being a major part of this mission that requires unique software applications and expertise. 
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea 
and surface vessels to develop and utilize  specialized software codes  that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire  events 
and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs ; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a 
far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near 
miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of a computational models; 5) Solve 
finite element model’s elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; 
and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. 
The technical areas in this Task Order (TO) shall include comprehensive software engineering, development, and 
enhancement, finite element and reduced order model construction to include deactivation diagrams and quality 
assurance, numerical model  and algorithm  review and verification , software application training , design yard 
qualifications submittal review , data analysis, data science, and artificial intelligence / machine learning in order to 
support the vulnerability design processes for multiple Navy platforms. 
3.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
• MIL-S-901D, MILITARY SPECIFICATION: SHOCK TESTS. H.I. (HIGH -IMPACT) SHIPBOARD 
MACHINERY, EQUIPMENT, AND SYSTEMS, REQUIREMENTS FOR (17 -MAR-1989) 
4.0 SCOPE OF WORK 
The contractor shall provide specialized scientific, engineering, and technical services in the field s of UNDEX shock 
qualification, UNDEX damage assessment, AIREX damage assessment , and ship survivability directed towards 
research, development, test , and evaluation (RDT&E) for various submarine and surface ship programs. The 
contractor shall provide all services, materials, facilities and equipment necessary to perform specific tasks within the 
following general tasking areas: 
4.1 Support the development, implementation, and transition of new technologies involving: testing 
strategies, transient shock analysis , and analytical methods that improve the ability of ship, 
components, systems, and personnel to resist the damaging effects of threat weapon attacks. Follow 
rigorous software development practices, including strict version control, continuous integration,  
use of code documentation generators to be specified in each Technical Instruction (TI) , unit and 
regression testing, code c overage assessments, and agile management for all tools developed or 
modified and share code repositories with Government personnel . Support developing, 
documenting, and execution strategies for verification and validation (V&V) of numerical 
simulations. Contractor support will range from limited assistance to government engineers on a 

 
task to autonomous execution of tasking with all results reported to the government as required by 
the TO and associated Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) deliverables. Guidance and criteria 
for contractor support will be defined in each individual TI. (CDRL A001, A002, A003) 
4.2 Develop Software: 
4.2.1 Support in the development of software applications, code, modules, and plugins that will 
aide in the fields of UNDEX shock qualification, UNDEX damage assessment, AIREX 
weapons effects evaluation, and ship survivability analysis. 
4.3 Develop Training and Documentation Manuals for Software: 
4.3.1 Develop detailed software theory manuals, user’s manuals , and verification manuals 
including example problems. (CDRL A003) 
4.3.2 Develop and conduct software application training courses for any tools developed in Task 
Area 4.2 for Government personnel at NSWCCD and/or the contractor’s facility. (CDRL 
A003) 
4.3.3 Develop and conduct training related to shock qualification of shock test machines, 
platforms and vehicles including training on UNDEX theory and methods of analyzing 
ship and equipment responses to underwater explosion shock. (CDRL A002) 
4.4 Software Support: 
4.4.1 Provide technical support to users to fix issues that arise post software deployments. 
Software is to be defined in the individual TI and may include but not be limited to specific 
weapons effects software such as  but not limited to  ASAP, NESM, INSiTE, TDC, 
UERDTools, and SUBVALUE. Maintain logs of technical issues and resolutions and 
provide quarterly reports tracking resolutions. (CDRL A001, A003, A004) 
4.5 Develop Analytical Methods and Various types of Models: 
4.5.1 Develop defined finite element and reduced order representations of test articles, platforms, 
and vehicles including systems and systems deactivation diagrams that appropriately 
represent and capture their responses to a damaging event due to UNDEX, AIREX, and 
penetration mechanics, documenting all efforts. (CDRL A001, A002) 
4.5.2 Develop or support the creation of or modification to finite element and reduced order 
models of naval maritime platforms to include structure, components, systems, and system 
deactivation logic. 
4.5.3 Develop defined finite element models and reduced order representations of shock test 
machines, platforms and vehicles that appropriately represent and capture their responses 
to a shock event documenting all efforts. (CDRL A002) 
4.5.4 Develop and execute strategies for analyses and qualification of external volumes subjected 
to weapons loads. (CDRL A002) 
4.6 Execute Computer Model Simulations and Analyses: 
4.6.1 Conduct computational UNDEX analyses of Shock test machines, platforms and vehicles, 
documenting all efforts. (CDRL A002) 
4.6.2 Conduct computational UNDEX, AIREX, and penetration mechanics analyses of test 
articles, platforms, and vehicles, documenting all efforts. (CDRL A001, A002) 
4.6.3 Conduct and document data analyses and research available data and documentation on 
both physical measurements obtained from Shock Testing and computational data. (CDRL 
A002) 
4.6.4 Support the e valuation of  numerical models, reduced order models, and finite element 
models developed by other contract activities  or Government personnel, for accuracy and 
applicability to s hock design and qualification processes , hull integrity evaluations, and 
live fire test and evaluation assessment s including recoverability, documenting all efforts  
in technical reports . Applicable agreement and use rights to be provided in individual TI 
defining subject tasking. (CDRL A002) 

 
4.6.5 Conduct or support computational weapons effects assessments of threat weapons against 
naval maritime platforms in all aspects of platform vulnerability and recoverability 
documenting all efforts. (CDRL Item A002) 
4.7 Provide support to shock qualification efforts for shipboard equipment in accordance with ship 
specifications including generation of ship and equipment finite element models, review of technical 
analyses and reports, and performing finite element and reduced order model analyses. Finite 
element and reduced order models may be provided by the government or developed by the 
contractor. Status of finite element and reduced models will be defined in the individual TI(s). 
(CDRL A002) 
4.8 Support Testing and Material Procurement: 
4.8.1 Provide support to conduct weapons effects  testing or other Navy shock qualification 
testing and measurement efforts including test design, planning, and execution efforts. This 
includes both physical, on-site support, in addition to support from the contractor’s primary 
place of performance. 
4.8.2 Provide support and technical guidance to shock test and trials planning, documenting all 
efforts. (CDRL A002) 
4.8.3 Procure equipment, materials, and information as necessary  with consent from 
Government to provide technical support as defined in the TI(s). 
5.0 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT/PROPERTY/INFORMATION 
The Government shall furnish all necessary Government -Furnished Equipment (GFE) and/or Government -
Furnished Property (GFP). Specific GFE/GFP items will be detailed within each corresponding Task Instruction (TI). 
All requisite information pertaining to the GFE/GFP will be included in the associated TI. 
6.0 DATA REQUIREMENTS AND DELIVERABLES 
Data to be provided shall be prepared as specified in individual TIs and shall be distributed to the designated 
Technical Advisor (TA). In addition, a copy of the Monthly Status Report shall be provided to the Contracting 
Officer’s Representative (COR). Below is a table of CRLS for each Task Area.
  
CDRL Title Task Areas 
A001 Computer Software Product 4.1 – 4.5 
A002 Technical Report – Study Services 4.1 – 4.5 
A003 Software User Manual and Support 4.1 – 4.5 
A004 Presentation Materials 4.1 – 4.5 
A005 Meeting Minutes 4.1 – 4.5 
A006 Contracting Officer’s Management Report 4.1 – 4.5 
A007 Software License Requirements List 4.1 – 4.5 
 
7.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 

 
Security will be in accordance with the terms and conditions cited in the DD Form 254, in Section J, of the TO.  The 
maximum level of security classification required for the work under this contract is SECRET; the classification of 
work under this contract will be specified in the individual TI. When tasking is at the CUI level, un-cleared US 
persons may work on the tasking in accordance with relevant security requirements  of the specific TI. 
7.1 Contractor shall be able to send and retrieve classified information  and electronic files to/from the 
government upon request using the Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNET), or via 
FEDEX, or by contractor courier. The maximum duration from the time of request to time of 
classified information receipt or retrieval shall be no more than 48 hours. 
7.2 Non-Disclosure   
The Contractor shall not disclose any information provided by the Government or developed or 
relating to the items to be delivered and services to be performed without the PCO’s prior approval.  
All data provided to the Contractor shall be protected from t he public.  Dissemination or public 
disclosure includes permitting access to such information by foreign nationals or by any other person 
or entity, publication of technical or scientific papers, advertising, or any other proposed public 
release.  The Cont ractor shall physically protect such information to prevent access by any 
unauthorized person or entity. 
7.3 Performance in Government Facilities   
The Contractor shall comply with the requirements of local instructions regarding performance in 
Government facilities.  All persons engaged in work while on Government property shall be subject 
to search of their persons (no bodily search) and vehicles at  any time by the Government, and shall 
report any known or suspected security violations to the appropriate Security Department.  
Assignment, transfer, and reassignment of Contractor personnel shall be at the discretion of the 
Contractor.  However, when the Government directs, the Contractor shall remove from contract 
performance any person who endangers life, property, or national security through improper 
conduct.  All Contractor personnel engaged in work while on Government property shall be subject 
to the DoD Standards of Conduct. 
7.4 Information Security and Computer System Usage 
Computer Usage: In accordance with U.S. Navy policy, any personnel, including the Contractor, 
who utilizes DoD-owned systems, shall assume responsibility for adherence to restrictions regarding 
internet and e-mail usage. Navy policy prohibits racist, sexis t, threatening, pornographic, personal 
business, subversive or politically partisan communications.  All personnel, including the 
Contractor, are accountable and must act accordingly.  
7.5 System Monitoring: DoD computer systems are monitored to ensure that the use is authorized, to 
facilitate protection against unauthorized access, and to verify security procedures, survivability and 
operational security.  During monitoring, information may be examined, recorded, copied, and used 
for authorized purposes.  All information, including personal information, placed on or sent over a 
DoD system may be monitored.  Use of a DoD system constitutes consent to monitoring.  
Unauthorized use may result in criminal prosecution.  Evidence of unauthorized use collected during 
monitoring may be used as a basis for recommended administrative, criminal or adverse action.  
7.6 Electronic Spillages 
7.6.1 General: Electronic spillages (ES) are unacceptable and pose a risk to national security.  
An ES is defined as classified data placed on an information system (IS), media or hardcopy 
document possessing insufficient security controls to protect the data at  the required 
classification level, thus posing a risk to national security (e.g., Sensitive Compartmented 
Information (SCI) onto collateral, Secret onto Unclassified).  The Contractor's performance 
as it relates to ES will be evaluated by the Government.  Electronic spillage reflects on the 
overall security posture of the Government and a lack of attention to detail with regard to 
the handling of classified information of IS security discipline.  If a Contractor is 

 
determined to be responsible for an ES, all direct and indirect costs incurred by the 
Government for ES remediation will be charged to the Contractor. The incident will be 
reflected in the Contractor’s performance rating. 
7.6.2 Spillage Responsibilities: Local command security will continue to be responsible for the 
corrective action plan in accordance with the security guidance reflected on the DD Form 
254. Command security will identify the Contractor facility and contract number associated 
with all ES during the investigation indicating Contractor support. Command security will 
notify the contracts division with the Contractor facility name and contract number, 
incident specifics and associated costs for cleanup.  The PCO will be responsible for 
working with the Contractor to capture the costs incurred during the spillage clean up.  The 
Contractor is also responsible for taking Cybersecurity Awareness training annually via its 
Facility Security Officer (FSO) as part of the mandatory training requirements.  If an ES

FA300226R0015 
Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought (SS) 
 
Strategic Talent & Assessment Research (STAR) Support  
 
1.0 DISCLAIMER 
 
This Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought (SS) seeks information regarding availability and 
capability of all qualiﬁed small business ﬁrms to perform a potential requirement. Responses received 
will be used for acquisition strategic decision-making purposes only and will not be disclosed outside this 
agency. This announcement is for informational purposes only. The information obtained may be used 
for acquisition planning purposes. This announcement does not constitute an Invitation for Bids, 
Request for Proposals, or a Request for Quotations, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the 
Government to issue a contract or otherwise pay for the information solicited. The Government does 
not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice. Companies responding to this RFI/SS notice 
are advised that participation does not ensure involvement in any future solicitation or contract award. 
No proposals are being requested or accepted under this notice, and this announcement shall not be 
construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or to ultimately award a contract, 
nor does this synopsis restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. Contact with 
Government personnel, other than those speciﬁed in this RFI/SS, by interested ﬁrms or their employees 
regarding this requirement is not permitted. The Government will not pay for any information submitted 
in response to this announcement. Any costs associated with providing information to either this notice 
or any follow-up information requests shall not be reimbursed. Costs incurred as a result of this 
announcement shall be borne solely by the respondent and shall not be payable by the Government.  
 
2.0 DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT 
 
2.1. The 338th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (ESS), at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) – Randolph, Texas 
(TX), is seeking information concerning the availability of technically capable small business ﬁrms to 
provide non-personal services for the Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC)/ Strategic Research & 
Assessment Branch (DSYX), located at JBSA-Randolph TX. The Headquarters, United States Air Force, 
Director of Air Force Military Force Management Policy, AF/A1P, Accession and Training Division (A1PT) 
is responsible for the Air Force Examining Activities Program, which supports the STAR Program 
established in DAFMAN 36-2664. The STAR mission is to develop assessments and screening processes 
to assess recruit and Airmen knowledge, skills, abilities, and potential, and then optimally match 
personnel to jobs that optimize their abilities and potential to support optimal warﬁghting mission 
capability. The purpose of the program is to apply scientiﬁc evidence-based practices to optimize human 
capital management, mission capability, readiness, reduce attrition, and increase retention by improved 
selection, classiﬁcation, and utilization assessment. The Service Provider (SP) shall provide a broad set of 
technical skills critical to the eﬀectiveness of STAR, including psychometric expertise, programming, 
database management, research design, data analysis, assessment development, aviation psychology, 
and direct software and system engineering. The SP shall be expected to provide technically qualiﬁed 
employees and meet all the requirements and responsibilities listed in the attached draft Performance 
Work Statement (PWS) (Attachment 1). 
 
2.2. For purposes of this RFI/SS Notice, the main North American Industry Classiﬁcation System (NAICS) 
code for the requirement will be 541715 Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and 
Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), Size Standard: 1,000 employees.  
 

FA300226R0015 
3.0 SMALL BUSINESS INFORMATION  
 
3.1 The Government reserves the right to determine whether a Small Business (SB) set-aside is 
appropriate for this acquisition based on responses to this notice. In order to support a Government SB 
set-aside determination, interested SB concerns must provide suﬃcient written information to indicate 
their capability to successfully perform and manage all the requirements listed in the attached draft 
PWS (Attachment 1). 
 
3.2 Identify business type (Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(A)-Certified Small 
Disadvantaged Business (8a), Hubzone Small Business (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business 
(WOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business 
(SDVOSB)) based upon NAICS Code 541715, Size Standard 1,000 employees. 
 
4.0 ACQUISITION INFORMATION 
 
4.1 The Government is contemplating an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a 5-
year ordering period. Information contained in this RFI/SS is subject to change. The attached draft PWS 
document is subject to change in any resultant solicitation. 
 
5.0 RESPONSE SUBMISSION  
 
5.1 All interested parties who believe they can meet all aspects of the requirements are invited to 
complete the attached Contractor Capability Survey (see Attachment 2) describing their capability and 
qualiﬁcations to provide the required support services. The purpose of using the survey format, in lieu of 
a free format, is to obtain pertinent and uniformed information from all interested ﬁrms. Interested 
ﬁrms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for payment from 
any Department of Defense activity. Information on registration and annual conﬁrmation requirements 
may be obtained at www.SAM.gov.   
 
5.2. To be considered by the Government, interested parties must email their response and completed 
Contractor Capability Survey (Attachment 2) to the Point of Contact identified below no later than 4:00 
PM, Central Daylight Time (CDT) on 10 Apr 2026.  
 
5.3. Information contained in this RFI/Sources Sought is subject to change. It is the responsibility of 
interested parties to check SAM.gov regularly for any changes or updates. The Government is under no 
obligation to consider information received after the due date as part of the formal market research for 
this acquisition.  
 
5.4. Responses to this notice and/or questions shall be submitted via email to Contract Specialist: 
Melissa Gonzalez at melissa.gonzalez.6@us.af.mil. 
 
 
 
Attachments: 
1. Performance Work Statement (PWS)_DRAFT_31 Mar 2026 
2. Contractor Capability Survey_31 Mar 2026

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
for 
Strategic Talent and Assessment Research (STAR) Support  
31 Mar 2026 
 
SECTION I 
 
1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 
 
1.1 General. The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to acquire technical 
execution and operations support services for the Strategic Talent and Assessment Research 
(STAR) Program. This contract is specifically for non-advisory, hands-on work of building, 
running, and fixing systems, directly responsible for operational output. Services include 
providing a broad set of technical skills critical to the effectiveness of STAR, including 
psychometric expertise, programming/database management, research design, data analysis, 
assessment development, aviation psychology, and direct software and system engineering. The 
Contractor shall provide technically qualified employees to meet the stated objectives and 
accomplish the work required under this PWS. Specific requirements will be identified by the 
issuance of individual Task Orders (TOs). 
 
1.2 Background. The Headquarters, United States Air Force, Director of Air Force Military 
Force Management Policy, AF/A1P, Accession and Training Division (A1PT) is responsible for 
the Air Force Examining Activities Program, which supports the STAR established in DAFMAN 
36-2664. The STAR mission is to develop assessments and screening processes to assess recruit 
and Airmen knowledge, skills, abilities, and potential, and then optimally match personnel to 
jobs that optimize their abilities and potential to support optimal warfighting mission capability. 
The program is supported by personnel at Air Staff, the Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC), and 
Air Education and Training Command (AETC). The purpose of the program is to apply scientific 
evidence-based practices to optimize human capital management, mission capability, readiness, 
reduce attrition, and increase retention by improved selection, classification, and utilization 
assessment. The program, which includes a staff of technically qualified researchers and 
analysts, requires direct technical execution via contract for a series of specialized technical 
skills either not possessed by the staff or deemed inefficient for the staff to support with their 
skillsets. This contract supports the DoW's emphasis on direct technical execution from 
contractors. 
 
1.3 Applicable Documents. This section contains the list of compliance and reference 
documents that the contractor and contractor subs shall comply with and reference in the 
execution of this contract. Although dates are provided with each document, for the purposes of 
executing the tasks in this PWS, all references shall be to the current edition in use by the 
Government at the time of award or when options are executed. Exceptions to these documents 
will require written Government approval from the CO prior to use. This list will be confirmed 
by the Government and Contractor. It will be updated prior to contract award and again at 
contract option exercise. Updates may occur during the POP. The CO is authorized to negotiate 
for additional compliance and reference documents and updates during base and prior to 

Attachment 1 
FA300226R0015 
2 
 
subsequent PoP options. Contractors shall use these additional documents when performing the 
contract. 
 
1.3.1 Compliance Documents 
 
1.3.1.1 AFI 33-332, Air Force Privacy and Civil Liberties Program. Applies to all 
government workers including contractors that work with Air Force records to ensure they 
remain in compliance with the Privacy Act of 1974. 
 
1.3.1.2 Department of Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 
DFARS 246.401. Mandates quality assurance for service contracts, that they be addressed and 
documented to facilitate evaluation of performance.  
 
1.3.2 Reference Documents 
 
1.3.2.1 AFI 36-2618, The Enlisted Force Structure. Provides the enlisted force structure 
along with the associated levels of education, training, experience, and leadership 
responsibilities. It will be important for contractors to be familiar with this structure to provide 
relatable and applicable deliverables 
 
1.3.2.2 AFI 36-2101, Classifying Military Personnel (Officer and Enlisted). Provides 
framework for personnel classification, including procedures for alteration of Air Force 
classification codes and identifies duties and tasks needed for each position. Contractors should 
reference this document in associated work with evaluation of entry standard evaluation 
requests as well as other work that utilizes this framework and information.  
 
1.4 Scope. The Contractor shall perform multiple support activities for a variety of STAR 
projects and initiatives. Due to the dynamic nature of STAR’s mission, the Contractor’s 
Program Manager may reassign individual contractor employee positions to different projects 
as contractor support needs are adjusted to support most important priorities. Contract-
provided employees supporting this effort and their respective skillsets needed shall fall under 
one of the following Tasks below with respectively listed qualifications. 
 
This Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract provides for the award of Task 
Orders that may be funded with Operations and Maintenance (O&M), Research, Development, 
Test & Evaluation (RDT&E), or Procurement appropriations, as appropriate to the work being 
performed. The Government will define the specific appropriation (color of money) at the Task

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 
 
Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) 
 
This is a Sources Sought notice is being issued for market research purposes to 
determine the availability, capability, and interest of firms for a potential Government 
requirement 
 
NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE 
 
Requests for a solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. 
Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current 
market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. 
 
GENERAL SCOPE 
 
The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Southwestern Middle East 
District (SWM) anticipates a potential requirement for a seven-year Single Award Task 
Order Contract (SATOC) to support the pre-design activities and 100% design solution 
supporting the development of a secure compound that is ICD-705 compliant at Al 
Udeid Air Base, Qatar.  These requirements stem from the Space Forces Central 
Command (SPACECENT) and the Al Udeid Air Base 2040 Strategic Master Plan. 
 
This project is anticipated to include the following:  
 
1. Produce a Planning Charrette Report II (PCR II), including a DD Form 1391. 
 
2. Geotechnical survey. 
 
3. Plan and design a Secure Administrative Headquarters building (CATCODE 141446, 
Combat Center Building). 
 
4. Ancillary supporting facilities to include, but not limited to, secure warehouse facility, 
general purpose storage, access control and guard house complex, antennae yard 
and shelter building, multiple unit buildings, secure perimeter fencing, Intrusion 
Detection System (IDS) and Closed Circuit Television surveillance of the perimeter 
and compound. 
 
5. All site and building utility services to include, but not limited to, services for potable 
water, non-potable water/fire water, electrical distribution, surface water 
management, sanitary sewer, lift stations, pump systems, secure and unclassified 
communication network, substations, generators, fueling operations, and chilled 
water. 
 
6. All site work to include, but not limited to, any applicable demolition, site preparation 
and grading, vehicle circulation network (paved and gravel), military and personal 

vehicle parking (paved and gravel), sunshades, concrete pads, pedestrian 
circulation, coordinated shelter for base circulation services, curb, gutter, sidewalks, 
ancillary hardscapes and xeriscaping.   
 
7. It is anticipated any other supporting work necessary to make a complete and usable 
facility to include any necessary element not listed herein will also be included. 
 
The potential requirement may result in a SATOC solicitation in approximately October 
2027. If solicited the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by 
approximately June 2028. 
 
The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for the potential 
requirement is anticipated to be 541330 Engineering Services. 
 
Companies with the professional qualifications, specialized expertise, technical 
competence, and workload capacity to complete the work described above are invited 
to provide capability statements. 
 
CAPABILITY STATEMENT 
 
Please complete the questionnaire at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/kmR3vNMHup by 8 
April 2026 11:59 Eastern Time. 
 
Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may 
result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an 
acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. 
Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted of the capability 
statements received. 
 
Questions may be sent by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Tracy Gusukuma at 
tracy.m.gusukuma@usace.army.mil. 
 
Please include, ‘MARKET RESEARCH Space Campus’ in the e-mail subject line.

INDUSTRY REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
Silver Bullets (SB)  
 
31 March 2026 
 
Note: This questionnaire/survey is for obtaining information only. Companies are 
encouraged to provide responses to this questionnaire but are advised that their 
participation is voluntary only.  Contractors responding to this Request for Information 
(RFI) are placed on notice that participation in this survey does not ensure participation in 
future solicitations or contract awards.  The government will not reimburse participants 
for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. 
 
INSTRUCTIONS: 
 
1. Attached is the draft PWS for the F-15 Engineering Services effort requirement and a 
contractor capability survey, which allows you to provide your company’s capability. 
2. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you 
should provide documentation that supports your company’s capability in meeting these 
requirements.  Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being 
unable to adequately assess your capabilities.  If you lack sufficient experience in a 
particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of 
experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, 
subcontracting, etc.) 
a. Identify any areas of work that your organization believes should be broken out 
exclusively for Small Business. 
 
3. Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research.   
 
4. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to Tyler Law, 
tyler.law.4@us.af.mil.  
  

 
 
 
 
Requirements Description 
Silver Bullets (SB) 
 
 
PURPOSE/DESCRIPTION 
 
       The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the 
expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements for the sustainment of 
all F-15 engineering services areas.  All engineering tasks issued within the period of performance 
are intended to be short-term projects, estimated at typically less than 1000 hours. 
The projected period of performance for this engineering service is five-years (basic plus 4 
option years) and will continue through FY32.   
These services have been performed sole source by Boeing for roughly 25 years, at which 
point it was with McDonnell Douglas which merged with Boeing in 1997. Over the past several 
years, F-15 Engineering has used a FFP pricing arrangement, with a most recent 12 month period 
of performance. Reports are delivered as tasks are completed via e m a i l  a n d  Boeing’s BPN 
website. Thorough technical, price and/or cost analyses have been and will be performed as 
necessary by the F-15 System Program Office (SPO), Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) 
and/or the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA). 
 
A complete description of work is provided in the attached draft Performance-Work-
Statement (PWS): Silver Bullet (SB) Requirements. 
 
   
  

 
 
 
 
CONTRACTOR CAPABILITY SURVEY 
 
Silver Bullets (SB) 
 
 
Part I.  Business Information 
 
 Please provide the following business information for your company/institution and for 
any teaming or joint venture partners: 
 
• Company/Institute Name: 
• Address: 
• Point of Contact: 
• CAGE Code: 
• Phone Number: 
• E-mail Address: 
• Web Page URL: 
• Size of business pursuant to North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code:  
541330. 
 Based on the above NAICS Code, state whether your company is:  
• Small Business    (Yes / No) 
• Woman Owned Small Business  (Yes / No) 
• Small Disadvantaged Business  (Yes / No) 
• 8(a) Certified     (Yes / No) 
• HUBZone Certified    (Yes / No) 
• Veteran Owned Small Business  (Yes / No) 
• Service Disabled Veteran Small Business (Yes / No) 
• Central Contractor Registration (CCR).   (Yes / No) 
• A statement as to whether your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign, please 
indicate the country of ownership). 
 
Please provide email responses to Tyler Law, tyler.law.4@us.af.mil and Tominica Pines, 
tominica.pines@us.af.mil, no later than, 12 May 2026.   

 
 
 
 
Part II. Capability Survey Questions 
 
 
1. Describe briefly the capabilities of your facility and the nature of the goods and/or 
services you provide.  Include a description of your staff composition/experience and 
management structure. 
 
2. Describe your company's past experience on previous projects similar in complexity to 
this requirement.  Include contract numbers, a brief description of the work performed, 
period of performance, agency/organization supported, and individual point of contact 
(Contracting Officer or Program Manager). 
 
3. Describe your company’s experience in developing, validating, and utilizing engineering 
expertise for military aircraft.  
 
4. Describe your company’s experience in troubleshooting, problem analysis, and 
performance and supportability improvement issues on fielded aircraft, support 
equipment, and trainers for fighter aircraft.  
 
5. Describe your company’s capabilities and experience in testing, simulation, modeling, 
problem analysis, training, parts substitution analysis, risk assessments, inspection 
advisories and corrective actions to resolve field operational problems and improvement 
requirements, for military aircraft. Include a description of your staff’s composition and 
experience levels.  
 
6. Describe your company’s capabilities in supporting accident and incident investigations-
(to include technical support for In-Flight Emergency (IFE) assistance requests and 
technical assistance in analyzing and/or recreating the accident/incident in order to 
determine the cause).  Please detail your experience with the following:  review of 
exhibits and failed components, computer simulation, failure analysis, participation in 
Mishap Investigation Boards, and input to associated reports. 
 
7. Describe your company’s capabilities and experience in providing laboratory, ground and 
flight testing as needed to support field problem investigations and development 
activities.  
 
8. Describe your company’s capabilities and experience in designing novel and complex 
repairs of aircraft.   
 
9. Describe your company's capabilities and experience in generating technical data, 
engineering drawings and repair procedures.   
 

 
 
 
 
10. Are there specific requirements in the documentation that was provided that would 
currently preclude your company from being a viable solution in meeting the 
requirement? 
 
11. Is your company’s cost and accounting system certified by Defense Contract Auditing 
Agency (DCAA) as adequate?

1.1 Objective(s):  This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the services required to 
provide an adequate level of continuous, quick reaction, sustaining engineering and logistics 
support for the following F-15 aircraft fleets:  United States Air Force (USAF), Air National 
Guard (ANG), and FMS Partner Nations to include but not limited to Royal Saudi Air Force 
(RSAF), and Israeli Air Force (IAF), Republic of Korea Air Force, Republic of Singapore Air 
Force, and Japan Air Self Defense Force. These services include testing, simulation, problem 
analysis, training, parts substitution analysis, risk assessments, inspection advisories and 
corrective actions to resolve field operational problems and improvement requirements.

Force (USAF) by providing continuous, quick reaction engineering expertise and analysis from 
the Contractor which exceeds the technical capabilities of the F-15 System Program Office 
(SPO). The studies performed under this program prevent potential mishaps thus preserving the 
F-15 fleet. 
 
1.3 Background: The F-15 Weapon System is an aging aircraft that operates in a highly dynamic and 
unpredictable work environment. Requirements for various unique scenarios arise which require 
testing, simulation, problem analysis, training, parts substitution, analysis, risk assessment, 
inspection advisories and corrective action to resolve operational problems and improvement 
requirements.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
Product Support Business Case Analysis (BCA) for USAF E-7A Aircraft 
10 March 2026 
1.0 Description 
1.1 The United States Air Force E-7A Program Office (AFLCMC/WIW), is seeking information 
from interested companies with the ability to perform a comprehensive Product Support Business 
Case Analysis (BCA) for the E-7A aircraft fleet.  
• Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) 
• Reference Number: RFI-E7A-BCA-2026 
• Posting Date: 10 March 2026 
• Response Due Date: 11 May 2026, 5:00 PM (EST) 
• Agency: Department of the Air Force (DAF) 
• Office: E-7A System Program Office (SPO) 
• NAICS Codes: 
541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services 
541330 - Engineering Services 
1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY . This RFI is issued solely for 
information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a 
promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for 
any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and 
will not accept unsolicited proposals. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. Not responding to this RFI does not 
preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. 
2.0 Background 
The Department of the Air Force is acquiring the E-7A aircraft to replace a portion of the E-3 
Sentry Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) fleet. The E-7A will provide critical 
airborne early warning, surveillance, and battle management capabilities. To ensure optimal fleet 
readiness and long-term affordability, the E-3/E-7A SPO is seeking to identify sources capable of 
performing a comprehensive Product Support Business Case Analysis (BCA). 
The objective of this BCA is to identify the most effective and efficient product support strategy 
for the E-7A fleet throughout its planned life cycle. The PS-BCA will need to accommodate a 

fleet size of at least two but possibly up to twenty-six aircraft. The analysis will inform the Air 
Force’s decision-making process for structuring the E-7A’s sustainment enterprise. 
3.0 Scope of the Business Case Analysis (BCA) 
The Government is seeking a comprehensive BCA that analyzes the costs, benefits, and risks of 
different product support strategies for the E-7A aircraft. The analysis must address sustainment 
at both the field level (organizational and intermediate maintenance) and depot level. 
The BCA must, at a minimum, analyze the following three product support alternatives: 
Alternative Field-Level 
Sustainment 
Depot-Level 
Maintenance 
Description 
Alternative 1 Organic Organic All maintenance, supply, and 
support functions performed by 
Government personnel and 
facilities.  
Alternative 2 Hybrid Contractor A single prime contractor is 
responsible for supporting 
Active-Duty technicians with all 
aspects of field 
and the single prime 
contractor is responsible for all 
aspects of depot sustainment 
(i.e., Contractor Logistics 
Support - CLS).  
Alternative 3 Hybrid-to-Organic Hybrid-to-Organic Public-Private Partnership. A 
single prime contractor is 
responsible for supporting 
Active-Duty technicians with all 
aspects of field and the single 
prime contractor is responsible 
for all aspects of depot 
sustainment utilizing 
only government buildings and 
government 
employees (i.e. providing ~50% 
of manpower, ~75% of tools and 
test equipment, supply and 
logistics support). Additionally, 
recommend timeline for support 
to be phased out and transitioned 
to alternative 1 full-organic.  
 

The final BCA report shall be developed in accordance with the latest version of the DoD 
Product Support BCA Guidebook and DoDI 5000.91, Product Support Management for the 
Adaptive Acquisition Framework, DAFI63-101/20-101 - Integrated Life Cycle Management. 
Additionally, information and/or recommendations that utilize government equipment must 
comply with DAFMAN 23-119 - Government Furnished Property guidance. 
The analysis for each alternative must include a detailed Life-Cycle Cost (LCC) estimate, a 
qualitative and quantitative benefit analysis against Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) like 
Materiel Availability, and a thorough risk and sensitivity analysis.   
4.0 Requested Information 
4.1 Interested parties are requested to submit a capabilities statement that addresses the following 
areas. Please limit your response to no more than 15 pages. 
4.1.1 Corporate Experience:  
• Provide a brief company overview, including CAGE code, business size, and 
socioeconomic status under the referenced NAICS codes.  
• Describe your company's experience in conducting Product Support BCAs for 
major DoD weapon systems, particularly for large airframes or complex 
Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and 
Reconnaissance (C4ISR) systems. Please provide at least two specific examples 
from the past five years.  
• Detail your experience with analyzing and modeling different sustainment 
strategies, including organic, CLS, and hybrid/PBL constructs.  
4.1.2 Technical Approach & Capabilities:  
• Outline your proposed methodology for developing the E-7A BCA, specifically 
addressing how you would structure the analysis of the three required 
alternatives.  
• Describe the analytical tools, cost models, and data sources you would employ to 
conduct the LCC, risk, and benefit analyses.  
• Describe your corporate capabilities for accessing and analyzing technical data, 
maintenance records, and supply chain information for a military weapon system.  
• Respondents should be able to provide information for fleet size ranging from two 
to twenty-six aircraft. 
4.1.3 Personnel Qualifications:  
• Describe the qualifications, certifications, and experience of the key personnel 
who would be assigned to this project (e.g., Program Manager, Lead Analyst). Do 
not provide resumes.  

4.1.4 Cost and Schedule:  
• Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate to complete the BCA 
as described in Section 3.  
• Provide an estimated timeline for completion of the BCA from the date of 
contract award.  
4.1.5 Government Requirements:  
• Identify any information required from the government to complete BCA such 
as phased inspection requirements, calendar date and/or flight hour-based 
maintenance requirements, facilities, tools, test equipment, 
and/or trained personnel.  
 
5.0 Submission Instructions 
5.1 Submissions are due no later than the response date and time specified in Section 1.0.  
5.2 Submissions shall be in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format and sent 
electronically. Submissions are due no later than 11 May 2026, 5:00 PM EST and submitted 
via e-mail only to richard.axtell.2@us.af.mil gregory.mackessy.1@us.af.mil  
5.3 The subject line of the email shall read: "Response to RFI-E7A-BCA-2026 - [Your Company 
Name]". 
5.4 Proprietary information, if any, should be clearly marked. To aid the Government, please 
segregate proprietary information. 
6.0 Industry Discussions  
E-7A Wedgetail representatives may or may not choose to meet with potential offerors. Such 
discussions would only be intended to get further clarification of a respondent’s ability to 
perform the Product Support BCA.  
7.0 Questions  
Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by email to the Contracting 
POCs (richard.axtell.2@us.af.mil and gregory.mackessy.1@us.af.mil). Verbal questions will 
NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by email; accordingly, questions shall NOT 
contain proprietary or classified information. The Government does not guarantee that questions 
received after 11 May 2026 will be answered. 
 
 
 
 

8.0 Summary  
This RFI is issued solely to identify sources and information that can aid in the completion of a 
Product Support BCA. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not 
binding on the Government. The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any of the 
items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as 
authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All 
submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

Remaining Items – Technical Assistance and Coordination Outcomes Database

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

BACKGROUND

The three programs within the existing Remaining Items (RI) Technical Assistance and Coordination Outcomes (TACO) database (RI-TACOd) are the National Flood Risk Management Program (NFRMP), Floodplain Management Services (FPMS), and the Planning Assistance to States (PAS) programs. The RI-TACOd was developed in 2022 and directly supports these three programs.  The tool serves as the primary mechanism to gather and record project/study proposals for the NFRMP, FPMS, and PAS programs. This includes collecting proposals, ranking/prioritizing for eligibility, selecting for funding, tracking and reporting progress, and project closeout.  The database resides within the Amazon Web Services (AWS) GOV cloud, which is managed by USACE’s Civil Works Business Intelligence (CWBI) program.  RI-TACOd uses AWS cloud-native tools and open-source technical solutions.  The AWS tools and scripts provide users with the means to submit their information, and program managers with the ability to manage and evaluate the process throughout its lifecycle.  With RI-TACOd already deployed, USACE has identified operation and maintenance (O&M) tasks that are necessary for the database to continue to thrive, as well as new development tasks to help advance the tool to its next phase of existence. 

SCOPE

This task order is designed to provide Contractor support to the Government for maintenance and modernization of RI-TACOd. Activities within major task areas will be evaluated and prioritized by the NFRMP/FPMS/PAS program managers (referenced as the Project Delivery Team [PDT] within this PWS) in consultation with the Contractor. Activities will reflect program requirements, user issues, and available resource levels. Several major task areas are to be managed through this delivery order. The task areas are described in Section 4. 

A description of general tasks includes the following:

General database development, assistance, and maintenance for DynamoDB and/or PostgreSQL databases.  

Make changes to database schema as needed to match any changes to the fields (name changes or additions).

Keep changelog of fields that renamed or added over time.

General assistance, and maintenance with web-based data entry interfaces and report generation.  The current interface uses ReactJS. 

General assistance in interfacing with customers and ensuring the Data Entry and Reporting system remains operational.  

Data must be made easily accessible to USACE for use in reporting tools such as Power BI,   A Representational State Transfer (REST) web service should be developed or a direct connection to the data accessible in Power BI should be made available.   Full instructions should be provided for end users to create a connection. General assistance with development of data services to ensure program data can be used within existing USACE tools (ex. Microsoft PowerBI). 

Develop a REST web service endpoint that provides geographic data in a GeoJSON format for use in ArcGIS Portal web maps.

General assistance to program managers in multiple business areas; this may include compiling reports for the managers, attending meetings, and presenting at meetings. 

Delivering training to users, database administrators, program managers, and others on how to enter data and pull reports once the new tool is operational.

Maintaining and enhancing system documentation.

Coordinate with CWBI PMO to maintain cybersecurity compliance, risk management framework documentation, and remediating vulnerabilities.

USACE access approvals and associated paperwork must be completed by Contractor personnel within 10-business days from notice to proceed and/or within 10 business days of notification and instructions from the Government.  As new staff join the team the development of new AWS capability to support RI-TACOd will be performed using Contractor assets.  More specifically, the Contractor will utilize the GovDEV environment for development of code. Any code or application passed to the Government will be hosted on the test/demonstration server for USACE Program Manger review and approval prior to being deployed by USACE resources with virtual technical assistance of deploying the components from the Contractor.  Ideally the Contractor will use continuous integration / continuous delivery pipeline with full infrastructure as code model to allow frequent automated deployments using Agile processes. The Government will host the testing and production cloud-based servers on the CWBI cloud environment. The Contractor will provide draft deliverables to the Government at the prescribed milestones and be available to the Government for any technical assistance needed to complete the loading of code in the test and production environments.  All code and deliverables developed are the property of USACE. All code must be maintained in CWBI's GitHub repository to ensure it can be scanned by CWBI's Information System Security Office. This team would also be responsible for responding to any findings from those scans.

The Contractor shall provide appropriate oversight and Project Management for every task in this PWS to ensure consistent oversight and coordination. Activities will reflect program requirements, user issues, and available resource levels. For the duration of this contract every month and when a need arises, the PDT in consultation with the Contractor, will evaluate and prioritize specific activities to be accomplished within each of the major task areas. Additional requests for updates and enhancements will be provided to the Contractor from the USACE Program Managers (PgMs)/Contracting Office Representative (COR) (both will be included on each request for situational awareness). These new requests will be addressed by the Contractor in the normally scheduled meetings or as necessary. 

The Contractor will work with the PDT to ensure technical accuracy, clarity and appropriateness of key software and documentations while balancing project tasks, deadlines, and on-time deliverables. 

The Contractor’s personnel must demonstrate the capability and appropriate experience to successfully perform a project of this scope and magnitude. The Contractor’s personnel should be familiar with the USACE Civil Works (CW) Program, and knowledge of the CW NFRMP, FPMS, and PAS missions or similar missions is beneficial but not required. The Contractor shall have extensive technical knowledge of programming in database and web-based data entry and reporting solutions to make the necessary revisions to the relevant systems. In addition to these general skills and experience, the Contractor should also possess the following:

Knowledge and experience in developing, maintaining and documenting changes to a relational database operated from a Government data center on Amazon Web Services (AWS cloud). 

Knowledge and experience of data entry and options to increase automation and efficiency.

Knowledge and experience with documenting data systems and processes and creating reports for increased efficiency.

Knowledge and experience in optimizing the performance of existing relational database applications, including procedures, functions, etc.

Knowledge and experience with creating Representational State Transfer (RESTful) services utilizing common data dissemination formats.

Knowledge and experience with making websites 508 compliant.

Knowledge of database design with respect to user experience to enable a design that maximizes efficient data entry and minimizes user data entry errors.

Maintain a clean, intuitive, and logical layout that is easy for users to navigate.

Use a consistent and accessible design for all text, colors, and interactive elements.

Knowledge and experience preparing geospatial services.

Knowledge and experience delivering solutions that align with Agile methodology.

As the Contractor updates their staffing plan an update will be provided to the PDT to ensure the requirements of this PWS are continuing to be met. An updated QA/QC plan with the updated staffing plan may be requested. 

In compliance with DoDI 8500.01 (2014) section 3.c.2, DoDI 8510.01 (2016) section 3.d, and USACE ER 25-1-112 (2014) section 7.1.3; all information systems (IS) and platform information technology (PIT) systems developed and/or supported under this contract shall comply with all Department of War (DoW), DISA, Army, and USACE cybersecurity and information technology (IT) requirements. This includes IS/PIT compliance with DISA security technical implementation guides (STIG) and being categorized IAW CNSSI 1253 using security controls developed IAW the risk management framework (NIST SP 800-53). STIG compliance shall include but is not limited to most current version of the DISA published Application Security and Development STIG and the internet access point (IAP) demilitarized zone (DMZ) STIG. Further, the Contractor shall comply with DFARS clause 252.204-7012 (Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting) and implement NIST SP 800-171 requirements to protect covered defense information / controlled unclassified information.

General REQUIREMENTs

The following sub-sections provide details of various general requirements for this effort.

Non-Personal Services

The Contractor shall provide strictly non-personal services and contractor employees are not subject to direct supervision and control by the Government.  The Contractor shall advise and assist the Government but shall not make final decisions or certifications on behalf of the Government nor perform any inherently governmental functions.  The Contractor and its employees shall not represent the Government nor appear to represent the Government in performance of these contract services.  Contractor personnel shall clearly identify themselves as contractor employees in all interactions during contract performance.

Place of Performance

All work will be performed at the Contractor’s site.  

Period of Performance

The period of performance includes base tasks with a 12-month period of performance, and several option tasks with a 12-month period of performance from date of award of the option.

Materials

All materials, minus expendable supplies, purchased by the Contractor with funds from this contract and used under this contract, become, and remain the property of the Government.

All developed code will become property of the Government.

Travel

The Contractor shall attend a post-award meeting as detailed in Task 1A. The COR will coordinate with the Contractor to schedule the orientation The contractor shall provide services necessary to plan and schedule travel and travel will be reimbursed at actual cost in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulation and the limitations set forth in Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO FAR) 31.205-46, Travel Costs. The appropriate Government Official, Quality Assurance Personnel or Contracting Officer will approve travel. All invoices for travel shall be accompanied by supporting receipts. The Contractor shall not assess profit or fee against other direct costs and/or travel. Other than post-award meeting, there is no travel required for this contract. The Contractor shall be equipped to communicate and collaborate virtually with strong facilitation skills and necessary support tools.

Data Storage, Rights, and Ownership

The Contractor shall physically maintain all data solely on equipment located within the legal jurisdiction of the United States IAW DFARS 239.7602-2(b).  All data, including but not limited to documents, administrative data, support data, and billing data, transmitted via the system or maintained in the system must reside in data processing and storage equipment located in the United States or in data processing and storage equipment of which the operation and maintenance are subject only to the laws of the United States. Data transmitted must only be subject to disclosure pursuant to U.S. Federal law and not the laws of any other jurisdiction or foreign nation. All DoW information/data placed or created by DoW users in a Cloud Service Provider’s (CSP) Cloud Service Offering (CSO) is owned by the DoW, the Mission Owner, and/or their Information Owner. The CSP has no rights to the DoW’s information/data. For more information on data storage, data rights, and data ownership requirements refer to Section 5.2, Legal Considerations, in the DoW Cloud Computing Security Reference Guide (SRG).

The Government shall retain unlimited rights to all development and automation performed and all data, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) or Configuration as Code (CaC) or processes created under this contract. This would not include code, processes, or automation that USACE might subscribe to that are commercially available under Commercial Use Rights and/or Government Purpose Rights.

NOTICE OF INTENT to Sole Source 
 
1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: NIMH26000869 
 
TITLE: LMP744 in Recurrent Glioblastomas 
 
2. CLASSIFICATION CODE:R499 – SCIENTIFIC CONSULTING SERVICES 
 
NAICS CODE: 541715 – Research and Development in Physical, Engineering, and 
Life Sciences. 
 
3. RESPONSE DATE: April 15, 2026, at 12:00 PM EST 
 
4. PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: 
Joe Kennedy 
Joseph.kennedy@nih.gov 
Phone: 262-391-7630 
 
5. DESCRIPTION: 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. 
 
THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) 
SYNOPSIS TO AWARD A CONTRACT WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR 
OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME).  
 
The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) intends to 
negotiate on a sole source basis with Emmes, for a base and five (5) option 
years. 
 
NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE 
and SET ASIDE STATUS 
 
The intended procurement is classified under NAICS code 541715 – Research 
and Development in Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences with a Size Standard 
of 1000 employees.  
 
This intended procurement will be a small business set-aside requirement.  
 
REGULATORY AUTHORITY  
This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Part 13—Simplified Acquisition Procedures. Contracts 
awarded using FAR Part 13—Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from 
the requirements of FAR Part 6—Competition Requirements. FAR Subpart 
13.106-1 (b) Soliciting from a single source provides that: For purchases not 
exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, Contracting Officers may solicit 
from one source IF the contracting officer determines that the circumstances of 
the contract action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, 

exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name OR industrial mobilization). 
 
The resultant contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses in effect 
through the Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) Number 2026-01, dated March 
13, 2026.  
 
DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT 
 
Purchase Description 
 
Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall 
furnish all the necessary services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and 
facilities, not otherwise provided by the Government as needed to perform 
the Statement of Work below: data collection, data abstraction, data 
identification, data validation, communication among clinical team, and 
understanding of clinical research protocol. 
 
Specific Requirements 
 
Clinical monitoring services will be responsible for overseeing clinical research 
efforts away from direct patient care. Detailed clinical monitoring will ensure 
accurate data abstraction, validation, and reporting. The place of performance will 
be a combination of onsite at the National Institutes of Health campus in 
Bethesda, Maryland and remote work 
  Salient Characteristics: 
 
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate progression-free and overall survival in 
participants with recurrent glioblastoma receiving LMP744 compared to historic 
controls. We will also directly compare molecular and metabolic profiles of 
tissue, CSF, and plasma pre- and postexposure to LMP744 to determine 
pharmacologic responses to the drug in this patient population. We will also 
correlate pre- and post-exposure molecular and metabolic profiles with clinical 
response and outcome, to determine which molecular and metabolic features are 
predictive of drug response. The latter information will be critical for the design 
of phase III clinical trials involving LMP744. Finally, we will evaluate the safety 
of LMP744 in patients with recurrent glioblastoma through continuous, objective 
monitoring. This is the first clinical trial to investigate the role of the novel 
indenoisoquinolone, CMYC/TOPOISOMERASE 1 inhibitor LMP744 in 
participants diagnosed with recurrent glioblastoma. Results from this study will 
provide objective assessment of the pharmacologic response to the drug and 
provide an initial assessment of efficacy when compared to historical controls. 
Our goal is to address the urgent need for effective therapies for patients with 
recurrent glioblastoma. Clinical trial monitoring of each enrolled patient (40 total) 
will be required for accutae assessment of safety for enrolled patients and future 
patients on study.  

 
Period of Performance 
 
The proposed period of performance shall be base plus 4 option years. 
 
Base: 5/1/26 – 4/30/27 
 
Level of Effort 
 
Clinical monitoring – 1634 hours total estimate over 5 years 
  
Government Responsibilities 
 
Clinical monitoring services will require access to government CTDB database 
reports. No requirement to access government facilities or equipment. No 
restrictions noted for holidays or other times.  
 
Reporting Requirements 
 
N/A 
 
OTHER CONSIDERARTIONS: 
 
Data Rights 
 
Data abstraction will be required for these requested services. Data will be abstracted 
from patient database reports. Collaboration with the clinical team as well as 
attendance of clinical research team meetings and individual meetings with PIs 
will be required for data review and protocol compliance. Clinical monitoring 
services will also require identification of missing source documents and requests 
of these from the research team 
 
Section 508—Electronic and Information Technology Standards 
 
Contracting services will be not required to procure, maintain and use electronic and 
information technology 
  
Confidentiality of Information: 
 
Contracting services will have access to clinical database reports for 
assessments. Data generated is not confidential - reporting to the public will 
include deidentified data. The contracting services will handle data/information 
prior to publication with discretion. 
 
(INCLUDING BRAND-NAME) DETERMINATION 
 
The determination by the Government to award a contract without providing for 
full and open competition is based upon the market research conducted. 
Specifically, Emmes, is the only vendor in the marketplace that can provide the 

services required by the National Institute of Health. 
 
The intended source is: 
 
 
Emmes Company, LLC 
401 N. Washington Street, Suite 700 
Rockville, MD 20850 
 
The essential characteristics of the clinical data management services that limit 
the availability to a sole source are sensitive clinical data abstraction, contracting 
service options and uniqueness of clinical trial discretion. Only this suggested 
source can furnish the requirements, to the exclusion of other sources, because 
current clinical trial approvals with readiness for patient enrollment of deadly 
brain cancer treatment.  
 
CLOSING STATEMENT 
 
THIS SYNOPSIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, 
interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to this notice.  
 
A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon 
responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible 
sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be 
considered by the agency. The information received will normally be considered solely 
for the purpose of determining whether to proceed on a non-competitive basis or to 
conduct competitive procurement.  
 
Responses to this notice shall contain sufficient information to establish the interested 
parties' bona-fide capabilities for fulfilling the requirement and include: unit price, list 
price, shipping and handling costs, the delivery period after contract award, the prompt 
payment discount terms, the F.O.B. Point (Destination or Origin), the Unique Entity ID 
UEI), the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), and the certification of business size. 
 
Responses must include the place of manufacturing (i.e. address if supply/equipment is 
a domestic end product and includes country of manufacture).  All offerors must have an 
active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) www.sam.gov. 
 
All responses must be received by the closing date and time of this announcement and 
must reference the solicitation number, NIMH26000869.  
 
Responses must be submitted electronically to Joe Kennedy, Contract Specialist, at 
joseph.kennedy@nih.gov   
 
U.S. Mail and fax responses will not be accepted.

Request for Information
DARPA-SN-26-51
Low Cost, Manufacturable Counter-Air Missile Propulsion
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
Tactical Technology Office
Responses due 22 April 2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).
This Request for Information (RFI) from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency 
(DARPA)’s Tactical Technology Office (TTO) seeks to improve its understanding of the 
U.S. industry and supplier base for rocket propulsion technologies that can enable the 
development and production of low-cost missiles at speed and scale.
Responses to this RFI will be used to inform DARPA programs on emerging weapons 
technologies and suppliers that could play a role in the development of low cost, highly 
manufacturable missiles.
Intellectual or other privileged or proprietary information contained in responses to this RFI 
will not be distributed outside of the U.S. Government. In the event that a new DARPA 
program is developed in response to this RFI and a solicitation is issued, no intellectual or 
other proprietary information received in response to this RFI will be divulged to agencies 
outside the U.S. Government.
BACKGROUND:
DARPA is seeking to revolutionize weapons development by dramatically shrinking the 
time it takes to produce today’s systems. One proposed strategy inverts the traditional 
process by prioritizing manufacturability from the outset, allowing the weapon’s ultimate 
capabilities to be determined by what can be produced quickly and efficiently at mass 
scale. An important area of focus for this initiative is the production of propulsion 
systems, which are a notorious bottleneck in missile manufacturing. DARPA is actively 
scouting breakthrough technologies capable of compressing this production timeline from 
months to days and potentially hours.
DESCRIPTION:
This RFI seeks information on state-of-the-art development and manufacturing processes 
for missile propulsion systems, leveraging advanced propulsion prototyping, manufacturing, 
and testing. This RFI will also be used to identify industry partners that can assist in rapid 
prototyping, specifically as it applies to missile propulsion development. 

DARPA-SN-26-51
2
REQUESTED INFORMATION: 
DARPA is interested in responses that must address all of the following technical areas:
1. Advanced, high performance missile propulsion technologies and rapid 
manufacturing and production approaches.
2. Rapid propulsion system prototyping technologies and approaches for rapid 
design iteration. 
3. Anticipated propulsion system performance based on proposed rapid production 
approaches.
SUBMISSION FORMAT:
Attachment 2 contains a format template for responses to this RFI.
General Guidelines: 
Respondents to this special notice are encouraged to be as succinct as possible, 
while also providing actionable insight.
All submissions must be written in English.
White papers shall not exceed seven (7) single-sided written pages using 11-point 
font with 1” margins all around. Font no smaller than 10-point may be used for 
figures, tables, and charts. 
Electronic submittal shall be in Microsoft Word or PDF format. 
All documents submitted must be clearly labeled with the DARPA special notice 
number (DARPA-SN-26-51), respondent organization, and white paper title.
To the maximum extent possible, respondents are encouraged to send non-
proprietary information. 
oRespondents are responsible for clearly identifying proprietary 
information. Submissions containing proprietary information must have 
the cover page and each page containing such information clearly marked 
with a label such as “Proprietary” or “Company Proprietary.” NOTE: 
“Confidential” is a classification marking used to control the 
dissemination of U.S. Government National Security Information as 
dictated in Executive Order 13526 and should not be used to identify 
proprietary business information.
Do not include elaborate brochures or marketing materials; only include 
information relevant to the areas identified above.
Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the response is permitted 
and counted towards page count.
Send unclassified submissions to DARPA-SN-26-51@darpa.mil. DO NOT 
SUBMIT CLASSIFIED INFORMATION TO THIS ADDRESS. Please see 
Attachment 1 - Security to this notice for instructions on submitting classified 
information.

3

Submissions sent through other mediums, channels, or after the prescribed 
deadline will not be considered. Early responses are encouraged.

PROGRAM SECURITY

Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Controlled Technical Information (CTI) on Non-DoD Information Systems

For unclassified white papers containing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), applicants will ensure personnel and information systems processing CUI security requirements are in place.

If an unclassified submission contains CUI or the suspicion of such, as defined by Executive Order 13556 and 32 CFR Part 2002, the information must be appropriately and conspicuously marked CUI in accordance with DoDI 5200.48. Identification of what is CUI or higher in reference to air-to-air missile concepts should be clearly detailed within your source security classification guide (SCG) or Controlled Unclassified Information Guide (CUIG).

Those submitting white papers involving the pursuit and protection of DARPA information designated as CUI must have an information system authorized to process CUI information IAW NIST SP 800-171 and DoDI 8582.01.

Further information on CUI identification, marking, protecting and control, to include processing on Non-DoD Information Systems, is incorporated herein and can be found at https://www.darpa.mil/about/offices/contracts-management/proposer-general-terms#cui.

Classified Submissions 

For classified white paper submissions, applicants will ensure all industrial, personnel, and information systems processing security requirements are in place and at the appropriate level (e.g., Facility Clearance Level (FCL)), and that Automated Information Security (AIS), Certification and Accreditation (C&A), and any Foreign Ownership Control and Influence (FOCI) issues are mitigated prior to submission. Additional information on these subjects can be found at https://www.dcsa.mil/.

	(a)	Classified Markings

At this time, DARPA anticipates that white papers submitted in response to this SN may involve access to classified information. Classified submissions shall be transmitted and marked in accordance with the security classification guidance referenced and sourced from your governing Security Classification Guide (SCG).  This SCG must be provided to the DARPA Program Security Representative for review along with written authorization for the use of classified information in response to this Request for Information from the Office of Primary Responsibility.

If a submission contains Classified National Security Information or the suspicion of such, as defined by Executive Order 13526, the information must be appropriately and conspicuously marked with the classification level and declassification date. Classification must be detailed equal to the level that the sourced SCG dictates. Submissions requiring DARPA to make a final classification determination shall be marked as follows: 

“CLASSIFICATION DETERMINATION PENDING. Final review by the DARPA PSR.  ____________________(insert the recommended classification level, e.g., Top Secret, Secret or Confidential)”

Submissions containing both classified information and CUI must be appropriately and conspicuously marked with the proposed classification level as well as ensuring CUI is marked in accordance with DoDI 5200.48.

	(b)  Classified Submission Requirements and Procedures

Those choosing to submit classified information from other collateral classified sources (i.e., sources other than DARPA) must ensure (1) they have permission from an authorized individual at the cognizant Government agency (e.g., Contracting Officer, Program Manager); (2) the proposal is marked in accordance with the source Security Classification Guide (SCG) from which the material is derived; and (3) the source SCG is submitted along with the proposal.

When a white paper includes a classified portion, and when able according to security guidelines, we ask that an e-mail be sent to DARPA-SN-26-51@darpa.mil as notification that there is a classified portion to the submission. When submitting classified white papers, digital submissions are preferred (email or CD-ROM) and will be accepted via appropriate channels. Pre-coordinate transmission by sending an unclassified e-mail to mailto:DARPA-SN-26-51@darpa.mil.  Submissions containing the classified portion of the white paper should be submitted as a single searchable Adobe PDF file. A single hard copy may be submitted, if desired, in accordance with the instructions outlined below. 

	(c) Both Classified and Unclassified Submissions 

For a white paper that includes both classified and unclassified information, they may be separated into an unclassified portion and a classified portion. The white paper should include as much information as possible in the unclassified portion and use the classified portion ONLY for classified information. The unclassified portion can be submitted to DARPA-SN-26-51@darpa.mil. The classified portion must be provided separately, according to the instructions outlined in the ‘Classified Submission Requirements and Procedures’ section above.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT  
 
PRE-DEMOLITION SURVEY  
 
VARIOUS BUILDINGS  
NASA AMES Research Center, CA 
San Francisco, CA 
 
Revision 0
