1.0  GENERAL STATEMENT OF SERVICES 
 
1.1 Introduction and Purpose. NASA has tasked the US Army Corps of Engineers Engineering 
and Support Center, Huntsville, to initiate a Facility Reduction requirement at the AMES 
research center in San Francisco, CA. Buildings are considered excess and will be demolished. 
The purpose of this contract is to procure Pre-demolition surveys according to the requirements 
set forth in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
1.2 Site Description and Location. AMES Research Center, 64 Facilities at Moffett Blvd, 
Mountain View, CA 94035. 
1.3 Security Requirements .  The Contractor shall be required to comply with all Installation 
entrance and security requirements.  The Contractor shall be responsible for assuring that all 
employees meet the access requirements of the Installation prior to the execution of work action 
on the Installation.   The Contractor will be required to present identification for base access 
installation requirements. 
1.3.1.1 AT Level I Training.  All contractor employees, including subcontractor employees, 
requiring access to Federally controlled facility or Military I nstallations, facilities, controlled 
access areas, or require network access, shall complete AT Level I awareness training within 30 
calendar days after contract start date or effective date of incorporation of this requirement into the 
contract, whichever  is applicable. Upon request, the contractor shall submit certificates of 
completion for each affected contractor employee and subcontractor employee, to the COR or to 
the contracting officer (if a COR is not assigned), within 5 calendar days after completion of 
training by all employees and subcontractor personnel. AT Level I awareness training is available 
at the following website: http://jko.jten.mil/courses/atl1/launch.html; or it can be provided by the 
RA ATO in presentation form which will be documented via memorandum. 
1.3.1.2 Access and General Protection/Security Policy and Procedures.  All contractors and all 
associated sub-contractors employees shall comply with applicable installation, facility and area 
commander installation/facility access and local security policies and procedures (provided by 
government representative). The contractor shall also provide all information required for 
background checks to meet installation/facility access requirements to be accomplished by 
installation Provost Marshal Office, Director of Emergency Services or Security Office. Contractor 
workforce must comply with all personal identity verification requirements (FAR clause 52.204 -

Page 2 of 45 
 
 
9, Personal Identity Verification of Contractor Personnel) as directed by DOD, HQDA and/or local 
policy. In addition to the changes otherwise authorized by the changes clause of this contract, 
should the Force Protection Condition (FPCON) or Health Protection Condition (HPCON) at any 
installation or facility change, the Government may require changes in contractor security matters 
or processes. 
1.3.1.2b For contractors who do not require a CAC but  do require access to a DoD facility or 
installation. Contractor and all associated sub -contractors employees shall comply with 
adjudication standards and procedures using the National Crime Information Center Interstate 
Identification Index (NCIC-III) and Terrorist Screening Database (TSDB) (Army Directive 2014-
05 / AR 190 -13), applicable installation, facility and area commander installation/facility access 
and local security policies and procedures (pr ovided by government representative, as NCIC and 
TSDB are available), or, at OCONUS locations, in accordance with status of forces agreements 
and other theater regulations. 
1.3.1.3 Suspicious Activity Reporting Training (e.g. iWATCH, CorpsWatch, or See Something, 
Say Something) . Military Instillations have suspicious activity reporting requirement. Report 
suspicious activities to appropriate law enforcement agencies. Infringement of the base policy may 
result in a fine or incarceration. 
1.3.1.5 Contractors w ill be escorted in areas where they may be exposed to classified and/or 
sensitive materials and/or sensitive or restricted areas.  All contract employees, including 
subcontractor employees who are not in possession of the appropriate security clearance or access 
privileges, will be escorted in areas where they may be exposed to classified and/or sensitive 
materials and/or sensitive or restricted areas. 
1.3.1.6 Pre-screen candidates using E-Verify Program. The Contractor must pre-screen Candidates 
using the E -verify Program (http://www.uscis.gov/e -verify) website to meet the established 
employment eligibility requirements. The Vendor must ensure that the Candidate has two valid 
forms of Government issued identification prior to enrollment to ensure the correct information is 
entered into the E-verify system. An initial list of verified/eligible Candidates must be provided to 
the COR no later than 3 business days after the initial contract award. 
1.4 Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Requirements . The scope of this effort 
requires the contractor and/or subcontractor information system to process, store, or transmit FCI 
or CUI, and requires the contractor and/or subcontractor to comply with CMMC requirements. The 
Contractor shall have and maintain for the duration of this contract, order, or agreement a current 
CMMC status at the following CMMC level, or higher:  CMMC Level 2 (Self) for all information 
systems used in performance of th e contract, task order, or delivery order that process, store, or 
transmit FCI or CUI.  See DFARS 252.204-7021 “Contractor Compliance With the Cybersecurity 
Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements”, for the definitions, requirements, reporting, 
and subcontract information for this contract/order/agreement” 
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE - The objective of this Performance Work Statement is to plan and complete 
the environmental sampling of facilities at the installation.  The structures of concern are listed in 
Table I.  The sampling will determine ACM and ORM materials and complete a Waste Stream 

Page 3 of 45 
 
 
Analysis for RCRA 8 metals, lead-based paint (LBP) and PCB’s-in-paint for those parts of the 
structure currently identified as potentially having any painted components.  Following 
sampling, the Contractor shall be able to completely quantify the environmental contamination 
present and the methods required to remove and dispose of said contamination in a safe manner.  
All sampling shall be planned and performed in accordance with Federal, State, and local 
regulations for the installation.  All recommendations for follow-on actions shall also be in 
accordance with Federal, State, and local regulations.  Laboratory testing and analysis shall be 
completed within the workdays identified in table two following the respective site sampling 
field activity completion. The results of the site investigation and sampling effort will be 
provided in an individual Pre-Demolition Assessment Report for the installation that will be 
submitted within the workdays identified in table two following the receipt of sample results.  
The intent of this contract effort is to provide comprehensive sampling for all ACM/ORM 
materials to include the facility exterior, roof, basement/crawl spaces, etc. The Contractor shall 
make every reasonable effort to access these areas when present in each facility. The Report will 
specifically address any areas within given structures that were not accessible during the survey 
and state the size of the area not accessed, and current or immediate previous use of the area not 
sampled.  
 
3.0  DETAILED  DESCRIPTION  OF  SERVICES 
3.1 General Requirements.  All work performed by the Contractor shall be designed and 
implemented in a manner which conforms to this PWS and all applicable Federal, State, and 
local requirements. The Contractor shall present a complete description of the planning and 
assessment process as applied to the subject facilities. 
 
3.2 (Task 1) Pre-Demolition Assessments. 
3.2.1 (Task 1.1) Accident Prevention Plan and Sampling Plan. No more than the workdays 
identified in table two after award, the Contractor shall prepare and submit an Accident 
Prevention Plan (APP), including the Sampling Plan.  No Site Investigation shall be performed 
until the APP has been reviewed and approved by the Government.  The APP must include 
recommendations for utilization of Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE) as required to ensure 
worker protection to the extent required by law or recommended as prudent and appropriate by 
the contractor.  The types and numbers of samples per material type shall be generally described, 
as well as the process for collecting and securing the samples.  The laboratory used for analysis 
shall be identified.  Any special conditions required by State or Commonwealth regulations shall 
also be noted in the plan. 
 
When the work plan is submitted, please provide a separate submittal consisting of the 
Abbreviated Accident Prevention Plan, Activity Hazard Analysis, and SSHO Qualifications.  
Specific requirements for these safety submittals can be found in Appendix D Safety 
Requirements. 
 
The Site-Safety Health Officer (SSHO) and the Quality Control Manager (QCM) shall always be 
present on- site while field activities are occurring. The SSHO shall comply with all applicable 
safety criteria and shall use their discretion to determine which activities require the SSHO to be 
present, and where the SSHO will be for day-to-day operations. 

Page 4 of 45 
 
 
Government Designated Authority (GDA) for reviewing and accepting all required safety 
submittals is the HNC Safety Office. 
 
The APP and all Activity Hazard Analysis’ (AHAs) shall be reviewed and accepted by the 
Government Safety Office prior to the notice to proceed. The installation or additional stake 
holders may require reviews of the Contractor’s AHAs which shall be accommodated by the 
Contractor. 
 
Reference Appendix D for safety additional requirements/details.

1.0 INTRODUCTION 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
The Contractor shall provide all personnel, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services to 
support the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA), Office of Counterintelligence (SIC) as defined 
in this Task Order (TO) Statement of Work (SOW), except for those items specified as government 
furnished property and services. This SOW describes the non-personal services contract required to 
support the mission of NGA for the Office of Counterintelligence. The Government shall not exercise any 
supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract 
service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor, who is responsible to the Government 
for accountability of Contractor and subcontractor personnel. 
1.1 BACKGROUND 
The Department of War is responsible for providing the most advanced technical security and 
countermeasures capabilities to protect sensitive facilities, information, and communications from 
unauthorized access or exploitation. The DOW Technical Security program is responsible for detecting, 
deterring, and neutralizing technical surveillance threats directed against DOW facilities and personnel. 
The Technical Security program implements DOW and Intelligence Community (IC) direction to 
integrate, enhance, and optimize technical security and signals countermeasures programs in support of 
the protection of national intelligence, sources, and methods, including sensitive compartmented 
information, and the facilities, systems, and networks that house them. 
1.2 SCOPE 
Except for those items specified as government furnished property and services, the contractor shall 
provide technical security support services to the Office of Counterintelligence necessary to complete 
associated tasks and responsibilities in the following functional areas outlined below and defined in this 
SOW: 
• Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM): Pre-Construction Surveys, Emergency Surveys, 
Routine Surveys, In-Place Monitoring 
• Data Engineering: Database design, implementation, and management 
• Software Development: Application design, coding, testing, and maintenance 
• Front-End Development: User interface design and implementation 
• Back-End Development: Server-side logic and API development 
• Technical Security and Signals Countermeasures (TSSC) Analysis: Technical security assessments 
and analysis 
1.3 Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) 
Prime Contractors are hereby informed that an actual and/or perceived OCI may arise in the 
performance of this requirement. This support, as fully described in Section 3.0, Appendix A and 
Appendix B, provides technical security support to DOW. These efforts may include access to existing 
technical security performance contract information and will include supporting all technical security 
areas, including but not limited to analyzing and documenting the following: requirements, existing and 
proposed technical solutions, financial data and estimates as well as any supporting documentation for 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
future technical security services. All personnel assigned to this task order will be required to sign the 
standard Non-Disclosure Agreement. 
Should an OCI arise under this contract, the contractor will be required to notify the Contracting Officer 
immediately and then provide an OCI Mitigation Plan for the Contracting Officer's review and approval 
within 48 hours from time of notification to the CO. 
2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
In addition to the documents listed in this SOW, a list of applicable reference documents is provided for 
reference. See Appendix C. 
3.0 DESCRIPTION OF WORK 
3.1 Security Support Service Requirements 
The contractor shall provide services necessary to complete associated tasks and responsibilities of the 
SOW in the functional areas listed and described below, which is inclusive of Appendix A: Anticipated 
Support Requirements that identify Labor Categories (LCAT) and Skill Levels, and Appendix B: Position 
Descriptions that identify government-defined labor. 
3.1.1 Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM) 
Functional Description: The TSCM functional area refers to the procedures and techniques implemented 
to detect, identify, and neutralize electronic eavesdropping devices or other technical threats that 
compromise the security and confidentiality of sensitive information. This includes: 
• Pre-Construction Surveys: Evaluating plans and designs for new facilities to identify and mitigate 
potential technical security vulnerabilities 
• Emergency Surveys: Responding to suspected technical security breaches or incidents 
• Routine Surveys: Conducting scheduled examinations of facilities to detect unauthorized 
surveillance devices 
• In-Place Monitoring: Continuous monitoring of sensitive areas for unauthorized signals or 
activities 
• The TSCM functional area refers to the procedures and techniques implemented to detect, 
identify, and neutralize electronic eavesdropping devices or other technical threats that 
compromise the security and confidentiality of sensitive information. This area is led by a Senior 
TSCM Lead who ensures team compliance with all TSCM activities and standards. 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Successful detection and neutralization of all unauthorized surveillance devices in NGA facilities 
• Comprehensive documentation of technical vulnerabilities in pre-construction designs with 
specific mitigation recommendations 
• Emergency response to suspected technical security breaches within 24 hours of notification 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Complete and thorough routine surveys conducted according to established periodicity 
• Effective continuous monitoring of sensitive areas with prompt alert response within 
established timeframes 
• Detailed survey reports documenting findings and recommendations delivered within 10 
business days of completion 
• Implementation of effective countermeasures that successfully mitigate identified threats 
• Compliance with ICD 705 and NGA standards for all TSCM activities 
3.1.2 Data Engineering 
Functional Description: The Data Engineering functional area encompasses the design, implementation, 
and management of databases and data pipelines to support TSSC operations and analysis. This 
includes: 
• Database design and optimization for TSSC data collection and analysis 
• Development of data pipelines for processing TSSC data 
• Implementation of data storage solutions for long-term analysis 
• Creation of data models to support analytical requirements 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Optimized database schemas that enhance TSSC data collection and analysis capabilities 
• Secure, efficient data pipelines with robust validation procedures that ensure data integrity 
• Properly implemented data storage solutions compliant with classified environment 
requirements 
• Comprehensive data models that effectively support analytical requirements 
• Documented database architecture that meets security and performance standards 
• Weekly data engineering status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• Data quality reports that demonstrate the effectiveness of data validation procedures 
• Secure integration with existing government systems and databases 
3.1.3 Software Development 
Functional Description: The Software Development functional area covers the design, coding, testing, 
and maintenance of custom software applications to support TSSC operations. This includes: 
• Development of TSSC analysis tools 
• Creation of reporting and visualization applications 
• Implementation of signal processing algorithms 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Integration with existing government systems 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Functional, secure software tools for analyzing TSSC data that meet user requirements 
• Effective algorithms for signal processing and analysis that enhance threat detection capabilities 
• Intuitive visualization tools that enhance understanding of TSSC data 
• Customized reporting interfaces that meet user requirements and streamline workflows 
• Secure integration with existing government systems with proper documentation 
• Weekly software development status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• Thoroughly documented code and technical specifications that facilitate maintenance 
• Applications that successfully pass security testing before deployment 
3.1.4 Front-End Development 
Functional Description: The Front-End Development functional area focuses on creating user interfaces 
for TSSC applications that are intuitive, responsive, and effective. This includes: 
• Design and implementation of user interfaces for TSSC applications 
• Development of interactive data visualization components 
• Creation of responsive web applications for field use 
• Implementation of user authentication and authorization interfaces 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Intuitive user interfaces for TSSC applications that enhance productivity and user satisfaction 
• Interactive data visualization components that effectively display technical security data 
• Responsive web applications optimized for field use by technical security personnel 
• Secure login interfaces with appropriate role-based access controls 
• User interfaces that comply with government accessibility standards 
• Weekly front-end development status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• User interface style guides that ensure consistency across applications 
• Usability testing reports that document user feedback and implemented improvements 
3.1.5 Back-End Development 
Functional Description: The Back-End Development functional area encompasses server-side logic, API 
development, and system integration for TSSC applications. This includes: 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Development of RESTful APIs for TSSC data access 
• Implementation of server-side business logic 
• Integration with government authentication systems 
• Development of automated data processing workflows 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Secure, well-documented APIs for TSSC data access with appropriate authentication controls 
• Robust server-side components with appropriate error handling and logging capabilities 
• Successful integration with government authentication systems 
• Efficient automated data processing workflows that enhance analytical capabilities 
• Server architecture that meets security and performance requirements 
• Weekly back-end development status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• API documentation that facilitates integration with other systems 
• Performance testing reports that demonstrate system efficiency and scalability 
3.1.6 TSSC Analysis 
Functional Description: The TSSC Analysis functional area covers the technical assessment and analysis 
of potential security vulnerabilities and countermeasures. This includes: 
• Analysis of RF signals and electromagnetic emissions 
• Assessment of physical security measures 
• Evaluation of technical security controls 
• Development of countermeasures recommendations 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Accurate identification and characterization of potential threat signals from RF analysis within 
48 hours of signal collection 
• Comprehensive evaluation of physical security controls with documented vulnerabilities 
delivered in standardized assessment reports 
• Thorough assessment of technical security control effectiveness with specific recommendations 
for improvement 
• Identification of gaps in technical security coverage with prioritized remediation 
recommendations 
• Tailored countermeasures recommendations with detailed implementation plans and resource 
requirements 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Cost-benefit analysis for recommended countermeasure options to support decision-making 
• Detailed signal analysis reports delivered within 10 business days of analysis completion 
• Physical security assessment reports with actionable recommendations that comply with ICD 
705 standards 
• Technical security evaluation reports identifying specific vulnerabilities with mitigation 
strategies 
• Quarterly summary reports that track trends and emerging threats to inform proactive security 
planning 
• Annual technical security threat assessments that inform strategic planning and resource 
allocation

ARCHITECT-ENGINEER QUALIFICATIONS OMB Control Number:  9000-0157 
Expiration Date:  1/31/2027
STANDARD FORM 330 (REV. 7/2021) PAGE 1 OF INSTRUCTIONS 
Prescribed by GSA - FAR (48 CFR) 53.236-2(b)
PURPOSE  
 
Federal agencies use this form to obtain information from 
architect-engineer (A-E) firms about their professional 
qualifications.  Federal agencies select firms for A-E contracts on 
the basis of professional qualifications as required by 40 U.S.C. 
chapter 11, Selection of Architects Engineers, and Part 36 of the 
Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).  
 
The Selection of Architects and Engineers statute requires the 
public announcement of requirements for A-E services (with 
some exceptions provided by other statutes), and the selection of 
at least three of the most highly qualified firms based on 
demonstrated competence and professional qualifications 
according to specific criteria published in the announcement.  
The Act then requires the negotiation of a contract at a fair and 
reasonable price starting first with the most highly qualified firm.  
 
The information used to evaluate firms is from this form and other 
sources, including performance evaluations, any additional data 
requested by the agency, and interviews with the most highly 
qualified firms and their references.
GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS  
 
Part I presents the qualifications for a specific contract.  
 
Part II presents the general qualifications of a firm or a specific 
branch office of a firm.  Part II has two uses:  
 
1.  An A-E firm may submit Part II to the appropriate central, 
regional or local office of each Federal agency to be kept on file.  
A public announcement is not required for certain contracts, and 
agencies may use Part II as a basis for selecting at least three of 
the most highly qualified firms for discussions prior to requesting 
submission of Part I.  Firms are encouraged to update Part II on 
file with agency offices, as appropriate, according to FAR Part 
36.  If a firm has branch offices, submit a separate Part II for 
each branch office seeking work.  
 
2.  Prepare a separate Part II for each firm that will be part of 
the team proposed for a specific contract and submitted with Part 
I.  If a firm has branch offices, submit a separate Part II for each 
branch office that has a key role on the team.
INDIVIDUAL AGENCY INSTRUCTIONS 
 
Individual agencies may supplement these instructions.  For 
example, they may limit the number of projects or number of 
pages submitted in Part I in response to a public announcement 
for a particular project.  Carefully comply with any agency 
instructions when preparing and submitting this form.  Be as 
concise as possible and provide only the information requested 
by the agency.
DEFINITIONS 
 
Architect-Engineer Services:  Defined in FAR 2.101.  
 
Branch Office:  A geographically distinct place of business or 
subsidiary office of a firm that has a key role on the team.  
 
Discipline:  Primary technical capabilities of key personnel, as 
evidenced by academic degree, professional registration, 
certification, and/or extensive experience.  
 
Firm:  Defined in FAR 36.102.  
 
Key Personnel:  Individuals who will have major contract 
responsibilities and/or provide unusual or unique expertise.
SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS 
 
Part I - Contract-Specific Qualifications  
 
Section A. Contract Information.  
 
1. Title and Location.  Enter the title and location of the 
contract for which this form is being submitted, exactly as shown 
in the public announcement or agency request.  
 
2. Public Notice Date.  Enter the posted date of the agency's 
notice on the Federal Business Opportunity website 
(FedBizOpps), other form of public announcement or agency 
request for this contract.  
 
3. Solicitation or Project Number.  Enter the agency's 
solicitation  number  and/or  project  number,  if  applicable, 
exactly as shown in the public announcement or agency request 
for this contract. 
 
Section B.  Architect-Engineer Point of Contact.  
 
4-8.  Name, Title, Name of Firm, Telephone Number, Fax 
(Facsimile) Number and E-mail (Electronic Mail) Address. 
Provide information for a representative of the prime contractor 
or joint venture that the agency can contact for additional 
information.
AUTHORIZED FOR LOCAL REPRODUCTION
Paperwork Reduction Act Statement - This information collection meets the requirements of 44 USC § 3507, as amended by section 2 of the Paperwork 
Reduction Act of 1995.  You do not need to answer these questions unless we display a valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number.  
The OMB control number for this collection is 9000-0157.  We estimate that it will take 29 hours (25 hours for part 1 and 4 hours for Part 2) to read the 
instructions, gather the facts, and answer the questions.  Send only comments relating to our time estimate, including suggestions for reducing this 
burden, or any other aspects of this collection of information to:  U.S. General Services Administration, Regulatory Secretariat Division (M1V1CB), 1800 F 
Street, NW, Washington, DC  20405.

Section C.  Proposed Team.  
 
9-11.  Firm Name, Address, and Role in This Contract. 
Provide the contractual relationship, name, full mailing address, 
and a brief description of the role of each firm that will be 
involved in performance of this contract.  List the prime 
contractor or joint venture partners first.  If a firm has branch 
offices, indicate each individual branch office that will have a key 
role on the team.  The named subcontractors and outside 
associates or consultants must be used, and any change must 
be approved by the contracting officer. (See FAR Part 52 Clause 
"Subcontractors and Outside Associates and Consultants 
(Architect-Engineer Services)").  Attach an additional sheet in the 
same format as Section C if needed.  
 
Section D.  Organizational Chart of Proposed Team.  
 
As an attachment after Section C, present an organizational 
chart of the proposed team showing the names and roles of all 
key personnel listed in Section E and the firm they are 
associated with as listed in Section C.  
 
Section E.  Resumes of Key Personnel Proposed for this 
Contract.  
 
Complete this section for each key person who will 
participate in this contract.  Group by firm, with personnel of the 
prime contractor or joint venture partner firms first.  The following 
blocks must be completed for each resume:  
 
12.  Name.  Self-explanatory.  
 
13.  Role in this contract.  Self-explanatory.  
 
14.  Years Experience.  Total years of relevant experience 
(block 14a), and years of relevant experience with current firm, 
but not necessarily the same branch office (block 14b).  
 
15.  Firm Name and Location.  Name, city and state of the 
firm where the person currently works, which must correspond 
with one of the firms (or branch office of a firm, if appropriate)  
listed in Section C.  
 
16.  Education.  Provide  information  on  the highest relevant 
academic degree(s) received.  Indicate the area(s) of 
specialization for each degree.  
 
17.  Current Professional Registration.  Provide information 
on current relevant professional registration(s) in a State or 
possession of the United States, Puerto Rico, or the District of  
Columbia according to FAR Part 36.  
 
18.  Other Professional Qualifications.  Provide information 
on any other professional qualifications relating to this contract, 
such as education, professional registration, publications, 
organizational memberships, certifications, training, awards, and 
foreign language capabilities.
19.  Relevant Projects.  Provide information on up to five 
projects in which the person had a significant role that 
demonstrates the person's capability relevant to her/his proposed 
role in this contract.  These projects do not necessarily have to 
be any of the projects presented in Section F for the project team 
if the person was not involved in any of those projects or the 
person worked on other projects that were more relevant than 
the team projects in Section F.  Use the check box provided to 
indicate if the project was performed with any office of the current 
firm.  If any of the professional services or construction projects 
are not complete, leave Year Completed blank and indicate the 
status in Brief Description and Specific Role (block (3)).  
 
Section F.  Example Projects Which Best Illustrate Proposed 
Team's Qualifications for this Contract.  
 
Select projects where multiple team members worked 
together, if possible, that demonstrate the team's capability to 
perform work similar to that required for this contract.  Complete 
one Section F for each project.  Present ten projects, unless 
otherwise specified by the agency.  Complete the following 
blocks for each project:  
 
20.  Example Project Key Number.  Start with "1" for the first 
project and number consecutively.  
 
21.  Title and Location.  Title and location of project or 
contract.  For an indefinite delivery contract, the location is the 
geographic scope of the contract.  
 
22.  Year Completed.  Enter the year completed of the 
professional services (such as planning, engineering study, 
design, or surveying), and/or the year completed of construction,  
if applicable.  If any of the professional services or the 
construction projects are not complete, leave Year Completed 
blank and indicate the status in Brief Description of Project and 
Relevance to this Contract (block 24).  
 
23a.  Project Owner.  Project owner or user, such as a 
government agency or installation, an institution, a corporation or 
private individual.  
 
23b.  Point of Contact Name.  Provide name of a person 
associated with the project owner or the organization which 
contracted for the professional services, who is very familiar with 
the project and the firm's (or firms') performance.  
 
23c.  Point of Contact Telephone Number.  Self-explanatory.  
 
24.  Brief Description of Project and Relevance to this 
Contract.  Indicate scope, size, cost, principal elements and 
special features of the project.  Discuss the relevance of the 
example project to this contract.  Enter any other information 
requested by the agency for each example project.

Section G.  Key Personnel Participation in Example Projects.  
 
This matrix is intended to graphically depict which key 
personnel identified in Section E worked on the example projects 
listed in Section F.  Complete the following blocks (see example 
below).  
 
26. and 27.  Names of Key Personnel and Role in this

29.  Example Projects Key.  List the key numbers and titles of

Section H.  Additional Information.  
 
30.  Use this section to provide additional information 
specifically requested by the agency or to address selection 
criteria that are not covered by the information provided in 
Sections A-G.  
 
Section I.  Authorized Representative.  
 
31. and 32.  Signature of Authorized Representative and 
Date.  An authorized representative of a joint venture or the 
prime contractor must sign and date the completed form.  
Signing attests that the information provided is current and

Provide a statement (be sure to include the date of approval) that the Mentor Firm has been previously approved under the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program (provide a copy of approval letter, if available) and is still eligible to participate as a Mentor Firm per the requirements set by DFARS Appendix I-102 or identify anticipated schedule to submit a Mentor Application.

Section F:	Mentor Firm Background

Provide a brief summary about the Mentor Firm including a company profile, volume of DoW/Service or Agency contracts, and accomplishments under their Small Business programs.  Indicate whether the Mentor Firm has one or more DoW contracts with an active small business subcontracting plan.

Section G:	Mentor Firm Capacity and Capability

Identify and describe the Mentor Firm's qualifications, capabilities, experience with small business assistance, expertice in related technical areas, proposed facilities and equipment, and capacity for achieving the proposed agreement objectives.

Section H:	Mentor Firm Past Performance

Identify and describe the Mentor Firm’s past performance, if any, in the DoW and Service/Agency Mentor-Protégé program.  Include all past and active Mentor Protégé Agreements and proposed agreements currently being considered (indicate agency).  Identify any past Nunn-Perry awards and/or any significant mentoring accomplishments.

Section I:	Protégé Firm Eligibility

Provide a statement that the Protégé Firm is currently eligible to participate in the DoW Mentor Protégé Program as a “disadvantaged small business concern” (DSB) as defined in Public Law 101-510, Section 831, as amended, pursuant to all of the following criteria below:

(1)  A small business concern as defined in the Small Business Act, 15 U.S.C. 631 et seq., and implementing SBA regulations in Title 13 of the Code of Federal Regulations;

 

(2)  Eligible for the award of Federal contracts;

 

(3)  Not more than the Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard for its primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code;

 

(4)  Not owned or managed by individuals or entities that directly or indirectly have stock options or convertible securities in the Mentor Firm;

(5) 	Is not currently a party to another Mentor Protégé agreement under the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program authority, 10 U.S.C. 2302 note;

(6) 	Has not had another Mentor Protégé agreement under the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program authority, 10 U.S.C. 2302 note; and

 

(7)  At least one of the following:

A small business concern owned and controlled by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals as defined in section 8(d)(3)(C) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(d)(3)(C)).

(B) 	A business entity owned and controlled by an Indian tribe as defined by section 8(a)(13) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(a)(13));

(C) 	A business entity owned and controlled by a Native Hawaiian Organization as defined by section 8(a)(15) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(a)(15));

(D) A qualified organization employing severely disabled individuals operating on a for-profit or nonprofit basis that -

Uses rehabilitative engineering to provide employment opportunities for severely disabled individuals and integrates severely disabled individuals into its workforce;

Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than 20 percent of its total workforce;

Employs each severely disabled individual in its workforce generally on the basis of 40 hours per week; and

Pays not less than the minimum wage prescribed pursuant to section 6 of the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 U.S.C. 206) to those employees who are severely disabled individuals (as defined in section 8501 of title 41, United States Code) or a severely disabled individual (as defined in such section).

(E) A small business concern owned and controlled by women, as defined in section 8(d)(3)(D) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(d)(3)(D));

(F)	A small business concern owned and controlled by service-disabled veterans (SDVOSB) as defined in Section 8(d)(3) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(d)(3));

(G) A qualified HUBZone small business concern (as defined in section 31(b) of the Small Business Act [15 U.S.C. 657a(b)]);

(H)	A small business concern that –

Is a non-traditional defense contractor, as such term is defined in 10 U.S.C. 2302; or

Currently provides goods or services in the private sector that are critical to enhancing the capabilities of the defense supplier base and fulfilling key Department of War needs.

GENERAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

VISN MUSE NX Performance PCS

PRESOLICITATION NOTICE 

Notice of Intent to Sole Source

-NONCOMPETITIVE-

Veterans Integrated Service Network 19 (VISN 19)

VISN MUSE™ NX Performance PCS Sustainment and Support

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 19, intends to award a non-competitive sole source firm fixed price (FFP) contract to GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES, INC. to provide continued sustainment, support and service of MUSE™ NX Performance PCS cardiology software (MUSE) for existing systems at VISN 19 facilities. The requirement includes ensuring that the equipment operates as the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) intended, uninterrupted (95% uptime), in a cost-effective, efficient manner, contributing to the Veterans Administration’s (VA)’s Mission.

MUSE is proprietary and highly specialized and is cardiology’s data management system.  There are no other authorized resellers or distributors of this product/service.   MUSE reads electrocardiograms (ECG)s prior to exams, identifies, analyzes readouts, and predicts emerging heart issues.  This system assists providers to manage cardiac disease and automates orders and billing which eliminates paper processes. 

A maintenance, sustainment and support contract is needed for MUSE. The services required include but are not limited to: technical phone support, corrective and preventative maintenance, bug fixes, and upgrades/patches. These services are used to keep the system working to avoid possible delays in patient care. Technical phone support aids in troubleshooting problems, corrective and preventative maintenance maintain workflow for clinicians, and upgrades prevent the system from becoming vulnerable while on the network. 

The FFP service contract anticipated will have a base period of one (1) year and four (4) 1-year ordering periods of performance.

The estimated period of performance is 9/1/2026 - 8/31/2031.

Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1(b).

The applicable NAICS Code is 541519 and the size standard is $34 Million.

*Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to meet the government’s needs.  

Responses to this Notice of Intent to Sole Source shall be received by 10:00AM (Mountain Time) 4/22/2026. to the Contract Specialist, Christine Jarvis, christine.jarvis@va.gov

If no responses are received, the Contracting Officer will proceed with the sole source requirement to proprietary GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES, INC.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

This intent to sole source announcement is posted for 15 days in accordance with FAR 5.2 - Synopses of Proposed Contract Actions. 

The Department of Veterans Affairs, The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center, Washington DC Office has an acquisition need for continued services and seeks a sole source acquisition strategy. The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center, Washington DC Office intends to modify Contract No. 36C24525P0477 to add an additional position and increase the contract value in accordance with FAR 6.302-1 Only one responsible source will satisfy the agency requirements. 

Background Information/Purpose. 

The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center (hereafter “DC WRIISC”) in Washington, DC is a national post-deployment health resource for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The WRIISC develops and provides post-deployment health expertise to Veterans and their health care providers through clinical programs, education and risk communication, and research.

HOME serves Veterans and their families as the leader and authority on health outcomes of military exposures through science, policy, education, and communication. HOME is a trusted team that Veterans and stakeholders rely on as a definitive source of information on military exposures. 

HOME consists of four interrelated programs, one of which is the WRIISC. The WRIISC thus requires the service expertise of a not-for-profit organization that provides scientific support related to military medicine and veteran health in support of this reorganization to leverage expertise acquired in the prior contract and apply it towards the new duties of these new workforce demands. In addition, WRIISC requires that the organization provides support and administrative capabilities to allow WRIISC staff to maintain their scientific and clinical focus to achieve their goals for Veteran healthcare. 

The organization must have extensive experience managing clinical research in the military/veteran community with expertise in recruiting and hiring research personnel and knowledge of the Washington DC VA Medical Center. Specifically, the WRIISC is interested in maintaining capabilities in the form of staffing of a Health Coach to assist Veterans with making better health choices through lifestyle changes; an Associate Scientific Director, who will support the Research Director and Director at the WRIISC in scientific planning and research portfolio management; and an Epidemiologist with expertise study design and statistical methods.  A Senior Education and Risk Communication Advisor (SERA), a doctorate level medical professional, will contribute strategic expertise in risk communication to enhance HOME outreach. 

Unique Qualifications — 

The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center (WRIISC) in Washington, DC is a national program dedicated to Veterans’ post‑deployment health concerns and unique health care needs. To meet increasing demands associated with the application of the PACT Act (H.R.3967 — 117th Congress) and to support leadership reorganization under the VA’s Health Outcomes Military Exposures (HOME), WRIISC seeks to modify its existing support arrangement. 

This modification adds one Epidemiologist position to serve as the lead for VMOAT operations, providing epidemiological oversight of survey instrument design and validation, exposure data governance, multi‑modal data integration (survey, clinical, biomarker, and administrative), analytic rigor (e.g., allostatic load and exposure mixtures), and regulatory coordination (IRB/HRPP) necessary for national scale.

The Epidemiologist will establish a rapid‑response operational infrastructure for VMOAT, manage QA/UAT cycles to ensure reliable downstream reporting, and translate findings into actionable risk communication and educational outputs for Veterans and providers.

This role preserves continuity with prior work under HJF, enables timely execution of VMOAT within WRIISC’s clinical and research mission, and directly advances HOME’s goals by providing trusted, science‑based evidence on military exposures and health outcomes. No inherently governmental functions are assigned; work will be performed as non‑personal scientific and technical support under Government direction.

Opening this contract to full competition or breaking up work among new vendors would introduce substantial delays, increase total costs, and create redundancies that impede progress on active tasks. Given the contract’s current momentum and the integrated nature of the SOW, HJF remains the only practical and qualified choice to continue execution without interruption. Awarding to HJF under FAR 13.5 preserves cost, schedule, and mission continuity, allowing VHA to meet essential directives under the PACT Act and HOME while advancing research and operational goals efficiently and on time.

Modification information – 

The Government awarded contract no. 36C24525P0477 and determined fair and reasonable pricing prior to award date of April 30,2025. The Government will modify the contract with the current pricing established in the base contract, and the pricing will be subject to no adjustments. The period of performance shall be for the remaining option year 1 through option 4.  Option periods are exercised as needed and are not guaranteed.  The Period of Performance reads as follows:

	

•	Option Year Period 1:			4/30/2026 – 3/29/2027			

•	Option Year Period 2:			4/30/2027 – 3/29/2028			

•	Option Year Period 3:			4/30/2028 – 3/29/2029		

•	Option Year Period 4:			4/30/2029 – 3/29/2030		

For any additional information or questions, please contact the Contracting Officer: Robert O’Keefe Jr. – Robert.okeefejr@va.gov

Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition Bureau of Land Management

FAR 13.106-1(b)(1) Simplified Acquisitions

PR # 0044040825

Identification of the agency and the contracting office. 

Bureau of Land Management – Department of the Interior -US Wildland Fire Service 4955 Canyon Crest Dr.

Riverside CA, 92507

Description of supply or service required to meet the agency’s needs. 

Tablet Command is an approved app that can be downloaded on our mobile devices through the DOI company portal. In order to use the app we need to purchase 25 licenses for users. We also need them to establish a portal for our organization that has maps of our specific Direct Protection Areas, Mutual Threat Zones, as well as the real-time satellite location data for all of our fire resources. We also need “view only” access to our cooperator’s Computer Aided Dispatch logs for fires, and vehicle location data for those same cooperators who we have data sharing agreements with. We also need the functionality to use tablet command for our Incident Commander’s to manage our Incidents.

The rationale or circumstances for limiting competition. We need to be able to receive and share data with our cooperators in real time, in the field, on mobile devices. This is important so we can have a common operating picture and make timely decisions on wildland fires that don’t conflict with our cooperator’s decisions. There is no other platform that can share the types of information that we need to share. We need to see the real time GIS locations of our cooperator’s fire equipment, and they need to be able to see our equipment locations in GIS. We need to be able to view Computer Aided Dispatch notes for our cooperators with data sharing agreements.

A description of the Market Research (MR) conducted and the results or a statement of the reason MR was not conducted. 

The Government has conducted research for a platform that could have the features and integration of tablet command. The data sharing ability with cooperators is the most important aspect. So many of our cooperators already use Tablet Command including San Bernardino County, Cal Fire SDU, Cal Fire RRU, Cal Fire BDU, San Diego County, Riverside County, Kern County, Imperial County, Los Angeles County, Redlands City, Highland City, Apple Valley City, Victorville City, and Palm Spring City. Since these cooperators are already using this platform, it is really easy to share locations, intelligence, and other data to maintain a common operating picture. There are many times on incidents that we are in unified command with 3 or 4 of these cooperators and the timely information sharing is critical. Tablet Command will remove several barriers to much of the information.

The Government was unable to locate a competitor with the ability to view interagency shared AVL (automatic vehicle locations or view shared interagency CAD (computer aided dispatch) incident data across

jurisdictional boundaries. These two items are the most critical components that we need to carry out our mission.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
M5 RACER Heavy Platform Maintenance Support 
26 FEB 2026 
Part 1 
General Information 
1. G eneral:  This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering
the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its
administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the
Government and its employees.
1.1  Description of Services/Introduction:  This is a non-personal service(s) contract to 
provide maintenance support for four (4) M5 Robotic Autonomy in Complex Enviornments for 
Resiliency (RACER) Heavy Platforms.   
1.2  Background:  The 36th Engineer Brigade has received four (4) RACER Heavy Platforms 
(RHP) with full autonomy sensors and compute capability, permanently transferred from the 
DARPA RACER program. These platforms are unique and not part of an established Army 
program of record, thus lacking institutional sustainment support. This contract is required to 
provide the necessary maintenance and support to ensure the RHPs are operational for use in 
training events, experimentation, and to support the 1st Cavalry Division’s Transformation in 
Contact (TiC) 2.0 efforts, culminating in a validating National Training Center (NTC) rotation 
(27-05).  
1.3  Scope:  The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall 
provide maintenance, sustainment, and training support for four RHPs. This includes, but is not 
limited to: on-site Field Service Representative (FSR) support during training events; 
preventive and corrective maintenance; management of a budget for replacement parts, 
sensors, and consumables; subcontracted support  
, ; remote and on- site autonomy software support, including updates and 
patches; and management of network and data subscriptions for the platforms. 
1.4  Objectives:  The objective is to provide a comprehensive maintenance and sustainment 
package that ensures the 4x RHPs are fully mission-capable, safe, and reliable for use by the 
36th Engineer Brigade. This support will reduce the risk of system failure during major training 
events and allow Soldiers to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot the platform effectively.  
1.5  General Information:

ontrol Plan (QCP): The Contractor shall develop and maintain a QCP to 
ensure services are performed in accordance with (IAW) this PWS. The Contractor shall 
develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE

The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, on behalf of VISN 6  intends to enter into a sole source procurement with CareFusions Solutions LLC, 3750 Torrey View Court, San Diego, CA 92130. 

NAICS code 541519-Other Computer Related Services. The proposed contract action is to provide software management services to Alaris Infusion System. The Contractor is to provide  software management services to include; internet, webinar and on-site training and clinical education, support ranging from remote monitoring of the Alaris Systems Manager to technical support for the Alaris Infusion System and includes collection of data and providing analytic tools and services to VISN 6 VA Medical facilities. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.103-1(b) using the procedures under FAR 12.102 (a), Restricting Competition. Contract will be for a period of performance of a base plus four option years. This notice of intent is not a request for quotation. Interested parties may identify their interest in the requirement and capabilities to monique.cordero@va.gov no later than 10:00 AM EST, Aug.7, 2024. Telephone inquirers will not be accepted.  All information shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government.

Gray market items are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) goods sold through unauthorized channels in direct competition with authorized distributors. Statement of Work 
NeuroX-Fusion: LLM-Foundation Model Alignment 
 
Period of Performance: 
Twenty-four (24) months from subcontract start date. 
1. Background and Purpose 
The DOE ASCR–funded NeuroX-Fusion project aims to construct a unified, multimodal foundation 
model of the human brain— integrating MRI, electrophysiology, video, and language— using a Large 
Language Model (LLM) as a shared semantic space. The roadmap culminates in NeuroX-Fusion, a 
130B-parameter “digital twin” that unifies NeuroX-MRI and NeuroX-Ephys via LLM-based alignment. 
 
The Subcontractor shall be a leader in: 
• Naturalistic fMRI and intracranial recordings 
• Brain–language mapping and LLM–brain encoding 
• Neural coupling during storytelling and real-world communication 
 
The Subcontractor will help refine LLM–brain alignment, validate cross-modal fusion between fMRI 
and electrophysiology, and co-develop protocols to use the digital twin for in-silico experiments.  
 
This Statement of Work (SOW) formalizes a focused, two-year subcontract to: 
• Design and validate LLM–Foundation Model (FM) alignment strategies and 
benchmarks for NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and NeuroX-Fusion. 
• Co-design neuroscience-aligned pretraining and auxiliary objectives that embed 
neurocognitive constraints directly into NeuroX foundation model training. 
• Deliver datasets, benchmarks, and prototype pipelines that integrate early NeuroX 
checkpoints and drive rapid iteration. 
• Academic dissemination (conference and journal publications) is encouraged, consistent with 
DOE and institutional requirements. 
2. Scope of Work and Major Task Areas 
Work under this SOW is organized into three major task areas: 
• Task Area 1 – LLM–Foundation Model Alignment 
• Task Area 2 – Neuroscience-Aligned Pretraining Objectives 
• Task Area 3 – Prototyping, Datasets, Benchmarks, and Hackathon 
 
Each task area includes specific subtasks and deliverables. 

 
  March 9, 2026

does not constitute “development” or “production” technology under applicable export control 
regulations. 
 
3. Detailed Tasks and Deliverables 
Task Area 1 – LLM–Foundation Model Alignment 
Objective: 
Ensure that NeuroX foundation models (NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and ultimately NeuroX-Fusion) 
learn latent representations that are neurally and cognitively plausible when aligned to an LLM, 
especially under naturalistic narrative and communication stimuli. 
Task 1.1 – Alignment Design for Naturalistic Language and Narratives 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Specify alignment strategies between: 
o Token- and layer-level representations from an LLM applied to continuous language 
(stories, conversations, movie dialogue); and 
o Brain representations from MRI and electrophysiology for the same stimuli. 
• Provide guidance on: 
o Which LLM layers and NeuroX feature levels should correspond to different 
cortical hierarchies and timescales of processing. 
o How to handle speaker–listener coupling, inter-subject shared versus idiosyncratic 
variance, and narrative/event structure in the alignment design. 
Deliverable T1.1: 
“LLM–Foundation Model Alignment Design Note” (approximately 2–4 pages, PDF), explicitly 
tailored to NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and NeuroX-Fusion. 
 
Task 1.2 – Alignment Benchmarks and Evaluation Metrics 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Define quantitative benchmarks to test whether NeuroX models, when projected into the 
LLM latent space, capture: 
o Semantic structure of continuous narratives (event boundaries, topic shifts, 
suspense points). 
o Known hierarchical processing patterns in cortex during naturalistic stimuli. 
• Propose metrics including, but not limited to: 
o Encoding/decoding performance (correlation/R²) for fMRI and Ephys. 
o Inter-subject correlation (ISC) and shared-variance measures. 
o Region- and layer-resolved alignment curves. 
 
Deliverable T1.2: 
Benchmark specification document (PDF) plus example evaluation scripts (e.g., Jupyter notebooks) 
runnable on modest-scale models and subsets of NeuroX data.

does not constitute “development” or “production” technology under applicable export control 
regulations. 
 
Task 1.3 – Cross-Modal Validation for NeuroX-Fusion 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Define tests to evaluate whether MRI and Ephys branches, when aligned through the shared 
LLM space, produce consistent semantic trajectories for the same stimuli. 
• Identify canonical paradigms (e.g., story listening, movie-viewing tasks) and expected cross-
modal patterns (spatial vs temporal signatures, hierarchical processing) that serve as validation 
targets for NeuroX-Fusion. 
Deliverable T1.3: 
“NeuroX-Fusion Cross-Modal Validation Playbook” (PDF), with specific contrasts, ROIs, and example 
analyses. 
 
Task Area 2 – Neuroscience-Aligned Pretraining Objectives 
Objective: 
Design, prototype, and specify neuroscience- and cognition-aligned pretraining/auxiliary 
objectives that encode realistic constraints from human communication and brain dynamics directly 
into NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and NeuroX-Fusion training. These objectives will complement 
other neuro-informed loss functions and fusion layers developed by NeuroX collaborators. 
 
Task 2.1 – Objective Design: Naturalistic Narrative and Communication Priors 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Co-design with BNL and collaborators a set of pretraining or auxiliary objectives that 
encourage NeuroX models to: 
o Predict/encode brain responses to continuous narratives given text, video, and/or 
internal NeuroX representations. 
o Capture speaker–listener coupling and shared semantic spaces across individuals. 
o Respect multi-timescale structure (fast lexical/phonetic vs slow narrative/event-
level dynamics). 
• Express each objective as a well-defined loss term compatible with NeuroX training (e.g., 
contrastive objectives, prediction heads, regularizers). 
Deliverable T2.1: 
“Neuroscience-Aligned Objective Specification” (PDF) describing each objective, required inputs, 
pseudo-code for loss computation, and its role in MRI, Ephys, and Fusion training. 
 
Task 2.2 – Prototype Implementations on Small-Scale Models 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Implement reference versions of at least two to three core neuroscience-aligned objectives using:

o Public LLMs and/or moderate-scale variants, and 
o Lab and/or publicly available brain datasets. 
• Demonstrate that: 
o The objectives are numerically stable; and 
o They improve alignment metrics defined in Task 1 (e.g., encoding correlation, ISC) 
compared with simple baselines. 
Deliverable T2.2: 
Prototype code modules (e.g., PyTorch / HuggingFace style) implementing selected objectives, with 
example training scripts and a short results note (figures or summary tables). 
 
Task 2.3 – Integration Requirements for NeuroX Training 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Translate objective designs into clear API and data requirements for the NeuroX training 
stack, specifying: 
o Necessary internal activations (e.g., layer-wise embeddings, temporal pooling outputs). 
o Annotation formats and batching schemes for aligned brain–text–video windows. 
• Coordinate with BNL and external collaborators (e.g., Cha/Moon labs) so these objectives 
are compatible with other knowledge-constrained loss functions and multi-modal fusion 
layers planned for NeuroX. 
Deliverable T2.3: 
“NeuroX Training Integration Requirements” (PDF), optionally co-signed with BNL, for engineering 
implementation. 
 
Task Area 3 – Prototyping, Datasets, Benchmarks, and Hackathon 
Objective: 
Provide concrete datasets, benchmarks, pipelines, and a focused hackathon that operationalize Task 
Areas 1 and 2 and accelerate integration with early NeuroX checkpoints. 
 
Task 3.1 – Dataset Curation for Pretraining and Evaluation 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Curate one or more naturalistic neuroimaging datasets (subject to IRB and data-use 
agreements) suitable for: 
o Neuroscience-aligned pretraining objectives (Task 2). 
o Alignment and evaluation benchmarks (Task 1). 
• For each dataset, provide: 
o Preprocessed fMRI or electrophysiology signals, or standardized preprocessing instructions.

o Time-aligned transcripts and/or annotations (e.g., words, sentences, events, scenes). 
• Recommended splits for model training, validation, and evaluation-only usage. 
 
Deliverable T3.1: 
Dataset package(s) or secure access instructions, plus accompanying documentation targeted to 
NeuroX engineers and scientists. 
Task 3.2 – Benchmark Definitions and Leaderboard Templates 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Define benchmark tasks that NeuroX models should be evaluated on, such as: 
o Predicting brain activity from text/video embeddings. 
o Inferring semantic/event labels from NeuroX brain latents. 
o Capturing shared vs idiosyncratic components across subjects. 
• Provide: 
o Formal task definitions and metric formulas. 
o Reference baselines using simpler models (e.g., linear models, smaller transformers). 
 
Deliverable T3.2: 
Benchmark specification (PDF) plus runnable evaluation scripts and an optional “leaderboard” template 
(CSV/JSON formats). 
 
Task 3.3 – End-to-End Prototype Pipelines 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Assemble minimal end-to-end pipelines mirroring planned NeuroX-Fusion workflows, for example: 
o Input: stimulus (text/video) ± brain data → 
o LLM + prototype brain model → 
o Neuroscience-aligned losses and alignment metrics → 
o Evaluation and visualization outputs. 
• Ensure these pipelines are structured to allow NeuroX-MRI/Ephys/Fusion checkpoints to be 
inserted later with minimal code changes. 
Deliverable T3.3: 
Example notebooks/scripts plus a brief summary of findings on current (non-NeuroX) models. 
 
Task 3.4 – NeuroX-Fusion Hackathon 
Objective: 
Conduct an intensive joint hackathon to integrate early NeuroX checkpoints into pipelines and 
stress-test neuroscience-aligned objectives and benchmarks.

The Subcontractor shall: 
• In collaboration with BNL, plan and execute a 2–3 day hackathon (virtual or hybrid) during 
Year 2 focused on: 
o Plugging early NeuroX-MRI / NeuroX-Ephys / NeuroX-Fusion checkpoints into  
pipelines and benchmarks. 
o Rapidly prototyping and comparing neuroscience-aligned pretraining objectives from Task 2. 
o Identifying failure modes, gaps in data or interfaces, and high-value follow-up experiments. 
• Before the hackathon: 
o Prepare a small set of ready-to-run tasks (e.g., narrative/fMRI benchmarks, speaker–
listener alignment tests). 
o Provide template notebooks and short documentation for participants. 
• After the hackathon: 
o Summarize experiments, results, and recommended adjustments to objectives, 
benchmarks, and integration plans. 
Deliverables T3.4: 
 
• T3.4-D1: “Hackathon Plan” (1–2 pages: objectives, agenda, roles, and technical requirements). 
• T3.4-D2: “Hackathon Outcome Report” (slides or short written report summarizing key results and 
follow-ups). 
 
4. Academic Publications and Dissemination 
Subject to DOE and BNL policies on publications and intellectual property, the Subcontractor is 
expected to pursue scholarly dissemination of key scientific findings arising from this work, 
including but not limited to: 
• Co-authored conference papers (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CogNeuro meetings) on: 
o LLM–brain/LLM–FM alignment results using NeuroX components. 
o Neuroscience-aligned pretraining objectives and benchmarks. 
• Journal articles in appropriate neuroscience or computational journals, highlighting: 
o New insights into brain–language mapping from NeuroX models. 
o Methodological advances in multimodal brain foundation modeling. 
 
Deliverable P1 (Academic Outputs): 
A brief annual list of peer-reviewed conference or journal manuscripts submitted and/or published 
that substantially involve work funded through this SOW, including DOIs where available.

Repair Program In-Service Engineering Agent’s responsibilities 
of progressive repair capability for Government electronic and 
electrical systems. The solicitation for this requirement will 
be posted in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment 
(PIEE) Solicitation Module and publicized via SAM.gov. 
 
A SeaPort-NxG Sources Sought notice was issued in the SeaPort 
portal on 26 January 2026 for this requirement entitled, “2MMTR 
FOLLOW ON.” Based on the responses received, NAVSEALOGCEN 
intends to issue this solicitation as a SeaPort NxG Small 
Business set-aside.   
 
NOTE:  To be eligible as a SeaPort-NxG Small Business during the 
competitive ordering process, the Prime’s basic SeaPort NxG 
contract must reflect a Small Business within the System for 
Award Management (SAM) at the time of proposal submission. 
 
This notice also provides a draft Performance Work Statement 
(PWS) for the upcoming task order solicitation. The draft PWS is 
being released to solicit comments and questions from interested 
parties.   
 
Interested parties/potential offerors are encouraged to respond 
to this Advance Notice with questions and comments as soon as 
possible in order to allow for review prior to release of the 
solicitation.  Questions and answers shall be submitted by email 
to marisa.n.wirfel.civ@us.navy.mil and 
cody.d.hutchinson.civ@us.navy.mil.  Note that questions/comments 
submitted in response to this draft PWS may not receive a 
response; however, all questions and comments will be reviewed 
by the Government to assist in identifying revisions that may be 
incorporated in the PWS.

task order issued on a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) basis.  It is

value basis to the Government, and a trade-off analysis will be

performance, and evaluated cost / price.  The solicitation is 
anticipated to include a one-year Base Period and four (4) one-
year Option Periods.

services for this requirement is Engineering Services Network 
under SeaPort-NxG task order N00178-19-D-7599/N6660422F3006.

around the following dates:

Task Order Start: October 2026

ECTION C – STATEMENT OF WORK 
3RD PARTY VESSEL INSPECTION SERVICES 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
1. BACKGROUND
The U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) is an agency of the United States Department of 
Transportation. MARAD requires the services of a third-party Ship Inspection Service provider 
(Contractor) to provide class-style inspections of MARAD Ships, outside of the Ship Inspection 
requirements of US LAW (American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) (Class) and the United States 
Coast Guard (USCG)). MARAD requires a comprehensive analysis of each vessel’s condition, 
including its documentation, machinery, hull, and coatings. The material condition assessment 
will include a thorough structural and machinery inspection of the vessels and a comprehensive 
report on the conditions of the vessels.  The Contractor shall assess deficiencies that have 
resulted in a USCG 835 or ABS Condition of Class or Finding. MARAD is seeking a third-party 
ship inspection, in addition to the official ABS and USCG inspections required by law, to obtain 
another professional opinion on the condition of its Ready Reserve Fleet vessels. Therefore, any 
entity, other than ABS, meeting the qualifications set forth herein may be considered for award. 
2. CONTRACT INFORMATION

The Contractor shall conduct vessel inspections in two phases. The first phase of the vessel 
inspection that will be conducted will be the preparation phase; the second portion of the 
inspection will be the on-site inspection phase.   
2.1 Preparation Phase  
The following information will be provided at the award of a task order to kick off the inspection 
of a vessel. All documentation shall be reviewed before the start of the on-site inspection. The 
following information will be provided to determine the scope of the on-site inspection.  
2.1.1. Vessel Information: 
o Number of Vessels: Six (6) vessels may be selected for inspection from 
the three classes listed below. 
o Vessel Class and Locations:  
• Watson Class (6ea): Baltimore, MD, Norfolk, V A, New Orleans, 
LA, Vancouver, WA 
• Bob Hope Class (5ea): Newport News, V A, Portland, OR 
• Cape S class (5ea): Norfolk, V A, San Francisco, CA 
o Inspection Scope: All areas of the ship to be inspected.   
o Past Reports: Obtain and review any prior class inspection and service 
reports 
2.1.2. Required Documentation: 
o Class Certificates: Verify all relevant class certificates and regulatory 
compliance documents. 
o Vessel Maintenance Records: Review records on the last dry docking, 
previous inspections, and maintenance conducted on each vessel. 
o Operational Logs: Ensure the operational logs for the vessel's 
machinery and equipment are current. 
2.2. On-Site Inspection Phase 
The Contractor shall apply its own professional maritime inspection methodology consistent 
with classification-society practices. The procedures listed in Sections 2.2.1 through 2.2.7 
represent minimum expectations for inspection scope and reporting and do not prescribe the 
Contractor’s proprietary methods. 
For each vessel, the inspections are to be scheduled during a monthly Dock Trial to allow 
machinery to be observed while in operation.    

2.2.1.  Hull Inspection: 
o Visual Inspection: Thoroughly examine the vessel’s hull for any signs 
of damage, cracks, corrosion, or other structural weaknesses. 
o Thickness Measurement: Review the most recent ultrasonic thickness 
gauges. 
o Condition of Coatings: Inspect the condition of anti-corrosion coatings 
and protective paints. Check for peeling, blistering, or any signs of wear.  
o Bilge Areas and Sea Chests: Ensure that these areas are free of debris, 
corrosion, and that the coatings are in intact. 
o Tanks and Tank Coatings: Inspect the condition of anti-corrosion 
coatings and protective paints. Check for peeling, blistering, or any signs 
of wear. Material condition of the steel structure to be noted. 
2.2.2. Machinery and Engine Room: 
o Main Engine and Auxiliary Equipment: Inspect the condition of the 
main engine, auxiliary engines, and generators for any signs of excessive 
wear, oil leaks, or vibrations. All equipment to be observed while in 
operation as practicable. 
o Piping and Valves: Check the condition of piping systems, including 
steam, fuel, lube oil, cooling water, and ballast systems, for leaks, 
corrosion, and proper insulation.  
o Electrical Systems: Inspect the main electrical panels, circuit breakers, 
and safety systems to ensure they are in good order.   
o HV AC Systems: Verify the air conditioning, ventilation, and heating 
systems in the engine room and house for proper functioning. 
2.2.3. Cargo Equipment: 
• Ramps, Cranes, Elevators, and Material Handling Equipment: 
Observe operational test. Identify and record any anomalies in 
machine performance. Inspect for material condition including 
hydraulic hoses and condition of wires. 
• Cargo Hold Ventilation: Verify all cargo hold fans are operational.  
2.2.4. Coatings and Paints: 

o Deck Coatings: Assess the condition of the deck paint and non-slip 
surfaces. Verify if there are any areas that need resurfacing or 
maintenance.  
o Interior Coatings: Review the condition of coatings in spaces like the 
cargo holds, ballast tanks, stair towers, and other interior sections prone 
to wear. 
2.2.5. Safety Equipment: 
o Lifesaving Equipment: Ensure all lifeboats, life rafts, life vests, and 
other required lifesaving equipment are in place, operational, and 
compliant with regulatory requirements.  
o Fire Safety Equipment: Inspect fire extinguishers, sprinklers, and 
alarms for operational readiness. 
o Navigational Equipment: Verify the functionality and calibration of 
navigational systems (radars, GPS, AIS, etc.) as per regulatory 
requirements. 
2.2.6.  Structural Integrity and Stability: 
o Ballast and Stability System: Inspect the vessel's ballast system and 
stability equipment. Verify that they are operating correctly. This is to 
include Ballast Treatment Systems.  
o Strength of Hull Supports: Assess areas that are critical to structural 
integrity, such as bulkheads, frames, and support beams. 
o Load Line Markings: Verify that the load line markings are intact and 
readable. 
2.2.7.  Pollution Prevention: 
o Bilge Water Treatment: Inspect the system for treating and discharging 
bilge water. Ensure it complies with MARPOL regulations. 
o Sewage Treatment: Inspect the sewage treatment system for material 
condition, functionality and regulatory compliance.  
o Garbage Management: Confirm the presence and condition of waste 
management systems. 
3. DELIVERABLES 
3.1. Post-Inspection Report 

After completing the inspection of each vessel, the Contractor shall compile a detailed report for 
each vessel that includes: 
3.1.1. Executive Summary: 
o Overview of the vessel’s overall condition and any immediate concerns. 
o Summary of key areas requiring attention or repairs. 
3.1.2. Inspection Findings and Deficiencies 
o List all deficiencies 
o Submit a plan for dates of inspections to the Ships Operations 
and Maintenance Officers (SOMOs) to be coordinated via 
area division COR. MARAD will reply within 3 business 
days confirmation of schedule or provide alternate date(s) of 
inspection. 
o Provide the location and immediate impact of each 
deficiency 
o Provide a prioritization for each deficiency - Critical, High 
Priority, Medium Priority, and Low Priority to guide 
prioritization of repairs or maintenance. 
o All Deficiencies shall be provided with an assessment of risk 
based on the ship’s ability to be activated within a 5-day 
window and complete 180 days of traditional cargo vessel 
operations.  
o Hull Condition: Specific areas that show signs of damage, corrosion, or 
wear. 
o Machinery Condition: Any issues found with the engine room equipment 
including pumps, electrical systems, or other mechanical components. 
o Coating Conditions: Any issues found with paint or coatings on the 
vessel, including deterioration or necessary touch-ups. 
o Safety Systems: Whether or not safety equipment is up-to-date and in 
good working order.

Part 1: Service Provision and Scope

The contractor shall provide all personnel, materials, supervision, other items, and non-

requirements of the  
Maneuver Support Center of Excellence (MSCoE) G6 at Fort Leonard Wood, 
Missouri.

microphones, speakers, amplifiers, and associated control systems

Automated Feature Extraction RFI Objective Questions 
Utilizing Section 3.0, 4.0, and Appendix A of the FDT AFE SOO as a reference, describe how you would 
address the following: 
Objective 1: Provide and Deploy a High-Performing Automated Feature Extraction (AFE) 
Capability or Service:  
What AFE automation processes do you utilize to produce features today? For a given source (or 
combination of sources), what is your methodology to create real world representations of specific 
features? What combinations of data types are used in your process (e.g. vector-to-vector, image-to-
vector, PDF-to-vector, and/or image-to-image, image-to-surface model, etc.) for specific features? How 
do your current processes ensure accurate position, confidence assessment and time is associated with 
automated feature extraction processing and its final product? How would attribution and identification of 
source data be handled throughout the AFE processing chain? Can you describe how your AFE 
solution(s) fits into geospatial data production tools and systems utilizing multiple input data formats? 
How do your capabilities integrate with other commercially available geospatial tools?  What Technical 
Readiness Level1 (TRL) is your capability current graded at?  Describe the process on how you would 
separate out multiple features that may be conflated during AFE processing. 
Objective 2: Ensure High-Quality Data and Enable Analyst-in-the-Loop Validation: 
How would you ensure that the changes that may occur during the feature extraction processing are 
detected and retained are relevant to geospatial data? What source formats would your system or 
algorithm(s) ingest to produce automated specific and/or multiple features within the same area of 
interest? What processes would you employ to provide GEOINT assurance that changes are verified, 
comprehensive and valid?  Describe your process to organize an analyst notification system and how 
would you ensure critical processes/outputs are prioritized for review?  What are your defined threshold 
metrics for minor, major and critical for AFE outputs for topographic, maritime and aeronautical 
features? How would you achieve an objective threshold accuracy of 80% with a goal for objective 
accuracy of 99% for topographic, maritime and aeronautical features? How does your solution interface 
with GIS systems for viewing, evaluating and editing results? Describe any AI/ML models that are used 
for your quality assessments. 
Objective 3: Enable Seamless Utilization by NGA's GEOINT Ecosystem via open APIs 
Describe the APIs your solution provides to allow external system (like NGA’s) to programmatically 
submit processing jobs, monitor status, and retrieve results. Please specify the API types (e.g., REST, 
gRPC), authentication methods, and data formats used. What standardized formats (e.g., GDB, Shapefile) 
to support interoperability with other NGA systems and direct dissemination to customer platforms would 
you recommend?  What would your compute and infrastructure needs be for your solution? 
Objective 4: Meet and Maintain Stringent Performance and Security Standards 
Describe your solution’s scalability, reliability, resiliency and security standards used in the production of 
AFE products.  What are the nominal/baseline operating benchmarks and infrastructure specifications for 
your system?
