AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management 
solution’s core technology, database structure, and application logic are owned by 
AGFA. The AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose 
Management solution requires the VA to procure specialized support, security, and 
technical integration for the reasons specified below: 
x
 Exclusive Vendor Support and Training: A GFA does not authorize third-party 
companies to support their systems. The maintenance, technical support, and 
system-level access required to manage these servers are restricted to AGFA, 
ensuring that only certified personnel work on the technology. 
x Complex, Integrated Ecosystem: AGFA servers and operating systems are 
heavily customized, closed-loop environments rather than generic, open-source 
platforms, and they use proprietary grid computing technology to manage real-
time imaging data. 
x Only Source Requirement: Due to the spec ialized nature of the software, servers, 
and operating system, AGFA is listed as the only source for the AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management 
solution support, meaning that alternative vendors do not possess the necessary 
training or access to provide support/maintenance for their solution infrastructure. 
x System Integrity and Data Security: The proprietary design ensures that the high 
volume of archived data (sometimes over 247 terabytes) remains secure and that 
the system components, such as workstations, scanners, and servers, function 
specifically with each other without interference from uncertified software, 
maintenance, or hardware. 
The AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose 
Management solution is critical for the VA because it provides real-time, enterprise-wide 
radiation dose monitoring, and it is considered irreplaceable due to its ability to 
aggregate data across multiple, diverse, and legacy imaging systems, eliminating the 
need for manual, site-specific reporting, and offering specialized, high-accuracy 
dosimetry for patients. More importantly, putting AGFA software on a new operating 
system and servers would not be feasible option for the VA due to dependencies on 
existing technology, strict hardware licensing, and specialized, low-level drivers that are 
not designed for modern operating system security standards. AGFA frequently stops 
releasing updated drivers when a new operating system is released, particularly for 
older scanners or imaging digitizers such as those used by the VA. Existing AGFA 
software often requires Kernel-type drivers, which have newer operating systems (like 
Windows 10/11) block to improve system security and stability.  
The AGFA infrastructure, servers, and other imaging software throughout VA use USB 
security dongles (license keys). If a user attempts to move to a new workstation, they 
may find the license is locked to the original machine or that the dongle is "retired" and 
cannot be activated on new hardware. AGFA servers, particularly those used in their 
radiology Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) and imaging solutions 
(like IMPAX), are considered proprietary because they are designed as closed systems 
where only AGFA-authorized personnel, software, and hardware can fully support and 


 
Page 3 of 6 
interact with the technology. Also, the server software is tightly coupled with specific, 
certified workstation hardware that has been uniquely configured 
by AGFA.  
There are 27 VAMC’s currently using the AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM 
Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution. AGFA is the only distributor that 
maintains a Memorandum of Understanding/Interconnection Security Agreement with 
the VA, which significantly improves remote system access, security, and efficiency 
during the implementation and support of the application. No other brand name software 
solution can integrate or will be interoperable or compatible with the current AGFA 
software solution, servers, and operating system. Specifically, the current AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution 
communicates through source code that is based on AGFA proprietary data. The VA 
currently utilizes the AGFA DoseMonitor and REM Registry - Enterprise Dose 
Management solution and has a dose tracking contract involving AGFA DoseMonitor 
that has been in place since 2021. This existing product provides the VA with dose 
tracking and software capabilities that are installed on a VLAN located in the Cleveland 
data center. The initial contract provided Dose Aggregation to Cleveland and ten (10) 
Sites. As part of a VA Innovator’s Network (iNET) initiative, sixteen (16) additional sites 
were added, and the VA REM Registry was developed and based in the Cleveland VA 
data center. The AGFA DoseMonitor and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose 
Management contract aggregates patient dose tracking for 27 VAMCs. Dose 
Aggregation and REM Registry require enterprise dose management to provide the 
means for vendor agnostic dose tracking of these VAMCs. The resulting AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management software 
licenses will provide a platform to integrate Dose Aggregation and REM Registry within 
the Oracle Cerner electronic health record. No other software can provide this 
communication capability without the OEM’s source code.  
Additionally, only AFGA can provide the necessary maintenance support as it is the only 
source able to maintain the propriety source code required for software updates, 
security patches, bug fixes, and technical support. No other firm currently has the 
capability of developing and issuing software maintenance support for the AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management software 
due to their inability to be interoperable and compatible with the software.  
The VA needs these software licenses and maintenance because they are currently the 
only software licenses and maintenance that are interoperable and compatible with the 
current AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose 
Management solution. If the VA were to purchase new software licenses and 
maintenance support, the VA would then need to purchase a new operating system and 
servers. Transitioning to a different vendor would necessitate replacing and 
reconfiguring VAMC server integrations, incurring costs exceeding . Failure to 
procure the AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose 
Management solution would result in the discontinuation of the REM Registry, as a new 
software solution would not be compatible or interoperable with the existing AGFA 
solution, thereby diminishing the VA's capacity to monitor and optimize radiation 
exposure, which would adversely affect Veteran health. Additionally, a new Enterprise 


 
Page 4 of 6 
Dose Management system would require significant duplication of time and costs 
required to redevelop, reconfigure
, and implement any alternative. Ultimately, if the 
AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management 
software licenses and maintenance support are not purchased, the VA will experience 
significant disruptions in diagnostic imaging services since AGFA’s imaging equipment 
is proprietary, and the company provides critical software updates, patches, and 
information security certifications. A loss of maintenance support could lead to security 
vulnerabilities and software failures. Moreover, consolidating data from across the VA 
has significantly advanced the VA’s ability to optimize radiation doses, and the AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution 
serves as a valuable resource when assessing cases involving higher radiation 
exposure.  
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition: Recent market research conducted, detailed in 
paragraph eight of this document, has confirmed that no additional sources have 
emerged that can meet the Government’s requirements without the need for multiple 
procurements or an undetermined amount of cus
tomization to one or more commercial 
products. There is no competition anticipated for this acquisition. Procurement data 
does not include any unnecessary requirements that may inhibit competition. The 
s
olicitation will be made publicly available, along with this justification in accordance 
with FAR 6.301(b)(2) and 5.201(c)(3).  Furthermore, the proposed action will be 
synopsized on the Contracting Opportunities Page in accordance with FAR 5.101. Any 
quotes received shall be evaluated. The Request for Quotation will be sent to
 AGFA 
directly via email.
7. Actions to Increase Competition: The Government will continue to conduct market 
research to ascertain if there are changes in the marketplace that would enable 
competition in future actions.
8. Market Research: The Government’s technical experts conducted market research in 
October 2025 by interacting with other VA
MCs, Veterans Integrated Service Networks 
(VISN) and the VHA National Health Physics Program. Similar products researched 
were Ignyte Group, ProAqCT, and Radimetrics. These products could not meet
 VA’s 
need due to not being compatible with the current AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and 
REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution.
Ignyte Group: AGFA integrates DoseMonitor with its existing Picture Archiving and 
Communication System (PACS), whereas Ignyte (Change Healthcare) provides a 
browser-based solution that is not currently compatible with the existing AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution, 
differing primarily in vendor focus and integration approach, with AGFA offering its own 
dose management tools.  
ProAqCT: AGFA’s solution integrates with their broader enterprise imaging platform 
and uses PACSHealth's DoseMonitor product for data acquisition and analytics. 
Conversely, ProAqCT is a s
tandalone solu
tion that uniquely incorporates automated 
image quality monitoring alongside dose tracking and would require significant 


 
Page 5 of 6 
customization, configuration, and transition costs to implement if the VA were to switch  
from AGFA’s proprietary software solution. 
Radimetrics: While the AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – 
Enterprise Dose Management solution emphasizes its interoperability and data 
integration capabilities within existing workflows, Radimetrics, for effective 
implementation, would require a robust validation process and a multidisciplinary team 
to ensure accuracy and reliability of data collection which would then require significant 
interoperability/transition costs if the VA were to switch  from AGFA’s proprietary 
software solution. 
Any new product’s server and data solution would have to be aggregated, sorted, and 
plugged into a new system, and the data could not be pushed together without having to 
rebuild. Furthermore, the current AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – 
Enterprise Dose Management solution communicates through a source code that is 
based on AGFA’s proprietary data. Also, discussions with representatives from other 
VAMCs and VISNs have resulted in a consensus that AGFA is the only authorized and 
delegated source with assigned authority to distribute and manage the AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution. 
On January 21, 2026, the Government’s technical expert contacted PACSHEALTH 
directly, and the company confirmed that AGFA is the only distributor of the AGFA 
DoseMonitor Aggregation and REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management solution. 
As a result, it was determined that the required AGFA DoseMonitor Aggregation and 
REM Registry – Enterprise Dose Management software licenses and maintenance must 
be procured on a sole source basis from AGFA. 
9. Other Facts: None.


 
 
Page 6 of 6 
 
Technical/Requirements Certification 
I certify that the supporting data under my cognizance, which are included in this 
justification, are accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief. 
   
 
Fair and Reasonable Cost Determination 
I hereby determine that the anticipated price to the Government for this contract action 
will be fair and reasonable compared to historical prices paid for the same or similar 
items. In addition, prices will be compared to catalog pricing for the software if available. 
Finally, if necessary, the proposed pricing will be compared to the Independent 
Government Cost Estimate.  
  
 
Contracting Officer Certification/Approval 
I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and 
belief.

CSO Project Sabre 
Call 001 
Vendor Question and Answer 
Feb 26th, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Contents 
General ......................................................................................................................... 2 
Focus Area 1 .................................................................................................................. 4 
Focus Area 2 .................................................................................................................. 7 
Focus Area 3 .................................................................................................................. 8 
Focus Area 4 .................................................................................................................. 9 
Focus Area 5 .................................................................................................................10 
 

General 
Question Answer 
The base CSO has slightly different response 
requirements than the individual call. Do the 
base CSO Solution Brief requirements still 
apply such as a Cover Sheet (which is 
excluded from the page count), an Executive 
Summary (1 page), and Company Viability 
(summary of current fundraising, top line 
revenues, and commercialization and go-to-
market strategy)? Or are responses strictly 
adhering to the required content in this 
specific call? 
Where there appears to be a conflict, the 
individual call instructions take precedence 
over the base CSO instructions. The purpose of 
a specific call is to provide tailored 
instructions for that particular effort. 
Therefore, responses should be limited to the 
five (5) pages or ten (10) slides and contain 
only the content explicitly required by the 
specific call.  
Is the 1 page a not to exceed limit, or is one 
page to be designated for the Executive 
Summary? 
See above.  
Can graphics, tables, charts, header/footer be 
exempt from the 12-point font requirement 
as long as they are readable? 
Yes, that is allowable. 
Will the Government please confirm that a 
.pdf submission of Briefing Slides in 
response to Step 1 is allowable? 
Yes, that is allowable. 
In Step 1: Solution Brief Submission 
Attributes, the Government states that, 
“Submissions are limited to either five (5) 
single-sided pages (12-point font) or ten (10) 
presentation slides.” Can the Government 
clarify if it intended to read, “…five (5) 
single-spaced pages…”? If not, please 
provide guidance for Offerors to submit 
single-sided digital documentation.  
No, the line reads five (5) single-sided pages. 5 
total pages of content, plus a cover-page. 
Cover-page does not count towards 5 page 
limit.  
Additionally, can the Government clarify if 
there are any formatting or font restrictions 
for the presentation slide submission format? 
No restrictions.  
Does the cover page/slide count towards the 
page/slide number limit?  
No, see above.  
Page 13 paragraph 3 describes that “The 
Government prefers an initial effort of 
approximately three (3) months that delivers 
a clear ‘minimum viable product’ before 
pursuing longer-term activities.” Is it 
assumed this excludes FA3 as the base 
period is only two months? 
Yes, that is correct.  

Will multiple awards be made for each topic?  The Government has not yet decided how 
many awards it will make for each Focus Area.  
This will depend on the quality of the 
proposals received and the availability of 
funds. 
Call 001 designates NAICS code 518210. 
The contract vehicle may be either an OTA 
or a FAR-based contract. Could you please 
clarify when it will be determined whether 
the procurement will utilize a FAR-based 
contract or an OTA? If a FAR-based contract 
is selected, we want to ensure we are 
properly registered under the designated 
NAICS code?  
This will partially depend on what instrument 
the offeror proposes.  As stated on page 14 of 
Call 001, Step 1, Required content: "Contract 
Vehicle Eligibility: State if your company is 
seeking an Other Transaction (OT) agreement 
and, if so, the basis for such an award (e.g., 
Non-Traditional Defense contractor status)." In 
other words, if your company is seeking an OT 
award, you must state your justification for 
receiving an OT in your Step 1 submittal.  The 
USG will make a preliminary finding 
regarding OT status after reviewing Step 1 
solution briefs and will make a final 
determination during Step 2 negotiations, prior 
to award. 
What does the initial task order look like? Take Focus Area 4, for example: The 12-
Month PoP is for the intial Task Order. The 
USG inteds to structure these like an IDIQ to 
allow follow-on task orders.  
We acknowledge that the Q&A window for 
the CSO – Call 01 has closed; however, we 
seek clarification regarding CUI handling. 
Proposals derived from the Call 01 CUI files 
would be treated as CUI derivatives and 
marked as such. Please advise whether the 
government will offer a secure submission 
channel for proposals containing CUI 
derivatives. 
The vendor will need to make sure the 
submission is encrypted. The method is up to 
the vendor who is submitting. 
 
  

Focus Area 1 
Question Answer 
What are the target frequencies we intend to 
jam?  
The target frequencies are up to the vendor to 
decide; an example of what could be done is 
provided in the CSO. Demonstrations should 
prove functionality of the prototype and be as 
close as possible to the desired form, fit, and 
function as presented in the Call. 
How many nodes do we intend to jam?  The number of nodes to jam is up to the vendor 
to decide; demonstrations should prove 
functionality of the prototype and be as close as 
possible to the desired form, fit, and function as 
presented in the Call. 
What range can the multiple nodes be from 
each other that we intend to jam? 
The number of nodes and distance between is 
up to the vendor to decide; demonstrations 
should prove functionality of the prototype and 
be as close as possible to the desired form, fit, 
and function as presented in the Call. 
Do we need to jam the uplink, downlink, or 
both?  
The decision to jam uplink, downlink, or both 
is up to the vendor; demonstrations should 
prove functionality of the prototype and be as 
close as possible to the desired form, fit, and 
function as presented in the Call. 
Do we need to jam the ground-based high-
power transmitter, the forward low-power 
drone / hand-held node, or both?  
The targets to jam are up to the vendor to 
decide; demonstrations should prove 
functionality of the prototype and be as close as 
possible to the desired form, fit, and function as 
presented in the Call. 
 Do we need to spoof, jam, deny, degrade, 
etc.?  
The decision to spoof, jam, deny, degrade, etc. 
is up to the vendor to decide; demonstrations 
should prove functionality of the prototype and 
be as close as possible to the desired form, fit, 
and function as presented in the Call. 
What power do we need to jam / what is the 
desired power output?  
The power needed to jam will depend on the 
demonstration that a vendor provides; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
How long do we need to sustain jamming 
operations?  
The length of sustained jamming operations is 
up to the vendor to decide; demonstrations 
should prove functionality of the prototype and 
be as close as possible to the desired form, fit, 
and function as presented in the Call. 

 What range from our own drone do we 
need to be able to jam?  
The range to jam is up to the vendor to decide; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
What range from our own operator does our 
own drone need to reach?  
Range details are up to the vendor to decide; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
 How long does our own drone need to be 
able to loiter at its max range?  
Loitering details are up to the vendor to decide; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
What is the anticipated launch platform(s) 
for this use case? 
Platform details are up to the vendor to decide; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
What is the maximum input power to the 
HW payload?  
Power details are up to the vendor to decide; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call; example power requirements 
mentioned are scalable between 1W-100W. 
 What is the maximum HW payload weight?  Weight details are up to the vendor to decide; 
demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
Are the antennas separate from this volume? Front-ends are excluded from the form factor 
and volume restrictions (e.g., antenna is 
separate from SOSA Nano board) 
How much payload volume relief for the 
month 12 flyable prototype demonstrator is 
acceptable if there is a design path to meet 
volume constraints?  
Demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
Please confirm that for the number of 
channels requested, front ends are excluded 
from the form factor restrictions.  
Front-ends are excluded from the form factor 
restrictions (e.g., antenna is separate from 
SOSA Nano board) 

Please clarify if the request is for 16 
independent tuners or a reconfigurable RF 
front end. 
The key word is scalable (but reconfigurable is 
also desirable): "Scalable Number of full-
duplex phase-coherent TX/RX channels: e.g., 
scalable from 1 up to 4 as the threshold with 16 
as a goal"; demonstrations should prove 
functionality of the prototype and be as close as 
possible to the desired form, fit, and function as 
presented in the Call. 
Is a trailing long wire, or trailing wing-edge 
long wire acceptable to support HF 
frequencies?  
Demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
Is the surface of the wing and/or fuselage 
available to use as an RF antenna to support 
HF to C/X-band frequencies?  
Demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
Is an external wing or fuselage mounted RF 
power amplifier, to support RF 
transmissions greater than 5 watts, 
acceptable?  
Demonstrations should prove functionality of 
the prototype and be as close as possible to the 
desired form, fit, and function as presented in 
the Call. 
 
  

Focus Area 2 
Question Answer 
The solicitation implies that the customer desires 
a physical piece of hardware that validates a 
PIC’s SOSA compliance. However, the only test 
harnesses specifically called out are an Out-of-
Band and In-Band System Management test 
harnesses. Would you be able to clarify what 
type of physical hardware you desire?  
The desire is to test SOSA 3U PICs for 
conformance, which include testing all 
rules relevant to the 3U form factor; 
vendors can propose testing all or part of 
SOSA 3U PIC conformance. 
 
  

Focus Area 3 
Question Answer 
Does the USG prefer solutions thar are 
hosted on-prem, cloud, or both? 
The USG has no preference for the solutions 
provided; the environment will need to be able to 
process CUI. 
Does the USG anticipate MBSE models 
being CUI, classified, or both? 
MBSE models will be CUI or Unclassified. 
What is expected at the end of each period 
in FA3? 
The delivery of each period and length (e.g., 2-
month vs 6-month) is up to the vendor to 
negotiate with the USG; as standards evolve, the 
amount of work that can be identified for an FFP 
award will vary. 
Are the deliverables in FA3 intended to 
align with each of the 2-month periods? Is 
each deliverable expected at the end of 
each period? If so, there are only 5 
deliverables. We can include final 
reporting each deliverable for the final 
period. 
The delivery of each period and length (e.g., 2-
month vs 6-month) is up to the vendor to 
negotiate with the USG; as standards evolve, the 
amount of work that can be identified for an FFP 
award will vary. 
 
  

Focus Area 4 
Question Answer 
Focus Area 4 (FA4) description states that the 
base period is 3 months, potentially followed 
by 9 months (page 11). Does this mean that 
the overall PoP would potentially be 12 
months or 9 months.  
The intent to award X vendors 3-month 
award. At the end of the 3-months, we intend 
on awarding Y vendors 9 more months, 
where Y < X. Therefore, 12 month total PoP. 
Will the exemplar IR/RF MPU(s) be delivered 
or made available? Can this be grabbed from 
DLE, or do we need to create/provide the 
skills? (FA4) 
All the documents the USG has deemed 
necessary to accomplish the objectives of 
each focus area on this call have been 
outlined in the shadow boxes throughout the 
call. A vendor who proves their CUI 
capability can request the call-outlined 
documents if they want to. The intention is 
for a vendor to take their existing Big Iron 
4.0 MPUs and convert to AMS GRA MPUs. 
The USG will NOT provide an MPU. A 
vendor needs to bring a capability to the table 
and show how to convert it.  
 
  

Focus Area 5 
Question Answer 
To better align our proposed solution with the 
Government’s expectations, could you provide 
additional visibility on the desired balance 
between automated and manual processes in 
verifying MPU conformance to AMS GRA 
interfaces and behaviors? 
 
Specifically, while the solicitation emphasizes 
a scalable tool for "maximally automated" 
verification and proposing change packages 
for non-automatable requirements, are we to 
understand that the AMS GRA standards 
documents describe the compliance tests you 
wish to automate? As an explicit example, the 
described tests in that (CUI) Compliance 
Assessment Approach - CDRL A093-
AMSGRA list numerous requirements that 
appear not fully set up for automated testing 
through software alone, potentially requiring 
manual analysis in some cases for the MVP 
and final deliverables.  
The intention is to automate, as much as 
possible, AMS GRA rules. As mentioned, 
there are rules that are not fully set up for 
automated testing. The desire is for vendors 
to provide updates to AMS GRA rules that 
keep the intent the same and result in more 
automated testing.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

REVISED STATEMENT OF WORK- AMENDMENT 1

Veterans Online Interactive Screening Program

1. SCOPE OF WORK

1.1 Description of Services: The contractor will grant the Veterans Crisis Line (VCL) a license to use an online interactive screening program, assist VCL staff in training Chat Crisis Responders in the procedures for use of the online interactive screening program, provide ongoing technical assistance/support to the VCL, and collect/evaluate quantitative data. 

Note: At no time shall the program, including the online assessment tool and all components of the interactive screening process, be conducted via artificial intelligence (AI), automated agents, or machine-driven decision-making. All user interactions, assessments, and crisis responses must be performed by trained human staff. Automated AI-based assessments, chatbots, or AI-generated mental health interventions are explicitly prohibited for this contract. The program, including the online assessment tool and any component of the interactive screening process, shall never seek to collect or store Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or Protected Health Information (PHI) from users through prompts, fillable forms, or free-text options.

1.2 Background: There are approximately 20 million Veterans in the United States and six million Veterans who receive care within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VHA). Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention indicate suicide rates among men between the ages of 20 and 65 at approximately 17 per 100,000 persons per year. VHA mental health officials estimate 6,400 suicides per year among Veterans, and 2,500 among veterans receiving health care from VHA. Recent reports have suggested that Veterans may be at an increased risk for conditions and behaviors associated with poor mental health, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression, and increased rates of substance use; all of which are established risk factors for suicide.

The VCL Chat program enables Veterans, along with their families and friends, to interact online anonymously with a trained VCL Crisis Responder. If the Crisis Responder, after a mental health assessment, determines that the user is in a crisis, the Crisis Responder can take immediate steps to transfer them to the VCL’s 24/7 call center, where further counseling and referral services are provided. The VCL chat program is intended to reach out to all Veterans who may or may not be enrolled in the VA health care system and provide them with online access to the VCL and the VA’s suicide prevention services. For many Veterans, their first contact with VHA is through this program.

To help facilitate Veterans’ utilization of the chat program and enhance the chat Crisis Responders’ ability to understand and respond effectively to Veteran-users, the VCL seeks to hire a contractor to develop, implement, and assist in evaluating an online assessment tool that would be seamlessly linked to the VCL Chat program. 

1.3 Objective:

1.3.1  Develop, implement, and assist in evaluating an online, evidence-based assessment tool that would be seamlessly linked to the VCL chat program.  The online, evidence-based assessment tool shall include symptoms of depression, PTSD, and other mental health problems and conditions that are associated with an elevated risk of suicidal behavior in veterans and active duty military service personnel. The assessment tool used for these mental health self-checks must be a standardized, validated mental health screening questionnaire and consistent with current clinical best practices. Completion of this standardized self-check questionnaire constitutes the first step in the crisis assessment process for Veterans accessing the VCL chat program.

1.3.2  The design shall provide full access to the assessment tool and all program functions from a smartphone or other mobile device and include a separate version of the assessment tool for family members and other advocates who wish to get help for a Veteran they are concerned about.

1.3.3  Each user’s submitted assessment, including the automation of the Reference code, shall be computer-classified into one of four tiers, depending on suicide risk, and routed to a live Chat Crisis Responder who provides a personalized response to the user and encourages follow-up conversation through the VCL Chat service. At no time shall artificial intelligence (AI) or automated agents be used to provide mental health assessments, referrals, or crisis responses. All such services must be performed by trained human responders. Automated AI-based interactions or interventions are not permitted. Using the understanding gained from reviewing the information the user provided in their assessment tool, the Chat Crisis Responder can provide appropriate referrals to services and, by including automated follow-up email reminders to participants, further engage the user in exploring and resolving barriers and resistances to service utilization.

1.3.4 An evaluation plan shall be implemented by the contractor and the VCL to measure the assessment tool utilization and outcomes. The contractor and VCL staff will collaborate to analyze and interpret the assessment tool data.

1.3.5 The contractor will work with VCL staff to analyze and interpret the data gathered through the online suicide assessment tool and collaborate with VCL staff in presenting evaluation findings at conferences and in manuscripts intended for professional audiences. Although the contractor will collect the data, VCL will own all collected data and have purview over all analysis, interpretation, and presentation of the data.

2. TASKS AND DELIVERABLES

Description of Tasks: 

Provide VCL an online suicide assessment tool; 

Provide unlimited access to the online assessment tool and collected data during the contract period;

Provide ongoing technical support and assistance with the assessment tool's functionality, including sending follow-up “reminder” emails to participants, updating the Crisis Responder templates, the welcome page, and the thank-you page, and/or creating new templates that target individualized demographic responses. Allow for regular website updates/changes of resource information to include videos, and so forth. 

All technical support, updates, and participant communications must be managed and executed by human staff. The use of AI, automated agents, or machine learning systems in delivering, interpreting, or responding to participant data is strictly prohibited under this contract.

Periodically monitor the online assessment tool to ensure user access and smooth functionality, including ensuring the Reference Code automatically populates for the Crisis Responder without requiring the participant to provide it.

Monitor the integration of the assessment tool and the Veterans Chat software to accommodate ongoing updates by the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline.

Assist VCL staff in training Chat Crisis Responders in the procedures of the online assessment tool and provide ongoing technical assistance and support to Chat Crisis Responders, as needed; 

Assist VCL staff in the analysis and interpretation of the online assessment tool data, including a data report/evaluation plan that includes specific data needs and timelines.

Participate with VCL in presenting evaluation findings related to the online assessment tool at annual conferences, as needed. 

Participate in the development of manuscripts related to the online assessment tool, as agreed upon by the contractor and the VCL. 

2.2 Reporting Requirements: The contractor will submit reports to the Contracting Officer’s Representative and the Quality Assurance Officer of the VCL.

Deliverables:

Online assessment tool, as described in the section above; website with enhancements and interfaces, including timely updates/changes as agreed upon by the contractor and VA staff;

Quarterly reports to be delivered on or before the 15th of the next quarter. Annual reports to be delivered on or before the 15th of the new Option year. Reports will include quantitative data (such as: number of quizzes, breakdown of participants, number/percent of symptom severity, evaluation data, number of new users, number of returning users, number of users who engaged in a chat, and so forth).  Ad Hoc reports upon request;

Secure transfer of all submitted assessment data to VCL. Data updates are exported and securely transferred to VCL Quarterly, concurrent with reports or Ad Hoc upon request.

Quarterly conference calls with the VCL to review reporting data, report on future events for volume increases, and address any issues or updates. Face-to-face meeting(s) scheduled if agreed upon by contractor and VCL.

Lean Depot Management System (LDMS) Sustainment Support

CAUTION:

The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that have experience with the Lean Depot Management System (LDMS) and the expertise to maintain the infrastructure to support and sustain the LDMS within existing USAF legacy systems.  This requirement is specifically for the USAF Small Arms Depot that has a requirement to sustain the LDMS within their unique depot repair operations.  The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought.  Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards.  The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey.  All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes

(a) The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this solicitation or to otherwise pay for the information solicited except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 31.205-18, Independent Research and Bid and Proposal Costs.

(b) Although “proposal” and “offeror” are used in this Request for Information, your response will be treated as information only.  It shall not be used as a proposal.

(c) This Request for Information is issued for the purpose of market research in an effort to overcome barriers to competition.

Purpose

This requirement is to provide the Air Force Small Arms (AFSA) Depot and the Small Arms Program Office (SAPO) with LDMS user support, accounts, help tickets and server administration (backups, security, patches, hardware, failures, etc.).  The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government.  Some of the services and support tasks are, but not limited to:

In LDMS, assist with uploads of equipment inventory, parts/kits, customer names, vendors, tooling, Illustrated Parts Breakdowns

Contractor expertise shall be required for all LDMS Functional areas

Brief Description

The AFSA Depot performs small arms and light weight depot repairs and provides weapons sustainment in support of the SAPO.  Systems include ground-fired rifles, carbines, handguns, grenade launchers, shotguns, and machine guns.  The depot also modifies and manufactures special tools and fixtures.  Weapons Repair Technicians may perform weapons inspections and repairs on all small arms and light weapons assigned to the Air Force.  They evaluate and provide technical solutions to complex small arms problems.  In addition, they assist in evaluating new and emerging technologies to be used in the small arms arena to satisfy new requirements.  Weapons Repair Technicians also support the USAF Shooting Team, National Match, Royal Air Force Atlantic Challenge, Defender Challenge and other competitions as requested and approved.  Weapons Repair Technicians provide rapid response affecting the entire Air Force, including complete weapons systems or to satisfy an urgent and compelling war fighter need.

The AFSA Depot provides a unique capability that does not exist in base intermediate shops or DoW depot-level overhaul facilities.

The LDMS sustainment allows continued visibility and traceability of all weapons/parts to meet Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) compliance.  This also facilitates the AFSA Depot operations and keeps it aligned with maintenance information systems already in use today by other USAF depots.

As an integral part of the AF maintenance and supply data tracking, it must maintain an interface/data exchange with current legacy and future systems to include but not limited to:

D043-Master Item Identification Control System

The contractor shall actively and responsively coordinate with designated AFSA Depot and SAPO team members participating in LDMS sustainment operations.

Expertise and Skills Sought

Program Management Support

At least 5 years of experience managing software, server administration, or database projects.

System Operational Support

At least 5 years of experience supporting and managing one or more servers within the AF network infrastructure

At least 5 years of experience supporting and managing databases within the AF network infrastructure

At least 3 years of experience working with legacy supply systems such as D043 and D035K and associated integration

At least 3 years of experience working with LDMS integration

DoD approved information assurance workforce certifications for necessary IA personnel as listed in the current version of DoDM 8140.03.  At a minimum: CompTia Security+ is required for the System Administrator (SA), Database Administrator (DBA), and Information Assurance Officer (IAO)

The contractor shall possess at a minimum the following:

Extensive knowledge and experience with LDMS and related infrastructure to ensure proper interface with legacy systems

User help desk and DD Form 2875, System Authorization Access Request, validation

LDMS help desk support for troubleshooting and report functions

Note: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY to identify sources that can provide sustainment support for the LDMS.  The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government.  The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any of the items/services discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought.  All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

Responses must be received no later than close of business 26 Mar 2026.

Please send responses to ricardo.jones@us.af.mil with a copy to jennifer.primus@us.af.mil and hayley.brown.2@us.af.mil.

1.0 Purpose 
The Army Contracting Command – Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of PEO Enterprise 
and the Project Manager, Enterprise Business Systems – Convergence (PM EBS-C), 
requests information from industry regarding capabilities, interest, and approaches to 
develop, host, integrate, and sustain Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) applications that 
support Army logistics and finance communities.  The Army is committed to fostering 
innovation and collaboration with industry, including non-traditional contractors, to 
develop solutions that align with modernization goals.  Vendors who may not have a 
fully developed solution but have the capability, interest, and willingness to develop 
applications tailored to Army needs are encouraged to respond.   
Vendor input will be used to inform the acquisition approach, technical requirements, 
integration strategies, and potential enterprise adoption consistent with Army LCNC 
guidance.   
Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for market research purposes and does not 
constitute a solicitation or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses 
to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a 
binding contract. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly 
voluntary. Respondents are responsible for all costs associated with response 
preparation. Responses will not be returned to the responder. Information received in 
response to this RFI shall be safeguarded adequately from unauthorized disclosure.   
2.0 Background 
The Army is undergoing a major modernization effort to establish a Common Business 
Operating Environment (CBOE) with EBS-C converging the current Army SAP ERP 
systems (Appendix A). This modernization effort includes assessing and migrating 
operational value chain processes (Appendix B) to enable:   
1. Supply Chain Simplification   
2. Process Automation   
3. Resilient and Secure Infrastructure   

UNCLASSIFIED  
 
 
 
LCNC Application Ecosystem RFI 
 2 
February 2026  
 
 
4. Agility to Support Maneuvers   
5. Scalability to Adapt to Future Demands   
6. Auditability to Maintain Transparency, Traceability, and Accountability 
The key elements of the CBOE are captured in the EBS-C architecture diagram 
(Appendix C), which includes the:   
• Transactional Core Layer: The foundation of the system using SAP S/4HANA 
and provides stable, governed, and reliable processing of all core business 
transactions (e.g., financials, procurement, logistics, HR, and manufacturing).   
• Engagement Layer: Facilitates all user interactions.   
• Agility Layer: Enables unique business processes and business workflows to 
avoid building customization of the Transactional Core.   
• Integration Layer: Ensures reliable, real-time flow and transformation of data 
between the Transactional Core, the Agility Layer, and external systems. 
A key aspect of the EBS-C architecture is the support of an application ecosystem to 
augment EBS-C capabilities at the operational level. LCNC solutions will play a critical 
role in modernizing hundreds of defense business systems that perform routine, non-
transactional functions (analytics and decision support tools) or transactional functions 
that integrate with ERP systems. These solutions will leverage APIs to authoritative data 
sources and align with the Army CIO Low-Code/No-Code Development Guidance 
(Appendix D).  Additionally, these solutions must align with the Army Unified Data 
Reference Architecture (UDRA) to emphasize interoperability and data portability across 
systems. 
3.0 Objectives 
The Army is establishing an LCNC ecosystem to accelerate delivery of business and 
mission solutions while ensuring governance, cybersecurity, and interoperability with 
Army enterprise services and data platforms.  LCNC applications will augment EBS-C by 
providing rapid user-centric solutions for mission support tasks that are not part of the 
EBS-C core.  
The Army seeks information on vendor capabilities and approaches that address the 
following high-level objectives:   

UNCLASSIFIED  
 
 
 
LCNC Application Ecosystem RFI 
 3 
February 2026  
 
 
1. Market Capabilities: Discover industry capabilities, interest, and willingness to 
support the Army’s ecosystem of applications in the areas of finance and 
logistics. Vendors may respond based on their existing solutions or their 
capability to develop applications tailored to Army requirements. Responses 
should categorize applications as transactional or non-transactional and assess 
integration needs.   
2. Development using Approved Platforms: Identify vendors, solutions, and 
development approaches using Approved Product List (APL) systems 
(Appendix E) to ensure compatibility, security, and compliance with Army 
standards.   
3. Development using non-APL Platforms: Determine the feasibility of 
adopting new platforms and the timeline for approval if not on the APL.   
4. Partnering for Rapid Acquisition: Design strategies to maximize outreach, 
encourage innovation, expand the industrial base, streamline acquisition and 
transition successful prototypes to production.   
5. Driving Mission Advantage through Innovative Technologies: Pursue 
innovative features or tools for accelerating development of the application and 
aligned with the functional communities’ needs for the application to improve 
operational readiness and enhance decision-making.  Collaboration with 
functional communities during development is required. 
6. Security and Interoperability Standards: Provide solutions that adhere to 
Army cybersecurity, interoperability, and governance standards.   
7. Cost and Schedule: Rapidly deploy and demonstrate prototype projects and 
determine development and operation costs.

4. Partnering: Please describe your team's approach to partnering. 
5. Certifications: Please list any relevant certifications, such as FedRAMP, RMF, or

4.2 Application Type and Data Model 
Please define your solution or proposed solution for development by selecting the 
category below that best describes its primary function and its interaction with Army 
data systems. Vendors who do not have a fully developed application but have the 
capability and willingness to develop solutions tailored to Army needs should describe 
their approach and technical expertise. If your solution or proposed solution for 
development has both transactional and non-transactional components, please describe 
each. 
1. Transactional Applications.   Definition: These applications are built to 
process data and execute transactions that require a two-way, read/write 
integration with an Army ERP system of record (Appendix A). Their core purpose 
is to create, update, or modify data within those authoritative systems. Your 
Response Must Describe: 
• Your technical approach to integration and data synchronization.   
• How you ensure data integrity, manage error handling, and maintain an 
audit trail between your application / proposed application and the Army's 
ERP. 
• Which specific Army ERP systems your solution is designed to integrate with. 
2. Non-Transactional Applications.   Definition: These applications are designed 
for analytics, decision support, visualization, or reporting. They consume data 
from authoritative Army sources in a read-only capacity and do not write new or 
modified data back to the core ERP systems. Your Response Must Describe:

• How your application or proposed application aggregates data from one or 
more authoritative sources to provide actionable insights. 
• Your methodology for transforming raw data into intuitive dashboards, 
predictive analytics, or other tools that enhance decision-making for the 
finance and logistics communities.   
• The primary Army data sources your application would leverage.   
4.3 Domain Expertise/Areas of Interest and Operational Impact  
Demonstrate your company's expertise and willingness to solve challenges specific to 
the Army's finance and logistics domains. Vendors who may not have a fully developed 
solution but have the capability and interest in developing applications tailored to Army 
needs should describe their approach and technical expertise. Your response should 
provide concrete evidence of your capabilities and experience. 
1. Primary Area of Expertise:  Please select the area(s) where you have proven 
experience and provide examples of your solutions or projected solutions you 
could develop.  
• For Finance: Describe a finance application you have developed or propose 
to develop based on your expertise. Explain the specific problem it solved or 
could solve (e.g., improved budget tracking, streamlined financial reporting, 
enhanced audit readiness) and the value it provided or could provide for the 
user.   
• For Logistics: Describe a logistics application you have developed or 
propose to develop based on your expertise. Explain the specific problem it 
solved or could solve (e.g., increased inventory accuracy, improved supply 
chain visibility, enhanced readiness reporting). Show how it delivered or 
could deliver measurable value to the user.    
• Describe your ability to develop logistics applications that support Army 
requirements (e.g., inventory management, readiness indicators and others). 
Provide examples of innovative logistics applications you have developed. 
2. Bridging the Finance-Logistics Divide: A critical Army requirement is 
maintaining a seamless, auditable link between logistical actions and financial 
transactions (e.g., linking a parts request to a purchase order and its final 
payment).

The 316th Contracting Squadron at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland intends to award a 
simpliﬁed acquisition on a sole source basis to Lumena Inc. in accordance with FAR 6.302-
1 Only.one.responsible.source. 
The Government has an existing MindGym hardware solution that requires continued 
support of the proprietary Mind Gym software to continue to function, remain up-to-date, 
and support. Lumena, a woman-owned small business (WOSB), is the only source capable 
of providing this proprietary software. No other vendors or contract vehicles offer or are 
authorized to distribute this product. The requirement is commercial in nature, and no 
changes to the government's technical documentation are needed prior to solicitation. No 
competitive opportunities apply due to the lack of alternative sources. The period of 
performance requested is 17 February 2026 (Tuesday). 
A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement action 
based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The 
North American Industry Classiﬁcation System (NAICS) Code for this acquisition is 541511 
with a size standard of $34M. Information received will be considered solely for the 
purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The government 
will not be responsible for any costs incurred in preparation of any capabilities statements 
or documents prepared for this notice. 
Parties interested in this announcement shall provide detailed information of their 
capabilities and certiﬁcations to clearly meet the requirements stated above. Responses 
will be via email, to include the company's name, point of contact, address, phone number, 
UEI number, business size, and CAGE code. All responses must be received by 13 February 
2026 (Friday) by 4:30 PM EST. Responses may be emailed to the Contract Specialist, Amn 
Zwe Naing via email zwe.naing@us.af.mil. 
NOTE: If documents are sent via e-mail, the contractor will be responsible for validating 
Government receipt by contacting the Contract Specialist. No solicitation is available and 
telephone requests for information will not be taken.

Byron E. Howard

CONDITION BASED MAINTENANCE PLUS (CBM+)  
 
 INDUSTRY DAY 
 
The Automatic Test Systems (ATS) Team, Product Manager Maintenance Support Systems 
(PdM MSS), Marine Corps Systems Command (MARCORSYSCOM) will host a Virtual 
Industry Day on 8 January 2026 from 9:00 a.m. -11:00 a.m. EST via Microsoft Teams focused 
on Condition Based Maintenance Plus (CBM+).  The Industry Day will consist of an overview 
briefing from the ATS team on the requirement, the planned acquisition approach and a one-hour 
question and answer period.  
 
MARCORSYSCOM has a requirement to operationalize CBM+ as a maintenance strategy for 
ground platforms across the USMC. CBM+ is a transformational concept that changes the 
approach of equipment management, readiness reporting, maintenance, and logistics to a data 
driven Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) enabled process using data analytics 
as the foundation to influence action. The CBM+ process starts with collecting data that is 
transferred, stored, analyzed and ends with visualized data to support decision making. The goal 
of the program is to improve material readiness and reduce lifecycle cost of systems and 
components. It also aims to improve logistics requirements forecasting for more responsive 
support capability across the battlefield.  
 
MARCORSYSCOM is seeking a single contract solution to collect, transmit, store, analyze, and 
visualize data from ground platform Controller Area Network (CAN) Bus, Global Combat 
Support System-Marine-Corps (GCSS-MC), Expeditionary Fluid Analysis System (EFAS),  
operating data, and other sensors and data sources as they become available.  Other data sets are 
expected to be added as they become available. Solutions must protect Government data and 
information from unauthorized disclosure at every phase of the process. 
 
The following capabilities are cited to provide focus for this event but are not an all-
encompassing list of CBM+ requirements: 
 
Collect:  MARCORSYSCOM expects that Hardware will be needed to collect data from ground 
platforms. Hardware devices must be capable of interfacing with a military vehicle’s CANbus 
via a wired interface (9-pin or 6-pin Deutsch connectors (with or without minor modification) to 
record/log all information present, store no less than 32GB of data, record a minimum of two 
CANbusses simultaneously and provide a method of transmitting/ transferring the data off the 
platform. Hardware must be no larger than 7.5”x 6” x 3” inclusive of any mounting 
plates/hardware, be able to provide FIPS 140-2 compliant encryption, and be compatible with the 
Marine Corps Enterprise Network (MCEN) Wireless LAN (WLAN).  
 
Transmit/Transfer: Transmit methods of interest are Wireless Fidelity (WIFI), Light Fidelity 
(LIFI), Bluetooth, tactical military radios, and Iridium Short Burst Data. Hardware must operate 

in a passive mode and not emit any Radio Frequency (RF) signal when not in range of an 
approved and configured network. Wired/manual offload of data should be possible.  
 
Store: All collected data will be stored in Department of Defense Cloud environments accessible 
only through the Department of Defense Information Network (DoDIN). The expected cloud 
environments are the Microsoft Azure Cloud environment on the MCEN and the Navy’s Jupiter 
enclave in the Advana cloud environment. The Government will provide access to the identified 
cloud environments for qualified personnel in the performance of this work. 
 
Analyze: Data collected will be analyzed in the cloud environment(s) identified above using 
tools available in those environments along with source code and models created in the 
environment(s). Analyzing data includes applying AI/ML models to predict failures, parts 
requirements, and remaining useful life of platforms and components. Additionally, the ability to 
conduct trend analysis on fault, parts, oil life, and usage data is required.  
 
Act: The outputs of AI/ML models will be visualized in a dashboard decision support tool hosted 
in the Jupiter Advana environment and accessible via Common Access Card authentication from 
a DoDIN connected system.  The decision support tool must provide Marine maintainers, 
maintenance officers, staff officers, and commanders at all levels the ability to determine overall 
readiness “at a glance” and provide the predictive information required to make data driven 
operational and maintenance decisions. Additionally, a maintainer level dashboard that includes 
fault codes, operational data, and troubleshooting assistance will be made available to 
maintainers in the Microsoft Azure Cloud environment to enable immediate action.  
 
MARCORSYSCOM anticipates the following applies to any future contract action related to 
CBM+.  Solutions function as intended for an indefinite period, without additional cost to the 
customer (e.g., subscription fees). The government shall retain all rights to models, source code, 
and visualizations created in the provided cloud environment.  All data and information input 
into the solution by the customer remains the sole property of the customer.  The customer (or its 
qualified, authorized representative, subject to an appropriate non-disclosure agreement) will 
have the technical data necessary to validate and verify the solution’s output and is both legally 
and contractually permitted to do so.  The customer does not typically have authorization to 
reverse engineer the product for purposes inconsistent with the purchase contract terms, unless 
pursuant to law or regulation. 
 
To register for this virtual event, Email the attached registration form to Thomas Hale at 
thomas.hale@usmc.mil. Registrations must be received by the closing time of 5:00 p.m. EST 29 
December 2026. A Microsoft Teams invite will be distributed to industry partners who respond 
by this deadline.  
 
Please note: Check over your submission to ensure your email and telephone numbers are 
correct. You will NOT receive an invitation to attend if your email is incorrect. In the event of 

unforeseen technical issues, the virtual session may be cancelled, and a copy of the slide deck 
will be provided to the registered attendees following completion of the event. 
 
Please include: 
 
• Your name and contact information, including (to the extent applicable): organization 
name, name and title of point of contact, phone number, email address, SAM.gov 
Unique Entity identification number; and website URL.  
• The offeror’s business type (large business, small business, small disadvantaged 
business, 8(a)-certified small disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, woman-
owned small business, very small business, veteran-owned small business, service-
disabled veteran-owned small business) based upon North American Industry 
Classification System (NAICS) code 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services.  
Please refer to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 19 for additional detailed 
information on Small Business Size Standards.  The FAR is available at 
https://www.acquisition.gov/. 
 
Event Format: This will be a 2-hour event, which includes a 1-hour question and answer session.  
• MARCORSYSCOM CBM+ Presentation 
• Closing comments 
• 10-minute break 
• Industry Q&A  
 
Initial questions about this event may be submitted to Thomas Hale via email at 
thomas.hale@usmc.mil, no later than 9:00am 6 January 2026. All questions and answers 
addressed during this event will be posted to Sam.gov.

Request for Information (RFI) 

Automated Pharmacy Prescription Dispensing Kiosks – Department of Veterans Affairs 

TAC RFI Number: 36C10B26Q0129

Purpose:

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking industry feedback to inform planning, acquisition strategy, and solution design for a secure, automated, pharmacy prescription dispensing kiosk that enables Veterans to receive medications prescribed by a licensed provider through a pharmacist-verified dispensing workflow to improve timely access to medications while maintaining full regulatory compliance and patient safety. This Request for Information (RFI) seeks responses from Vendors interested in supporting an initial pilot implementation, with the potential to expand to a full-scale deployment, and demonstrating the ability to deliver a unified solution that supports ongoing operations, maintenance, and enterprise-wide adoption of the product.

This RFI is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources of supply, industry practices, and input specific to the information provided. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposals, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Any proprietary/sensitive information must be clearly marked by the vendor. 

Background:

VA pharmacies are a key resource for Veterans, family members, caregivers, and survivors, and are often required to support overall Veteran care. The VA currently delivers pharmacy services through a combination of medical center pharmacies, outpatient clinics, mail order fulfilment, and community partners (i.e. Community Care Networks).

To improve timely access to medications and enhance the Veteran experience, the VA plans to pilot and deploy automated pharmacy prescription dispensing kiosk(s) as part of a more unified and modernized pharmacy service delivery model. This effort seeks to expand secure, pharmacist-verified dispensing capabilities in strategic locations (to be determined), leveraging standardized technology workflows, and inventory management practices. The goal is to improve convenience and continuity of care through the automated system, reduce wait times and operational burden, support secure after-hours access in centralized locations including rural communities, and deliver safe, accurate, and consistent pharmacy services for Veterans. 

Performance Objectives:

Improve Veteran Access to Medications

Enable timely, convenient access to specific non-controlled, non-hazardous prescriptions that a patient may need to start right away, such as antibiotics or urgent short-term treatments, all available through a kiosk. 

Potential to support a feature that allows Veterans access to a pharmacist in real time.

Vendor must have a plan for potential positioning of their solution outdoors and potentially separate from the point of care provided (state laws do not prohibit such positioning) to enable 24/7 access by Veterans. 

Solution must have the capability to integrate (via Application Programming Interface) with VA’s Federal Electronic Health Record (Oracle Health) and existing Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) electronic health record system.

Vendor must provide 24-hour support to resolve information technology issues.

Support Verified Provider Prescriptions

Accept and process prescriptions from any licensed and authorized prescriber for all Veterans verified within VA systems.

Ensure all prescriptions undergo appropriate pharmacist review and verification prior to dispensing.

Ensure Patient Safety, Accuracy, and Authentication

Maintain a high standard of dispensing accuracy.

Provide pharmacist oversight to ensure appropriate dosage of medications are stocked within the automated system. 

Ensure proper replenishment of medications is available and completed promptly. 

Verify patient identity using secure, reliable authentication methods to ensure medications are dispensed only to authorized recipients.

Maintain Regulatory and Policy Compliance 

Comply with all applicable federal, state, and local pharmacy laws, VA policies, and cybersecurity and privacy requirements, including Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and VA information security standards.

Support Data Visibility and Reporting

Provide accurate and timely reporting on utilization, inventory, and system uptime.

Support Organizational Change Management

Assist with communication, training, and deployment planning across the VA network.

Help advertise the existence among local Veteran populations.

Requested Information:

Vendors are encouraged to provide the following:

A brief capability statement, including relevant experience. Please do not include generic marketing materials.

Footprint of the device.

Specific requirements for operation (power, connectivity, etc.).

Recommended approach to achieving full scalability VA-wide utilizing the above objectives, including:

Operational Plan detailing a unified enterprise-ready solution.

Proposed approach to adhere to varying state mandates and approach to obtain waivers, if necessary. 

Proposed approach to integrating solution with VA’s Federal Electronic Health Record (Oracle Health solution) and VistA electronic health record system.

Proposed approach for monitoring and maintenance to include software updates and mechanical repair.

Examples of automated pharmacy prescription or other medical dispensing kiosk deployment.

Proposed approach to providing remote pharmacist access.

Describe system operations and maintenance, to include:

Overall inventory capacity as well as inventory at the unit-dose and bottle level, including real time counts. 

Describe how the system manages lot numbers, expiration dates, and recalls.

Proposed approach to maintaining appropriate inventory.

Proposed approach to Veteran verification, to include:

Describe security controls to prevent unauthorized access, theft, or removal of medication without a verified prescription. 

Key risks and mitigations VA should consider

High-level cost and schedule considerations

Innovative ideas or technologies VA should explore 

Other considerations the VA should consider regarding implementation of a pilot program to full scale deployment.

Submittal Information:

This is a RFI only. It is requested that all companies interested in participating in this effort note their interest and provide an indication of their respective capabilities to perform the effort described above. Marketing material will not be accepted as an indication of capability. The vendor must display that their solution is tested and has been successfully implemented in a healthcare setting. Only responses related to the Government’s requirements as listed above will be considered. 

Provide the following information on the first page/slide of the submission:

Name of Company

Address

Point(s) of Contact

Phone Number(s)

Fax Number

Email addresses

Company Business Size and Status

NAICS code(s) – If applicable, identify your company’s Small Business size status based upon the applicable NAICS code of 541512. For more information refer to http://www.sba.gov/.

Socioeconomic data

Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number

The vendor shall submit their response no later than February 2, 2026 at 12 PM ET.  Submissions should not exceed 15 pages. Questions shall be submitted no later than January 21, 2026 5 PM ET. Responses and questions are to be sent via email to Andrea Caltabilota at Andrea.Caltabilota@va.gov, Nicole Bestreski at Nicole.Bestreski@va.gov, and Robert Kirzow at Robert.Kirzow@va.gov. Please include " Automated Pharmacy Prescription Dispensing Kiosks " in the subject line of your response. Mark your response as "Proprietary Information" if the information is considered business sensitive. 

NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.

The Government will only review what is being requested under the “Submittal Information” section of this RFI. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included that exceed this limit.

DISCLAIMER

This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.
