### Sheet: Questions
No. | Original Sorting Order | Solicitation Document | Applies to both CSOP and SOW | Document Section | Page Number | Question | Government Response | 
1 | 1 | CSOP |  | 2.0 | 6 | The RFI expresses a strong interest in exploring "alternative methods other than CBP’s existing Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) standards of electronic data transmission". What are CBP's specific expectations and preferred technical standards for secure API-driven data exchange between a new government cloud solution and the existing ACE environment? | CBP is open to exchanging messages in alternate open and non-proprietary standards but ACE is currently implementing an API capability with JSON payloads however this should not be a limitation on proposed solutions. | 
2 | 2 | CSOP |  | 8.1.2 d | 8 | Given the requirement that "ground-truthing or tuning of systems will be performed only on CBP systems and not on contractor networks unless specifically authorized", how does CBP define a "CBP system" in this context? Specifically, would a dedicated, secure environment within a government cloud instance, separate from the primary ACE production environment, be considered a "CBP system" for such data processing activities in a potential future phase? | Not applicable since for the pilot the system will not run in the government environment. A CBP system is any information system that CBP transmits, stores, or processes data or information and is (1) owned, leased, or operated by CBP, (2) operated by a contractor on behalf of CBP, or (3) operated by another Federal, state, or local Government agency on behalf of CBP. | 
3 | 3 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1
Section 1 | 9 | The RFI states that the proposed technology solution "cannot operate behind the CBP IT firewall" for the initial pilot, while also indicating development "via a test environment within ACE". Given that the existing Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) Portal already operates in a FedRAMP High Government Cloud environment hosted by its provider, how does CBP specifically define "behind the CBP IT firewall" in the context of cloud-based solutions? Does this imply a new, entirely separate government cloud environment, or is a distinct logical environment within the same government cloud provider's ecosystem (where ACE resides) considered "outside" for the initial pilot phase? | Not applicable since for the pilot the system will not run in the government environment. ACE will only be ingesting data provided by the proposed solution in a test environment. | 
4 | 4 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1
Section 1 | 9 | To fulfill the requirement that the proposed technology solution "cannot require any CBP data input to achieve the capability" for initial demonstration, what specific types or categories of non-CBP data are considered acceptable and preferred for showcasing the capabilities? For example, would the use of publicly available export data from foreign customs agencies or other types of private sector trade compliance data be sufficient and meet this criterion for the initial pilot demonstration? | This requirement refers to the fact CBP is not providing solution providers with access to the data housed within CBP systems, and therefore, any solutions should not rely on access to such data to fulfill one or more of the described capability pillar objectives. The examples provided in the question would be sufficient. | 
5 | 5 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1
Section 1 | 9 | When the RFI specifies that the development and implementation of private sector solutions will be conducted "via a test environment within ACE", does this mean a logical test environment within the existing ACE production instance, or can it encompass a separate, dedicated government cloud environment that is architecturally distinct but designed for eventual integration with ACE? | There is no requirement to host the pilot system in the ACE test environment. Information sent by the vendor will be ingested into ACE test environment. | 
6 | 6 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1
Section 2 | 9 | What are CBP's estimated operational requirements in terms of typical transaction volumes, concurrent users, data processing loads, and desired throughput for a fully operationalized solution? | CBP anticipates this will vary significantly and is unique to the solution provider. CBP does not have plans at this time to mandate trade community use of any solution(s) that may be selected for awards. As such, details around typical transaction volumes, data processing loads, and the like will be informed by the amount of data the solution providers are prepared to share with CBP. This may be based on the solution providers existing importer clientele, for example, among other factors. | 
7 | 7 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1
Section 2 | 10 | Are there any specific API management platforms or data integration patterns that CBP prefers or currently uses for non-EDI based data exchange? | No, all solutions will be considered for evaluation for this solicitation. | 
8 | 8 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 1 | 5 | AI Enabled Solutions: Tariff classification – are you interested in validating tariff classification or classifying tariffs numbers based on the description and other information? | All solutions will be considered for evaluation for this solicitation. | 
9 | 9 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 1 | 5 | AI Enabled Solutions: What sort of validations would apply to the country of origin? e.g. would this be for goods possibly substantially transformed inside another country? | CBP is seeking solutions that can address all current as well as emerging tariff requirements, including innovative and expedient methods of handling substantial transformation requirements. | 
10 | 10 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 1 | 5 | AI Enabled Solutions: What other items could fall under “etc.”? e.g. would this include validating PGA data? | All solutions will be considered for evaluation for this solicitation. | 
11 | 11 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 1 | 5 | Earlier Tariff Collection:  Do you envision this process working through service providers or directly with other international government’s postal services? | All solutions will be considered for evaluation for this solicitation. | 
12 | 12 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 1 | 5 | Supply Chain Tracing:  What are the requirements for this? In other words, how far back in the supply chain would you like to track? Back to the original manufacturer, or somewhere else in the supply chain? | Ideally from origin to end user. | 
13 | 13 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 1 | 5 | Supply Chain Tracing: Are we talking about pre-departure planning, after departure shipments bound to the USA and actors involved in them, but also higher up the chain stages such as manufacturer logistics/MRP planning or even higher up such as manufacturer CRM (Customer Relationship Management), SCM (Supplier Relationship Manager), etc.? | Any or all of these as part of a solution could be considered for evaluation for this solicitation. | 
14 | 14 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 2 | 6 | Are you envisioning an importer portal for filing entries, such as the ACE AES Direct portal, or collecting data from a third-party provider that would file directly with the ACE system? | The solicitation is not limited in either aspect and is open to consider all viable solutions. | 
15 | 15 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 2 | 6 | Would any of the elements of Pillar 1 come into play for Pillar 2 e.g. AI tariff classification, etc. | Yes, solutions that reach across Pillars are acceptable. | 
16 | 16 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 3 | 6 | Is this a system intended to work with the WCO’s “Smart Customs Community Portal”, adjacent, alternative or something different? | Something different. | 
17 | 17 | CSOP |  | 2.0
Pillar 3 | 6 | What services would such “international customs platform” provide? | An international customs platform may be built in an interoperable manner for ease of integration and allow carriers to share import and export data with customs agencies | 
18 | 18 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1 | 9 | In reference to Requirement #3, if the proposed solution uses a commercial platform already in use by the government (such as Amazon Web Services) and the vendor has cleared personnel, will the government allow testing within the CBP firewall? Use of existing commercial solutions will save the government significant funds and enhance the evaluation of the pilots if vendors are allowed to configure existing licenses within the CBP firewall. | No. | 
19 | 19 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1 | 9 | In reference to Requirements #3 and #5, will the pilots be run entirely within the technology providers environment? If so, can the government provide additional requirements/specifications for transmitting data to CBP? | The pilots will involve the technology provider transmitting data from their environment to CBP's test environment in ACE, without going behind CBP's firewall. | 
20 | 20 | CSOP |  | 2.0 | 6 | It is our understanding that pilots must run without any access to CBP data. Will the government consider providing data to solution vendors to enhance the evaluation of the pilots? | The Government will not formally transmit data to solution vendors to enhance the evaluation of the pilots. The Government may give feedback in other forms regarding the quality of the data received and other measures of success. | 
21 | 21 | CSOP |  | 3.1 | 7-8 | The Government requires a minimum font size of 12 pt. in Times New Roman. Would the Government allow the use of 8 pt. font size in tables, graphics, and figure/table captions? | The Government will allow the use of 8 pt. font size in tables, graphics, and figure/table captions. | 
22 | 22 | CSOP |  | 8.0 | 19 | Depending on the nature of the solution, the SOW compliance requirements have the potential to lack proportionality and specificity in certain areas. For example, if the solution is cloud service based, there are a number of requirements that would not be applicable.  Please confirm there will be flexibility to negotiate these requirements at a subsequent stage to ensure alignment with standard commercial cloud terms. | Yes, Section 5.7 of CSOP Solicitation states " Based on the Phase 1 and 2 evaluations, the government may enter directly into negotiations with each submitter to make a resultant award. | 
23 | 23 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1 | 9 | The CSOP states that "the technology solution cannot operate behind the CBP IT firewall and cannot require any CBP data input to achieve the capability." Is this requirement limited to the demo/orals, or will it apply to the pilot and the final implementation? | At the conclusion of this procurement process, CBP may select several candidates to proceed with as part of an ongoing pilot via a test environment within CBP’s Automated Commercial Environment (ACE).
The intended awarded pilot may ultimately inform minimum security criteria and certifications for vendors to transmit data to CBP systems beyond the pilot phase. | 
24 | 24 | CSOP |  | 5.5
C.1 | 16 | The CSOP references two models for the Phase II evaluation process: "Award of a contract can only be made to a submitter: 1) Whose proposal is technically acceptable or represents the best value;"  Please confirm the Government will use the "Best Value" and not "Technically Acceptable" evaluation model during Phase II. | Awards will be made to a submitter whose proposal is technically acceptable or represents the best value. However, in terms of best value,  proposals will not  be compared with each other to determine best value, as each submitter will be evaluated on their own individual merit. Trade-off evaluation procedures will not be utilizes since each solution swill be evluated on its own merit. | 
25 | 25 | CSOP |  | 3.2.1 | 9 | Does the government have a definition for “CBP data” as defined in the CSOP, Section 3.2.1? | "CBP data" in this context refers to data housed within CBP's systems, such as trade data CBP receives from importers via ACE. The intent of this compliance question is to ensure the solution provider understands there will be no access to such information protected behind the CBP firewall. | 
26 | 26 | CSOP |  | 8.5 | 20 | Please confirm that Section 8.5 of the CSOP, "Title," is not applicable to commercial services provided as part of the solution which will be government by commercial IP terms. | The full language in question reads as follows, "Unless specified elsewhere in this contract, title to items furnished under this contract shall pass to the Government upon acceptance, regardless of when or where the Government takes physical possession." This is standard language used in CSOP Solicitations. For this particular solicitation, it is not CBP's intent to suggest CBP would take title of commercial services. | 
27 | 27 | CSOP |  | 2.0 | 7 | Section 2.0 of the CSOP seeks solutions that address "earlier tariff collection and payment to the U.S. Government, especially in the international mail environment." Does the international mail environment include both postal and commercial carriers (i.e., express carriers)? | Yes, in this context. | 
28 | 28 | CSOP |  | 2.0 | 6 | Regarding the risk management requirements in CSOP Section 2.0, does the government have data management principles you would be willing to share in order for vendors to provide robust AI driven risk management and supply chain tracing solutions? Or would this be shared during the pilot? | We would like to better understand what AI driven risk management and supply tracing solution your company is capable of delivering. | 
29 | 29 | CSOP |  | 2.0 | 5-6 | Regarding Pillars 1 and 2 requirements in CSOP Section 2,0, what are the scaling requirements (Avg. and Peak) on number of clearances and number of products within each clearance? | Scaling abilities will depend on the particular solution offered for consideration. | 
30 | 30 | SOW |  | 8.1.1 | 7 | A number of the CSOP solicitation and SOW compliance requirements reference government policies and standards that offerors appear to be unable to access. For example, it appears DHS’s Artificial Intelligence System Security Guide (March 2025 - version 3.0) is unavailable online. Please confirm that offerors will be provided with access to all referenced documents and provided a future opportunity to submit questions. | A copy of DHS’s Artificial Intelligence System Security Guide may be provided to submitters that advance to Phase II. | 
31 | 31 | SOW |  | 8.1.4 | 9 | Section 8.1.4(a) references FIPS 140-2 validation. Given that FIPS 140-3 replaced FIPS 140-2 as the current federal standard and represents enhanced security requirements aligned with modern threats, will CBP accept cryptographic modules that have been validated under FIPS 140-3 | Yes |

INTRODUCTION 
This SOURCES SOUGHT is a market research tool to determine the availability and technical capability of 
small businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, HUBZone Firms, 
Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses and Woman Owned Small Business) to 
provide the required products and/or services. 
DISCLAIMER 
THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR 
PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A 
COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE 
GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS 
ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS 
ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION 
IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 
 
PROGRAM BACKGROUND 
 
The contractor shall install inside and outside plate telecommunications and Local Area Network 
(LAN) infrastructure requirements throughout Tinker AFB and designated Geographically Separated 
Units (GSUs). The contractor shall support base mission changes, major or minor Base Infrastructure 
and Telecommunications Support (BITS) infrastructure modifications, and other support requirements 
necessary to meet mission requirements. Support requirements may originate from technology changes, 
hardware and software systems upgrade, reconfigurations, new or additional equipment, dial central 
office reconfigurations to include routing and diversity requirements, and any other environmental 
changes that impacts or alters the BITS requirements. The contractor shall advise technical personnel of 
upcoming trends for voice, data, LAN, and video solutions and make recommendations for migration to 
these solutions. The push for convergence of voice, data, LAN, and video shall be considered when 
recommending new solutions. All efforts shall be directed towards a Unified Convergence Network by 
identifying deficiencies and shortcomings of the current communication network when evaluated 
against an adopted IPv6 and VoIP standard IAW the Draft PWS. 
 
This is a bridge contract for the installation and production requirements of BITS. The new contract will 
be an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Firm Fixed price task orders. This bridge  
contract is anticipated to be conducted as a commercial services purchase IAW FAR Part 12 as an IDIQ 
with a 12 month ordering period and a minimum guaranteed award of $400,000, this work is anticipated 
to be transferred in Summer 2025 to an upcoming Enterprise contract.  
Place of Performance: Tinker AFB, Oklahoma. However, the Contractor may be required to travel to 
various equipment installation sites to meet US Air Force requirements. 
 

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES 
The Contractor shall provide technical engineering products and support services in support of the 
United States Air Force Base Infrastructure Telecommunications Support and systems at Tinker AFB, 
Oklahoma. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached for review. 
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification shall apply to this requirement and the 
prime contractor shall have or demonstrate ability to obtain a "Secret" Facility Clearance and "Secret" 
safeguarding of classified information under this contract. 
The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking that would be accomplished by labor categories 
that are subject to the Service Contract Act. 
This contract requires a transition period IAW the Draft PWS. The contractor shall reference the Draft 
PWS for the requirements of Government Furnished Property as well as Contractor Furnished 
Equipment necessary to perform the contract.  
ELIGIBILITY 
The applicable NAICS Code for this requirement is 541519, Engineering Services with a Small Business 
Size standard of $34 Million. The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this effort is DF10 - IT and Telecom – 
Business Application/Application Development Software as a Service. This Sources Sought Synopsis is 
requesting responses to the following criteria ONLY from businesses that can provide the required 
services under the NAICS Code. 
SUBMISSION DETAILS 
Interested businesses are requested to submit a capabilities statement of no more than six (6) pages in 
length in Times New Roman font of not less than 12 pitch. 
Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package that shall address, at a 
minimum, the following items: 
1.) What type of work has your company performed in the past in support of the same or similar 
requirement? This should include the contract number, organization supported, indication of whether as 
a prime or subcontractor, contract value, Government point of contact, and a brief description of how 
the referenced contract relates to the services described in the draft PWS. 
2.) Can or has your company managed a task of this nature? If so, please provide details. 
3.) What specific technical skills does your company possess which ensure capability to perform the 
tasks outlined in the draft PWS? 
5.) Please note that under a Small-Business Set-Aside, in accordance with FAR 52.219-14, the small 
business prime must perform at least 50% of the work themselves in terms of the cost of performance. 
Provide an explanation of your company's ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this 
PWS for the base period. 

6.) Provide a statement including current small status and company profile to include number of 
employees, annual revenue history, office locations, DUNS number, CAGE code, etc. Also indicate 
whether they qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Women-Owned, HUBZone, or Service-Disabled 
Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern. 
7.) Any Contract vehicles that would be available to the Government for the procurement of the product 
and service, to include GSA Federal Supply Schedules (FSS), or any other Government Agency contract 
vehicle. (This information is for market research only and does not preclude your company from 
responding to this notice.) 
In order to make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small 
businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications and ability to perform in 
accordance with the Limitations on Subcontracting clause (FAR 52.219-14). 
To assist the Government in making a determination regarding the level of participation by small 
business in any subsequent procurement that may result from this Sources Sought, you are also 
encouraged to provide information regarding your plans to use joint venturing (JV) or partnering to 
meet each of the requirements areas contained herein. This includes responses from qualified and 
capable Small Businesses, Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Service Disabled-Veteran Owned Small 
Businesses, Women-owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses, and 8(a) companies. You 
should provide information on how you would envision your company's areas of expertise and those of 
any proposed JV/partner would be combined to meet the specific requirements contained in this 
announcement. 
 
Your responses to this Sources Sought shall be electronically submitted to Rebbecca Drydol-Brandon and 
De’Vonn Lyons in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF) via e-mail with the subject 
line BITS Sources Sought 24 TAFB to rebbecca.drydol-brandon@us.af.mil and devonn.lyons@us.af.mil. 
 
The deadline for response to this request is 6 June 2024, 2 pm (1400) Central Time. 
 
Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials. All 
information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Please be advised that all 
submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 
 
No phone calls will be accepted. 
 
Questions may be submitted via email to rebbecca.drydol-brandon@us.af.mil or 
devonn.lyons@us.af.mil. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information 
provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to these 
Sources Sought.

Statement of Work 
Research, Development, Test & Evaluation Project Management Database 
1.0 OBJECTIVE 
The Research, Development, Test & Evaluation (NA-11) organization must establish a program 
management information (PMIS) system. This system will address NA-11’s requirement to have a 
system, or tool, that will enable efficient program management by integrating all program management 
activities within the RDT&E portfolio through the tracking the progress of defined project scope, work 
packages, and/or priorities within each organizational unit as well as integrating budget requirements 
across organizations, when necessary. 
2.0 BACKGROUND 
The Research, Development, Test & Evaluation (RDT&E) portfolio provides the scientific foundation; 
the capabilities, tools and components to enable design assessment, qualification, certification, and 
technology maturation; and balances the most pressing investments needed to meet Department of 
Defense (DoD) warhead requirements and schedules, along with the critical long-term research and 
development needed for a robust and responsive future stockpile.  
RDT&E is comprised of the following five subprograms: 
1. Assessment Science 
2. Engineering and Integrated Assessments 
3. Inertial Confinement Fusion 
4. Advanced Simulation and Computing 
5. Weapon Technology and Manufacturing Maturation 
The RDT&E organization currently lacks the ability to integrate program management activities with the 
Planning, Programming, Budget, and Evaluation (PPBE) process throughout the life cycle of a project. 
Additionally, it lacks an integrated system to track the progress of defined scope, work packages, and/or 
projects within each subprogram (listed above) and, where necessary, integrate budget requirements 
across the subprograms. 
The PMIS system will be NA-11’s primary resource for program management. Over the course of the 
PPBE, it will serve several purposes. In the planning and program phase, the tool will be used to collect 
requirements from the management & operating labs, plants, and sites (M&Os) with sufficient 
information for the federal program manager (FPM) and office leadership to make programmatic and 
budgetary decisions in developing the program’s 5-year Future Years Nuclear Security Plan (FYNSP). 
Information from the Project Plans (PPs) will be captured in the PMIS and will facilitate accounting for 
mortgages for projects over their life cycle. Once projects are funded by the program office, the tool will 
be used to track execution, develop roadmaps and communicate accomplishments with end users and 
stakeholders. 
3.0  PROJECT SCOPE 
The ultimate scope of the project is to design a PMIS system that will allow the NA-11 Principal Assistant 
Deputy Administrator (PADA) and Deputy PADA to easily track the progress of the NA-11 program. It 
will also allow the PADA to respond to external stakeholder inquiries from Congress and the White 
House’s Office of Management and Budget. The development of a Program Management Plan (PMP) will 
happen concurrently to acquisition and implementation of the PMIS, therefore the initial instantiation may 

not be what is finally deployed. The following goals and objectives capture the current understanding of 
what is needed: 
• Goal 1 – Standardize program management. 
 Provide a user-friendly program management system for all members of the NA-
11 community. 
 Have easy access to information requested from external stakeholders. 
 Automate routine tasks. 
• Goal 2 – Streamline decision making. 
 Provide transparency in scope, cost, and schedule to NA-11 Leadership. 
 Allow FPMs to easily coordinate cross-office scope. 
 Utilize modern analytical capabilities for ease of decision making. 
o Provide a change control process for approval of fund transfers during execution. 
• Goal 3 – Communicate effectively. 
 Create standardized reports and presentations for internal and external 
stakeholders 
 Capture consistent information across subprograms. 
• Goal 4 – Scalability. 
 Allow for other Defense Programs organizations to adopt it in time, should they 
so choose, through flexibility in construction of the application. 
 Utilize the information from the variety of existing tools at HQ and the M&Os 
and have a useable system quickly 
NA-11 would like to implement a solution that can be used for the long term. The need is for something 
that can implemented immediately but can be updated based on user needs and lessons learned from 
previous instantiations. As the research and development organization of Defense Programs, being at the 
forefront of using artificial intelligence for efficiency in program management is an important part of this 
project. 
4.0 REQUIREMENTS 
General System Requirements 
A.  Security, Access, and Authorization 
• Instance on both the low and high side that are reconciled at a regular interval. 
• System developers will require appropriate clearances to support classified implementation. 
• Access controls – need to know as well as classification. 
o Appropriate interfaces and access restrictions for: 
 PADA/DPADA 
 ADAs 
 Office Directors (ODs) 
 FPMs 
 Budget Team 
 Support Service Contractors  
 Labs, Plants, and Sites 
 Offices – may have slightly different data/template/report needs. Should strive to 
minimize differences as much as possible.  
• NA-113 

• NA-114 
• NA-115 
o Appropriate access levels for: 
 Classified: up to Secret Restricted Data (SRD) 
 Controlled unclassified information (CUI) 
B.  Version Control 
• Have a schedule for updating project information to maintain version control and fidelity of 
information (Monthly, Quarterly or PPBE cycle). 
• Central location for files, documents, user-guides, Standard Operating Procedures, etc. currently 
housed on DP Biz Ops and/or Shared Drive. 
o To be a “dashboard” and not as a duplication of existing methodologies. 
• Central repository for data calls. 
o Warehouse to collect/store/reference prior year deliverables/Data Calls. 
o Current and prior years. 
o Pull in Crosscuts from FormEx. 
• Allows collaboration on working documents while maintaining version control. 
C.  End User Operating Environment 
• Flexible search capability. 
• Main project form user interface for data entry and project review (see example in Figure 1). 
• Ability to add, remove and modify data fields as needed. 
o Each field should have “other”, “Not Applicable,” and flexibility to update selections. 
o Some fields may be dependent on other fields.  
• Ability for large data download and uploads in XLS or CSV file types. 
• Ability to attach files to individual project entries (text, images, movies...etc.). 
• Unclassified and classified instances should look the same. The only difference should be that 
detailed classified information can be included on the classified instance. 

Figure 1 – Main Project Form  
 
D.  Implementation 
• The system will be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days per year (24/7/365). 
Downtimes for maintenance will be scheduled and announced to users in advance. Servers will be 
monitored 24/7/365. 
• Real-time linkage (communication) with existing systems to limit or avoid duplication of input. 
o Regular cadence of updating with other systems (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, 
or annual document linkages as appropriate). 
o Should interface with milestone reporting tool (MRT) and other high visibility tools such 
as System to Track and Report Spending (STARS), FormEx/CostEx, G2 for 
infrastructure, SIR, etc. for consistency and to remove redundancy for users.   
• Allows cross referencing to catch possible errors in reporting data. 
• Facilitate tracking of requirements currently done in MS Teams Pages. 
• Utilizes existing instances of the software at HQ and all M&Os as much as possible. 
• Implements artificial intelligence (AI) solutions to utilize all available data to inform funding and 
programming decisions.  
• Employ workflows that are scaleable to the part of the organization using them. 
• Creates automated alerts for specified items to which various users should be alerted (e.g., an 
M&O is 5 days late in updating monthly execution data, so the FPM receives an alert, or a project 
plan is submitted that has duplicative scope to an existing project in another office, both FPMs 
should be notified.) 
• NNSA owns the data within the system. 
• Minimize burden of initial data entry as much as possible. 
• Provide and maintain user training and support. 


Application Requirements 
A.  Budget  
• Should handle both FYNSP planning and a single FY budget execution.  
• Tracking budget with flexibility for scope that is level of effort or in the way of maintenance and 
operation and user support.  
• Able to handle committed funding level and anticipated scenarios (for instance, IF a specific item 
is demonstrated, THEN we do X, OTHERWISE we do Y).  
o This will enable a more realistic planning for the program multiple years out.  
B.  Schedule  
• Able to support FYNSP planning with a five-year FY horizon if not FYNSP+2 for the higher-
level DP coordinated work, and link milestones across subprograms, other programs in NA-11, 
and DP writ large—label designations would be OK but should be unique enough for data calls 
and searches.  
• Should be deliverable based, include interim and final deliverables rather than quarterly updates.  
C.  Project/Scope Descriptions  
• Captures what constitutes a project or scope/work package. 
• Allows for storage of discrete tasks within a program, even if a particular task isn’t funded for a 
particular execution year. 
D.  Project/Scope Progress   
• Will need to track progress based on HQ-defined metrics. 
• Metrics will vary by program/office. 
E.  Priority Tasks/Items which Need Attention  
• The ability to order a (by priority, deadline, time etc.) list of activities which need attention, are 
late for review, coming up for review etc.?  
• Can this automatically email a summary at some cadence that a user can select?  
• Dashboard and reports that tie programmatic scope and strategic priorities to funding and 
schedule (see example in Figure 2). 

Figure 2 – Projects Roadmap  
 
 
Data Requirements 
A.  Planning & Programming Phase Data Requirements  
In the planning phase, M&Os will communicate their proposed requirements to meet the mission as stated 
in the strategic plan and planning guidance. This will include requests for unfunded requirements (UFRs) 
that will be considered in programming. Below is the list of data that will be collected in the planning 
phase and used throughout the life cycle of a project.   
• Program Management  
o NNSA Work Breakdown Structure (NWBS) down to Level 8 or 9 (one level below 
B&R)  
o Project ID# and Title  
o Site(s) (Identify lead site if multi-site project)  
o Needs or opportunity  
o Proposed solution and project scope  
o Benefits to nuclear security enterprise (NSE)  
o End use or Transition Organization (Next funding Source)  
o Target Program of Record  
o External dependencies (NA-90, NA-12, NA-19...etc.)  
o Project dependencies (e.g. Technology dependent on demonstrator for technology 
readiness level (TRL) advancement or Mod/Sim capability dependent on experiment for 
Verification and Validation (V&V))  
o Partnerships and collaborations  
o Project risks and potential obstacles   
o Project linkages  
o Laboratory Directed Research and Development (LDRD), Site Directed Research and 
Development (SDRD), or Plant Directed Research and Development (PDRD) (check 
box)  
o M&O Priority (1 – 5 at intervals 20% of budget)   


o FPM Priority  
• Strategic Alignment  
o Weapons Activities (WA) Integration Areas  
o WA Process Improvement  
o NA-11 Priorities   
o NA-115 Strategic Plan Goals & Ends  
o Integrated Priorities Roadmap 
o Requirements Drivers  
• Roadmaps and Progression Metrics  
o Project proposal date  
o Project start date  
o Target transition date  
 Type of project (Progression metrics)  
 TRL/Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL)  
 Line-Item construction (Critical Decision)  
 Facility and Capability Sustainment (Level of effort)  
 Modeling and Simulation (Level of effort)  
 Experiments and data collection (Execution date)  
• Financial Data  
o Note: Financial data to be collected and reported by site  
o +1 outyear programmed funding  
o +2 outyear 5-Year FYNSP  
o Beyond FYNSP total project cost (Line-Item and Minor Construction)  
 
B.  Execution & Evaluation Phase Requirements  
The PMIS system shall continue to track data from Planning and Programming phases, as well as 
execution metrics listed below. The database will be the official record of funded activities and would 
replace some organizations’ Implementation Plans (IP) Appendix Project Lists.  
• Data fields to collect in the Execution and Evaluation phase:  
o Technology Transfer Agreement (TTA), Technology Realization Team (TRT), Interface 
Requirements Agreement (IRA) and other agreements  
o Execution year scope with deliverables and milestones  
o Level 2 Milestones Status  
o Current progression metric (TRL/MRL, Critical Decision (CD), execution date)  
o Threats to cost, schedule, or scope  
o Mitigation strategy to threats to cost, schedule, or scope  
o Noteworthy accomplishments or information   
o Financial Data  
 Allocated site splits included in IP for Work Authorization  
 Carry-in and carry-out numbers 
5.0 REPORTING 
The vendor will provide monthly status updates to the COR. Technical updates with the customer will be 
negotiated on an as-needed basis. 

6.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 
The development team will need adequate personnel with DOE Q clearances to develop the classified 
instance of the deployed system. 
7.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
Standard five-year base with five one-year renewal options.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)

PROGRAM EXECUTIVE OFFICE

ENTERPRISE INFORMATION SYSTEMS (PEO EIS)

PROJECT MANAGER

ARMY DATA AND ANALYTICS PLATFORMS (PM ARDAP)

FORT BELVOIR VA 22060-5526

THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. PEO EIS is performing market surveillance for Army Data Platform 2.0 (ADP 2.0), to include acquisition strategies. No solicitation exists. This is not a request for a quote, request for proposal, request for a prototype solution, or an invitation to bid. This is not to be construed as a commitment by the US Government to form a binding contract or agreement. The Government will not reimburse or pay for information submitted in response to this RFI. RFI participation constitutes acknowledgement there is no basis for any future claims against the U.S. Government in relation to said participation. 

Any responses received do not commit the Government to contract for any future services. The Government is not currently seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. 

SECTION 1: ADP 2.0 DESCRIPTION

The Project Manager Army Data and Analytics Platforms (PM ARDAP) manages a portfolio of systems that will modernize Army business processes and enable scalable, agile, and trusted data platforms integrated with data services/applications, visualization, and analytic tools to facilitate fact-based and resource-informed decision-making. Product Manager Army Data Platform (PM ADP), within PM ARDAP provides unified data analytics capabilities that support federated communities while operating as part of a broader coalition of tools that enable Army enterprise analytics. 

ADP 2.0 will be a multi-award task order indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract (MATOC) providing enterprise data platforms from multiple data platform vendors. These platforms will enable self-service data domains and data product owners to create, manage, use and publish data products. ADP 2.0 will provide capability to federated communities across the Army enterprise with the scalability and speed that current Army capabilities cannot provide. The goals for ADP 2.0 include: 

Maximizing the use of both innovative, emerging technologies and existing Army enterprise tools throughout the program’s lifecycle.

Establishing self-service data product management across all platforms. 

Integrating agile Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (CI/CD) methodology to rapidly deploy software throughout the program’s lifecycle.

Maintaining continuous competition through a multi-award task order contract to ensure innovation, promote program affordability, and eliminate vendor lock.

Continually researching and refreshing product offerings through continuous testing and acquisition of emerging technologies.

​

SECTION 2: CONTEMPLATED ADP 2.0 ACQUISITION APPROACH

ADP 2.0 is under the DoDI 5000.87 Software Acquisition Pathway using the Defense Business Systems sub-pathway. ADP 2.0 will include a MATOC award that includes multiple data platform vendors to test, deploy and support enterprise-level capabilities for the Army. 

Award a Multi Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for up to five vendors.

Align ADP 2.0 with the 5000.87 Software Acquisition Pathway and 10 USC § 2222 requirements. 

The notable advantage of this award is to grant the freedom and flexibility to employ the best platforms and tools based on the Army’s mission needs. 

Promote and foster a competitive ecosystem for ADP 2.0 to drive affordability and adaptability. 

Continually conduct industry / innovation research for improved emerging technologies. 

Enable opportunities for on and off-ramping vendors by providing viable alternatives to existing platforms.

Provide guidance and oversight on DoD & Army Cybersecurity requirements to enable vendor(s) Assessment and Authorization.

Streamlined Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT) for Task Orders that will improve customer experience.

Leverage use of existing contract vehicles where possible. 

Fully transition from Army Vantage by FY2027.

SECTION 3: ADP 2.0 CONCEPT

ADP 2.0 is the follow-on capability to the current Under Secretary of the Army directed Army Vantage program and provides an Enterprise level data platform capability. It directly supports five of the six components of the Business Enterprise Architecture Data to Decision business process, and it is anticipated to be the platform component of the Army’s initial transition towards a “Data Mesh” implementation. It is a core component of the Army’s efforts to become a Data-centric force and supports the implementation of the Army Digital Transformation Strategy goal of using data as a strategic asset. The other components of the Data Mesh would include the Army Data Catalog (ADC), an Application Programming Interface (API) Layer, and Identity Management.

ADP 2.0, as the self-service data product management platform, provides compute and store for data products too complicated for an API layer to generate and is the engine for developing and refining data products to meet mission requirements.  Data platforms traditionally provide the following layers (see Figure 1):

Connection Layer – capable of ingesting, storing, cleansing, analyzing, categorizing, and extracting massive amounts of unstructured and highly structured data through numerous protocols which would include Open Database Connectivity (ODBC), Java Database Connectivity (JDBC), Tabular Data Stream (TDS), APIs, streams, and other native formats. 

Transformation Layer – provides data integration services that support extraction, transformation, and enrichment to create Data Products for use by internal and external Data Visualization capabilities.

Data Product Layer – Contains curated data products ready for subscription and consumption. Also capable of making Data Products available to external consumers via standardized APIs.

Data Visualization – Provides tools for analytics, workflow, dashboards, artificial intelligence, and machine learning (AI/ML) to self-service data scientists, citizen analysts, and their chain-of-command. These capabilities can be a component of a vendor's platform, or they can be an open architecture business intelligence plug-in tool that is interoperable with platforms. 

Each integrated platform must be interoperable with a variety of analytic tools, and they must also be capable of exchanging data with other platforms using open API architecture.

Figure 1: ADP 2.0 Concept

SECTION 5: RESPONSE FORMAT AND DELIVERY

Responses must be received prior to noon 16 Oct 2024 via SAM.gov and CHESS.

Participation (or non-participation) in response to this RFI will not preclude any vendor from responding to future acquisitions, either individually or as part of a team. Marketing brochures will not be considered adequate information in response to this RFI.

Interested capable vendors are invited to respond to questions presented below. Responses should be submitted electronically as one complete document. In responses, use of any proprietary information should be minimized and clearly identified as such.

Army Data Platform 2.0 Terms and Definitions

TERM | DEFINITION

Analytic Tools | A capability that provides data visualizations and reports.  Analytic tools can be integrated within a platform, or they can be a plug in approved by the Army.

Application Programming Interface (API) | A set of routines, protocols, and tools for building software applications. 

Army Data Catalog  | The Army Data Catalog is one of four components of the Data Mesh.  It provides data definitions, data discover, and data management functions to automate data governance.

Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) | Access control based on attributes associated with and about subjects, objects, targets, initiators, resources, or the environment.  An access control rule set defines the combination of attributes under which an access may take place. 

Authority to Operate (ATO) | Authorization granted by an Authorizing Official for an information system to process information based on results of a security evaluation of the system.  

Authorizing Official (AO) | Senior official or executive with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the nation.

Data API services |  Data as a service enabled through API design capabilities to - Create and manage outbound API endpoints over existing data assets. - Handle inbound API consumption to ingest internal and external data. 

Data Domain |  An organization having specific functional expertise to produce data products that can be shared and consumed by other data domains based on 58 mission need. Data Domain Owners govern what data is presented and who is allowed to use it.  

Data governance support |  Capabilities that assist data governance mandates (e.g., data quality, data lineage, policy enforcement, masking, and annotation) while handling data for meeting specific use cases (e.g., master data management and operational data sharing). 

Data governance support | Capabilities that assist data governance mandates (e.g., data quality, data lineage, policy enforcement, masking and annotation) while handling data for meeting specific use cases (e.g., master data management and operational data sharing).

Data Product |  A pre-packaged curated set of data to satisfy the Army’s mission need. Data products are designed to be high quality, easy to use, self- describing and easy to share.

IaaS | Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is a type of cloud computing service that offers essential compute, storage, and networking resources on demand, on a pay-as-you-go basis. IaaS lets you bypass the cost and complexity of buying and managing physical servers and datacenter infrastructure.
